There is no second package, so there is no re-presenting wrapper to keep.

Six methods, and they do not share a standardization status (verified 2026-08-27 against execution-apis at tag and at main):
- In tagged v1.0.0-beta.7 and the vendored spec: eth_syncing (src/eth/client.yaml), eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash and ...ByNumber (src/eth/block.yaml).
- On main only, in no tag: net_listening and net_peerCount (commit 7c58b32, #843, after beta.7).
- Never in execution-apis at all: web3_clientVersion, which is defined only by EIP-1474.

All six go into Cartouche.RPC. The untagged three get a @doc naming what defines them and what a refusing endpoint returns. Their capability answer comes from task 2137's shared refusal classification rather than a new per-method probe. Wrapping net_listening and net_peerCount with their status written down stops a later re-vendor from main silently reclassifying them as standard, which is the same trap eth_baseFee fell into.

Existing copies in Onchain.RPC (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex): syncing :446, eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash :601, ...ByNumber :636. eth_syncing's false-or-object union is the only decode of substance.

(2026-09-29 review) net_version is not missing. It is in the tagged spec since v1.0.0-beta.5 (src/eth/client.yaml) and Cartouche.RPC already wraps it. The vendored spec is also mislabelled. packages/onchain/priv/specs/openrpc-v1.0.0-beta.4.json carries x_pinnedSource ethereum/execution-apis@1ad4d255, which is the v1.0.0-beta.5 tag commit, not beta.4. Onchain.RPC.Specs reads it by that name (lib/onchain/rpc/specs.ex:6). Re-vendor from the v1.0.0-beta.7 tag, never from main, so the untagged net_* and eth_baseFee methods cannot slip in as standard.

task.title: eth_simulateV1 on Cartouche.RPC — the portable simulation entry point, keeping per-call failure, request rejection and unsupported distinct
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.RPC gains eth_simulateV1 modelling blockStateCalls with state and block overrides, and decoding per-call results including logs and per-call error objects into structs
The request surface covers the spec'd shape — blockStateCalls, stateOverrides, blockOverrides, returnFullTransactions, traceTransfers, validation — as structs per repo conventions

A live test pins one real multi-call simulation success (e.g. a funded transfer via a state override) and one real per-call failure (a reverting call inside a successful response, asserting status 0x0 and the per-call error code) and one real request rejection (a -380xx JSON-RPC error, e.g. nonce too low under validation: true), each exactly as the node reports it

Succeeded, per-call failure (CallResultFailure), request rejection (-38010..-38015 and the other codes execute.yaml lists) and method-unsupported stay distinguishable in the return type; unsupported comes from task 2137's shared refusal classification (-32601), not a new classifier
@doc names eth_simulateV1 as carried by the tagged spec since v1.0.0-beta.5 and contrasts it with the privileged trace_callMany / debug_traceCall path (task 2135)
Behaviour is verified on >=1 hosted endpoint via the task-2136 seam as well as the archive node — a real result or its real refusal, never a skip
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: A convenience simulation DSL or bundle-builder on top of the raw surface — the raw spec'd surface is the deliverable
Deprecating or changing trace_call / trace_call_many / debug_trace_call — task 2135 owns their portability contract; they stay
Refactoring onchain_tempo's AA-specific simulate/3 — it is a domain caller, not a duplicate wrapper; see the body
task.body:
`eth_simulateV1` entered the execution-apis spec at tag `v1.0.0-beta.5` (2026-06-03, `src/eth/execute.yaml`) — verified by walking the tags directly, beta.1 through beta.7 — and it IS present in the vendored local spec. It is squarely cartouche's under the stack boundary, and it is the portable answer to the privileged `trace_callMany` / `debug_traceCall` pair cartouche already wraps.

Client support is real and was verified against each client's own source, not from memory: geth (`internal/ethapi/api.go`, `BlockChainAPI.SimulateV1`), reth (`crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/core.rs`, with the tracking issue closed as implemented), erigon (`rpc/jsonrpc/eth_simulation.go`, and its rpcdaemon README lists it supported) and nethermind (`EthRpcModule.cs`). So the premise the earlier version of this task flagged as unverified is now confirmed for the archive node's client — but confirm the node's live answer anyway before building on it, because a client implementing a method and an endpoint serving it are different facts.

**One existing caller, and it is NOT a duplicate to delete.** onchain_tempo calls `eth_simulateV1` at lib/onchain/tempo/rpc.ex:128, but it is a domain consumer, not a competing wrapper: it builds a single AA-folded 0x76 call, interprets the result as success / revert / unsupported for a fee-payer gas-drain guard, and carries an empirically-verified note that `tempo_simulateV1` is not deployed on Tempo mainnet or Moderato. That is exactly the layering the boundary prescribes — the chain-specific package re-presents the node method for its domain. It stays.

What it does reveal is a second transport escape: it builds its own `do_rpc_request/4` directly on Req + Jason rather than going through the shared transport, mirroring why `Onchain.HTTP` exists. Worth noting, out of scope here.

(2026-09-29 review) Failures arrive at two different layers, and the decode must keep them apart (execution-apis v1.0.0-beta.7 src/eth/execute.yaml `errors:` and src/schemas/execute.yaml `CallResultFailure`:172):
- Per-call failure. A revert or EVM error inside one call is not a JSON-RPC error. The request succeeds, and that call's result carries `status: "0x0"`, `returnData`, `gasUsed` and an `error {code, message, data}` object.
- Request rejection. `-38010`..`-38015` (nonce too low or too high, baseFeePerGas too low, intrinsic gas, insufficient funds, …) and the other codes execute.yaml lists are a JSON-RPC error on the whole request, typically under `validation: true`. onchain_tempo's `-38013` handling is this layer, not a per-call failure.
- Method unsupported (`-32601`). This comes from task 2137's shared refusal classification, which is also where onchain_tempo's `-32601` -> `:unsupported` shape should come from.
Success plus these three outcomes must stay distinguishable in the return type. Collapsing any two of them is what makes a fail-open caller unsafe.

Authority: the tagged execution-apis spec plus the live node.

task.title: EIP-712 conformance: encode_type non-termination, bytesN padding direction, array-of-struct support, int types
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Typed.encode_type/2 terminates for a type referencing two or more DISTINCT struct types, and a test asserts termination with a bounded Task.yield rather than hanging the suite; today `%{"Root" => fields [{"z","Zebra"},{"a","Apple"}]}` never returns

Referenced struct types are appended sorted by name, per EIP-712 'the set of referenced struct types is collected, sorted by name and appended'; a test pins a type whose field order and alphabetical order differ and asserts the exact encodeType string

bytesN values are zero-padded AT THE END per EIP-712; `encode_data_value(<<0xCC>>, {:bytes, 32})` returns <<0xCC, 0::248>>. The doctest at typed.ex:279-280 currently asserts the opposite and must be corrected, not deleted
Address and uint stay LEFT-padded (address is uint160, big-endian) — a test pins both alignments side by side so the two opposite semantics can never be re-conflated into one pad/2 call

Struct types referenced through an array field are collected into encodeType (today `Root(Person[] people)` omits `Person(string name)` silently), and encode_data_value/2 encodes an array-of-structs field without raising
int8..int256 are representable: deserialize_type/1 returns an int variant, serialize_type/1 round-trips it, and encode_data_value/2 sign-extends to 256 bits big-endian per EIP-712

The whole surface is pinned against independent implementations the way docs/verification-ledger.md pins transactions: signTypedData vectors generated from BOTH ethers and viem, covering nested structs, arrays of structs, bytesN, and a negative int — following test/fixtures/vectors/generate.cjs's existing pattern
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: EIP-712 domain-separator policy or chain-id binding — this task fixes encoding conformance, not domain semantics
A typed-data message builder for Hyperliquid or any specific venue — orthogonal, and already fenced off by task 104
Refactoring Cartouche.Hex.pad/2's signature; adding a right-padding function beside it is fine, changing every existing caller is not
task.body:
`Cartouche.Typed` is the EIP-712 path the stack signs permits and orders through — task 69 records that ERC-2612 permit "already expresses it". It has four confirmed spec defects. All four were verified by executing the compiled module, not by reading it; the reproductions are below and should be turned into the failing tests before any fix.

1. `encode_type/2` DOES NOT TERMINATE for a type referencing 2+ distinct struct types. `do_encode_type/4` (typed.ex:811-836) updates its pending queue as `next_new_types = rest ++ Enum.reverse(new_types_r)` (typed.ex:831). When `rest` is non-empty and the current type discovers no new struct, `rest` is re-appended to itself instead of shrinking, so the queue never drains. Reproduced live: `Root` with fields `{"z","Zebra"},{"a","Apple"}` did not return in 4s. This is not an exotic shape — any `Order{maker: Person, item: Item}` hits it. It was never caught because every existing doctest uses exactly one distinct referenced type (`Person` twice, for `from`/`to`), and `test/typed_test.exs` (88 lines) never calls `encode_type` at all.

2. Referenced struct types are appended in field-discovery order. EIP-712 requires them "collected, sorted by name and appended". Fixing (1) without also sorting produces a terminating but still non-conforming `typeHash`.

3. `bytesN` is LEFT-padded. `encode_data_value(value, {:bytes, _})` (typed.ex:296) calls `Cartouche.Hex.pad(value, 32)`, and `pad/2` (hex.ex:632-635) prepends zeros. EIP-712: "bytes1 to bytes31 ... are zero-padded at the end to bytes32". The doctest at typed.ex:279-280 asserts the wrong answer, so the test suite ratifies the bug — this is the coverage-ratifies-the-constant pattern from CLAUDE.md, and the doctest must be corrected as part of the fix. Note carefully that the SAME `pad/2` is correct at typed.ex:292 for `:address`, because address is uint160 and numeric types are big-endian left-padded. One function is serving two opposite alignments; separate them and pin both in one test so this cannot regress.

4. Arrays of structs are broken in both directions. `encode_data_value(value, {:array, ty})` (typed.ex:300-304) recurses with a struct-name `ty` that has no matching clause -> FunctionClauseError (reproduced). And `do_encode_type`'s discovery guard (typed.ex:820) tests `is_binary(type)`, which is false for `{:array, "Person"}`, so `encode_type` returns `"Root(Person[] people)"` with `Person` silently omitted — a wrong hash even where nothing crashes.

Separately, `Type.primitive()` (typed.ex:25-33) has no int variant and `deserialize_type("int256")` raises `"unknown type: int256"`. EIP-712 defines int8..int256; signed fields (ticks, deltas, funding) are unrepresentable.

Severity ordering for the implementer: (3) and the array half of (4) are SILENT wrong signatures — no error, no validation failure until a counterparty rejects. (1) is a hang. (2) is a wrong hash. The int gap is a loud raise. Fix all of them, but write the silent ones' tests first.

Authority is the EIP-712 text plus two independent implementations — ethers `_TypedDataEncoder` and viem `hashTypedData`. Where the EIP is terse, agreement across those two is the spec in practice; a single implementation's behaviour is not.

task.title: EIP-191 personal_sign byte length, a recovery helper that applies the prefix, and the 65-byte signature invariant
acceptance_criteria: Recover.prefix_eth/1 uses the UTF-8 BYTE length of the message, matching go-ethereum accounts.TextHash and viem; a test pins a multi-byte message (e.g. "café" -> length 5, not 4) and asserts the exact prefixed bytes

A recover_personal_sign/2 (or equivalently named) function applies the prefix and recovers, so the use case Recover's own moduledoc advertises — verifying MetaMask / WalletConnect personal_sign payloads — works without the caller hand-assembling the envelope

The signature-width contract is made true or made honest: Signer.sign/3 (signer.ex:307-312) builds v as chain_id*2+35+recid and encodes it with :binary.encode_unsigned/1, so any chain id > 110 yields a 66-68 byte result, while Cartouche.signature() is declared <<_::520>> (cartouche.ex:103) and RecoveryBit.normalize_signature/2 pattern-matches <<rs::binary-size(64), v>> (recovery_bit.ex:100). A test signs on a non-mainnet chain id (e.g. Base 8453) and asserts the documented behaviour end to end, including that normalize_signature/2 does not FunctionClauseError
Signer.sign/3's @spec is narrowed from bare binary() to the real return type so dialyzer can see the contract; mix ci's MIX_ENV=test dialyzer stays clean

RecoveryBit's EIP-155 normalization no longer silently reads the process-global :chain_id (recovery_bit.ex:62, :143) when the caller can supply the signature's own chain — or, if the global stays, a test pins the documented failure for a signature from a different chain rather than leaving it to raise 'Invalid EIP-155 Signature' opaquely
Every touched module is at critical-tier >=95% coverage BEFORE mutating (raise coverage first if below, per the coverage gate)
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: EIP-712 encoding conformance — a separate task owns lib/cartouche/typed.ex and lib/cartouche/hex.ex; do not touch those files
Transaction.V1.add_signature/2's missing chain-consistency guard — related, but it is a transaction-envelope concern and would collide with the transaction surface's write set
New signer backends
task.body:
Three defects on the signing surface, all verified by execution.

`Recover.prefix_eth/1` (recover.ex:75) builds the EIP-191 envelope with `to_string(String.length(msg))` — grapheme clusters, not bytes. Its own `@doc` two lines above (recover.ex:60-63) says "the byte length of `msg`", so the implementation contradicts its documentation. go-ethereum's `accounts.TextHash` uses `fmt.Sprintf("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n%d%s", len(data), data)` over a []byte, and viem's `toPrefixedMessage` uses the byte size — two independent references agree. Reproduced: `prefix_eth("café")` emits `...\n4café` where every mainstream wallet emits `...\n5café`, so the digest differs and recovery silently fails. The only doctest uses "hello", where grapheme count and byte count coincide — which is why it survived.

The same module's moduledoc (recover.ex:19-20) sells it as the surface for "verifying user-supplied signatures (e.g. `personal_sign` payloads from MetaMask, WalletConnect)", but `recover_eth/2` does not apply the prefix and there is no personal_sign helper. A consumer following the moduledoc recovers the wrong address. Add the helper so the advertised path exists.

The signature-width defect is a type lie with a latent crash behind it. `sign/3` (signer.ex:307-312) computes `v = chain_id * 2 + 35 + recid` and appends `:binary.encode_unsigned(v)`. For any chain id above 110 — which is every chain in `Cartouche.Chain` except mainnet and the dead testnets — `v` does not fit in one byte, so the "65-byte signature" the moduledoc (signer.ex:10-11) and `sign_direct/4` (signer.ex:236) promise is actually 66-68 bytes. `Cartouche.signature()` is typed `<<_::520>>` (cartouche.ex:103) and `RecoveryBit.normalize_signature/2` matches `<<rs::binary-size(64), v>>` (recovery_bit.ex:100), so a Base or Sepolia signature FunctionClauseErrors there. Dialyzer cannot see it because `sign/3`'s spec returns bare `binary()`. The doctest at signer.ex:124-126 asserts the multi-byte behaviour, so again the suite ratifies it.

Decide deliberately which way to resolve the width contract and record the reasoning: either the concatenated form stops carrying EIP-155 v (returning 65 bytes with a parity byte, chain binding living in the transaction envelope where V1 already threads it), or the docs and types stop claiming 65. Do not "fix" it by widening the guard in one place and leaving the other two.

While in `RecoveryBit`: `recover_base/1` (recovery_bit.ex:143-151, :62) normalizes an EIP-155 v against `config :cartouche, :chain_id` — a process-global — in a library whose `Chain` module knows 24 chains and whose `Transaction.V1` takes a per-call chain id. Either thread the chain through or pin the failure explicitly.

Critical tier: this is signing. Raise coverage to >=95% on each touched module before mutating it.

task.body:
Verified against ethereum/execution-apis main: the trace_* namespace is absent from the spec, and src/debug/trace.yaml carries debug_traceBlockByNumber, debug_traceBlockByHash and debug_traceTransaction but not debug_traceCall. Cartouche.RPC ships four non-standard reads: trace_trx -> trace_transaction (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:1435), trace_call (:1586), trace_call_many (:1790) and debug_trace_call (:1872).

The README caveat already exists: packages/onchain/docs/cartouche/README.md:117 lists all four as absent from execution-apis. What is still missing: none of the four @docs says so, no provider refusal has been observed, and there is no probe, so a consumer only finds out deep in a pipeline.

trace_* is the OpenEthereum/Parity namespace, inherited by Erigon and implemented by reth (our archive node serves it, which is why every trace test is green here). Verify each client claim against that client's own documentation before writing it into a @doc, and cite what you checked. The probe follows Onchain.Trace.available?/1 (packages/onchain_evm/lib/onchain/trace.ex:218) and classifies refusals through task 2137's shared transport rather than string-matching.

task.title: Multi-endpoint live-test seam so node-portability rule 4 can actually be executed
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Test.Live gains a named-endpoint lane beside the existing single live_rpc_url/0: an endpoint is addressed by name (e.g. :archive, :alchemy, :infura, :cloudflare) and resolves to a URL from a per-endpoint env var, so a test can request the SAME call on two endpoints without the whole suite being re-run under a different env var

The existing live_opts/0 and live_rpc_url/0 keep working unchanged — all 56 existing call sites across test/rpc_integration_test.exs, test/filter_test.exs and test/rpc_debug_namespace_test.exs stay green with no edit. This is an additive seam, not a migration

A helper expresses rule 4's actual assertion shape: run one call against the privileged node AND against >=1 hosted endpoint, and assert on BOTH answers — the hosted endpoint's real refusal is as much a pass as its success. A hosted endpoint that answers -32601/-32600 must be recordable as the expected result, not treated as a test error

Absent env vars flunk with the exact export command for that endpoint, never skip — matching assert_node_available!/0's existing flunk style. A portability test that silently skips on the hosted lane is the exact failure this seam exists to prevent
assert_node_available!/0's hard chain-id-1 assertion is preserved or generalized per endpoint; a hosted mainnet endpoint must satisfy the same mainnet pin the archive node does

At least one real portability test uses the seam end to end and is green: re-verify base_fee/1 (task 127's subject) on the archive node and on >=1 hosted endpoint, recording the hosted answer verbatim
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Rewriting the existing integration tests onto the new lane — additive only; migrating call sites is a later task if ever wanted
The dev/anvil lane (dev_opts/0, ephemeral anvil boot) — untouched
Fixing base_fee/1 itself, or writing the trace_* portability docs — tasks 127 and 135 own those; this task only makes their evidence obtainable
A general RPC provider-abstraction or failover layer in lib/ — this is test infrastructure
task.body:
node-portability.md rule 4 says: "Verify on a second, unprivileged endpoint before claiming portability. Green on localhost:8545 alone proves nothing. A hosted endpoint's real refusal is evidence; our node's {:ok, _} is not." The same file then admits, under Honest limits, that "Rule 4 has no tooling today — whoever builds it should build it first."

This task builds it first.

The current seam is single-endpoint by construction. `Cartouche.Test.Live.live_rpc_url/0` (test/support/live.ex) returns one string from `CARTOUCHE_LIVE_NODE_URL`, defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8545, and `live_opts/0` bakes it into a keyword list used at 56 call sites across three test files. There is no way to express "this call, on that other endpoint" inside a test — the dual-endpoint base_fee verification recorded in node-portability.md's worked example was done by manually re-running the whole suite with a different env var, which is not something an acceptance criterion can require of a dispatched agent.

The consequence is concrete, not theoretical: tasks 127 and 135 both carry criteria demanding a hosted-endpoint observation, and as written neither is satisfiable with the current seam. Five read-surface tasks (128-132) want the same evidence. Every one of them is blocked on infrastructure that does not exist, which is why this is filed as a prerequisite rather than folded into any single one of them.

Endpoints are already available to the operator and need no procurement — ~/.secrets defines ETHEREUM_ALCHEMY_URL, ETHEREUM_INFURA_URL and CLOUDFLARE_ETHEREUM_API_URL (three distinct vendors on mainnet), alongside ETH_RPC_URL / ETHEREUM_API_URL and the Base/Sepolia URLs. Read the variable NAMES from the operator's environment; never print, log, echo or commit a value — these are credentialed URLs and an Alchemy or Infura URL embeds the API key in its path. A test that flunks must name the env var, not interpolate its contents.

Design note, deliberately left to the implementer: whether the named lane is a keyword/atom map, a per-endpoint module attribute, or a small struct is a judgment call — follow the file's existing style (module attributes + plain functions, no config) rather than introducing a config-driven registry. The one thing that is NOT a judgment call is the assertion shape: a hosted refusal must be a first-class expected outcome. If the helper can only express "both endpoints returned {:ok, _}", it has failed to encode rule 4 and would have ratified the base_fee bug.

The house idioms to reuse verbatim in docs and flunk messages: "a real result or its real refusal, never a skip"; "the consumer's node — not ours — as the case that matters"; "the identical green run on both endpoints is what the portability claim rests on".

acceptance_criteria: Exactly one JSON-RPC HTTP transport remains in packages/onchain: Onchain.RPC's do_rpc/3 and batch/2 route through Cartouche.RPC.send_rpc/3 (or its batch sibling), and the second POST path in lib/onchain/rpc.ex is deleted

Every in-repo pattern match on a raw JSON-RPC error from the RPC path is listed in the task outcome, found by grepping packages/*/lib for `code: -3`, `%{code:` and `-32_` (known sites: packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:437 and :745, packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/filter.ex:182, packages/onchain_aerodrome/lib/mix/tasks/aerodrome.capture_fixtures.ex:554). Each one either still matches once classification runs under send_rpc/3 or is updated in the same diff with a test

The `@default_ethereum_node "https://mainnet.infura.io"` fallback in lib/onchain/rpc.ex (no project id, cannot answer) is gone with the second POST path: a call with no :rpc_url/:ethereum_node and no :cartouche app-env node fails with an error naming the missing option, pinned by a test (added 2026-09-29 review)
out_of_scope: Deleting per-method duplicate wrappers — 2128–2131 and 9035 own those
Migrating onchain_tempo's private transport
Bang variants (foo!/N)
task.body:
Context (post-9030): hieroglyph and cartouche now live inside packages/onchain, namespaces unchanged, so Cartouche.RPC (lib/cartouche/rpc.ex) and Onchain.RPC (lib/onchain/rpc.ex) are two modules in one package, and task 9036 will rename both to one Onchain.RPC. The milestone is RPC unification inside the merged core before 9036: each spec'd method gets exactly one wrapper, one decoder and one struct, built on the single transport from task 2137. Put the surviving implementation in Cartouche.RPC for now (9036 does the rename), and delete the Onchain.RPC copy in the same diff. There is no second package, so there is no re-presenting wrapper to keep.

(2026-09-29 review) Single calls already share one HTTP path. Onchain.RPC's do_rpc/3 wraps Helpers.do_rpc/3, which calls Cartouche.RPC.send_rpc/3 (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc/helpers.ex:28-33). The only second POST path is batch/2. The real gap is that the hardening lives in Onchain.RPC alone. Cartouche.RPC.send_rpc/3 (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:515) has no retry, no telemetry and no refusal classification. Onchain.RPC's private do_rpc/3 (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:1308-1314) wraps every call in :telemetry.span([:onchain, :rpc, :request], ...), optionally retries (retry_rpc/4, :1352 — transport failures retry, JSON-RPC errors with a code are final), and passes the result through classify_node_refusal/1 (:1378), which turns -32601 / -32600 / -32001 into tagged outcomes pinned against live Alchemy responses (moduledoc :41-99). batch/2 (:1097) is a second POST path, and it reads its URL from :cartouche, :ethereum_node but its transport options from :onchain (:1529).

Make one transport. Cartouche's typed wrappers decode inside send_rpc/3 through its :decode option, while retry_rpc/4 is hardcoded to Helpers.do_rpc/3 and cannot wrap a typed call. So the hardening has to move under send_rpc/3; putting it on top would invert the nesting and silently drop retry. Onchain.RPC's do_rpc/3 and batch/2 then route through it, which gives the codegen'd and hand-written Onchain.RPC wrappers the same behaviour as the Cartouche.RPC ones.

onchain_tempo independently reimplemented -32601 -> :unsupported and its own Req transport (packages/onchain_tempo/lib/onchain/tempo/rpc.ex:164). That is a third copy of the same idea. It is noted here, not migrated.

The classification is the highest-value piece. Tasks 2127, 2131, 2132 and 2135 all build their capability answers on it and must not grow their own.

task.title: defrpc macro — codegen named JSON-RPC wrappers from declarative specs

task.body: The 11 existing Onchain.RPC.* wrappers follow a near-identical shape: per-arg validation + param construction + do_rpc(method, params, to_signet_opts(opts)) + an identical bang variant + a Descripex api() annotation. A defrpc macro expands a declaration like `defrpc :block_number, "eth_blockNumber", decode: :hex_unsigned, description: "..."` into the full function + bang + api() + @spec. Precedents that disprove the macros-are-scary objection: Phoenix.Router, Ecto.Schema, Absinthe.Schema — defrpc faces strictly less variance. The knob-growth failure mode is solved by NimbleOptions: the validate!/2 schema IS the macro's contract; adding a knob requires changing the schema, making drift visible. Variance to handle: per-arg validators, nested-map params, literal extra params, filter-key whitelist (eth_get_logs), :decode pass-through, descripex returns: variation. If a case doesn't fit, follow Ecto and add a sibling macro (defrpc_with_filter) rather than overloading defrpc.

task.title: ERC-7730 clear-signing descriptor parser + binding evaluator

task.body: ERC-7730 (eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7730) standardizes a JSON descriptor that binds calldata / EIP-712 typed messages / ERC-4337 UserOps to human-readable display rules. Three pieces (pure Elixir, no native deps): (1) descriptor loader/validator — parse the JSON schema, validate structural rules; (2) binding evaluator — given {chain_id, contract_address, calldata} (or EIP-712 payload, or UserOp), resolve which descriptor applies via the binding context (chain ID, address, EIP-712 domain separator, proxy detection); (3) display rule engine — apply field formatters (token amount w/ decimals, address w/ checksum/ENS, date, enum, interpolated strings) to decoded ABI/EIP-712 fields, producing {label, value, formatted_value}. Deps already in onchain: ABI decoding, EIP-712 hashing (Cartouche), ERC-20 metadata, Address checksum, proxy detection. Registry side (fetching curated descriptors from Ledger's repo/IPFS/CDN) stays OUT — start with caller-provided descriptors. Module layout: lib/onchain/erc7730.ex (load/1, format/2, format!/2) + descriptor.ex / binding.ex / formatter.ex. First pass covers common formatters; defer rare ones (NFT URI, recursive sub-message). Survey how Ledger/Uniswap reference impls handle proxy detection before implementing.

Selectors via Cartouche.Hash.keccak; named-signature decode via ABI.FunctionSelector. Three fixtures (ERC-20 transfer, Uniswap V3 SwapRouter02, EIP-712 ERC-2612 permit) under test/support/fixtures/erc7730/. 82 unit tests + 1 RPC integration test (live USDC decimals). Proxy/addressMatcher + registry fetch + includes/$ref + calldata/nftName sub-formatters deferred (documented). Verified: compile --warnings-as-errors clean, credo --strict clean, dialyzer 0 warnings, doctor 100%, coverage 84-88% per module, full offline suite 600/0.

task.title: Stop dialyzer cold-building the PLT per harness worktree (it OOM'd the host twice)
acceptance_criteria: A `mix dialyzer.json` run started in a freshly-created git worktree (no priv/plts present) reuses an existing core PLT instead of rebuilding the OTP+deps PLT from cold — verified by timing/log: cold-build path is not entered when a seed PLT is reachable.

The chosen mechanism is concurrency-safe under concurrency_cap=4: multiple simultaneous dialyzer runs across worktrees must not corrupt or race on a shared PLT file (either each worktree gets its own copy seeded read-only from a shared core, or builds are serialized — document which).
Main-checkout `mix dialyzer.json` behavior is unchanged (still finds priv/plts).
mix.exs dialyzer config documents WHY the path strategy changed (the harness-worktree cold-build OOM), referencing the existing OOM-mitigation comment.
out_of_scope: Not changing plt_add_deps/plt_add_apps tuning (the apps_direct mitigation stays).
Not a harness-side change — harness's general per-run memory watchdog is tracked separately (harness task 200); this is the onchain-side targeted fix so the common case never approaches the limit.
Not adding a CI workflow.
task.body:
Root cause of the 2026-06-04 double host-OOM (kernel watchdog panic 13:10 + jetsam OOM 13:41 -> reboot 13:48): the onchain reviewer check_command ends in `mix dialyzer.json`, and the PLT path is worktree-relative (plt_core_path/plt_local_path = "priv/plts"). priv/plts is gitignored, so it is ABSENT in every fresh harness run worktree. Each dispatched run therefore cold-builds the entire core+deps PLT from zero (all of OTP plus plt_add_apps [:mix, :hieroglyph]) in one mix/dialyzer beam -> the 12-27 GB runaway process (PID 16184 in the worktree run-1780547484818-438b5f97). Proof it was killed mid-build: the worktree's deps-dev.plt was truncated at 1.84 MB (core-PLT size) vs the complete 5.43 MB in the main checkout. Oban crash-only retry re-dispatched after reboot -> a second cold build (14:02-14:09 timestamps) -> second OOM. The harness node itself was calm at 30 MB; this was entirely the spawned check_command's dialyzer.

mix.exs already carries an "OOM mitigation: skip transitive deps" comment (plt_add_deps: :apps_direct) — but that only helps once a PLT exists; the cold build from zero in a throwaway worktree pays full cost every run.

Fix direction (implementer picks, must satisfy the concurrency-safety AC): either (a) point plt_core_path at an absolute shared path outside the worktree so the expensive cold OTP/core PLT is built once and reused read-mostly (deps PLT can stay worktree-local), or (b) have the check seed priv/plts into the worktree by copying from a known-good shared PLT before invoking dialyzer. (a) is cheapest but needs a guard against concurrent cold-build races under concurrency_cap=4.

RESOLUTION (2026-06-05) — premise was wrong; fix was upstream, not the PLT path. Measurement falsified the cold-build hypothesis: a single dialyzer run peaked at ~30 GB even with a fully cached PLT (the main checkout did too), and trimming plt_add_apps didn't lower it. The real culprit was in cartouche: `Cartouche.Assembly.compile/1` had seven fixed-arity tuple heads ({op,a}..{op,a,b,c,d,e,f,g}), each guarded by a large opcode atom-union — a 7-shape tuple_set product type whose success-typing fixpoint under compile/1's self-recursion exploded to ~30 GB peak RSS on OTP 29 (cartouche Task 103). cartouche 0.2.2 collapses those into one `def compile(op) when is_tuple(op) and tuple_size(op) >= 2` clause. Bumping onchain to `{:cartouche, "~> 0.2.2"}` drops a cold dialyzer build from ~30 GB to 0.94 GB peak RSS (measured on development, total: 0, warnings: []). No onchain-side PLT-path change, seeding, or serialization lock is needed — those were stopgaps for an irreducible-30-GB premise that turned out false. The earlier serialization-lock PR (#4, branch task-75-plt-seed) was closed unmerged.
task.implemented: Bumped {:cartouche, "~> 0.2.2"} — the Assembly.compile/1 tuple_set fix (cartouche Task 103) drops a cold onchain dialyzer build from ~30 GB to 0.94 GB peak RSS. No onchain-side PLT-path/seeding/lock change. PR #4 (serialization stopgap) closed unmerged.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Task 63 defrpc macro is unused — wrappers still hand-written
task.body:
Task 63's acceptance criterion #2 — "Existing 11 wrappers reimplemented through it with byte-identical public behavior" — is UNMET. `grep -rn 'defrpc' lib/` returns zero call sites outside lib/onchain/rpc/codegen.ex: every wrapper (block_number, chain_id, syncing, get_balance, get_transaction_count, get_code, eth_send_raw_transaction, and all `!` variants) is still a hand-written `def`. The `Onchain.RPC.Codegen` macro module, the `nimble_options` dep, and the `.doctor.exs` ignore entry were all added to support a macro that is never invoked — dead code.

The CHANGELOG (b67f5cc/a4d9d64, "### Changed — defrpc macro codegen") claims the wrappers "now expand from declarative specs" — materially false. `roadmap/tasks.toml` task 63 carries `verified = true`, also inaccurate. The audit corrected the CHANGELOG claim in this commit; this task tracks the actual decision: either (a) wire the uniform wrappers through `defrpc`/`defrpc_bang` as the task intended, or (b) per acceptance criterion #4 ("Kill the prototype if 3+ wrappers need bespoke escape hatches"), remove the unused macro + nimble_options dep + doctor ignore.

Corroborated by Claude (grep verification) + Codex. Filed by audit-review against commits b67f5cc/a4d9d64 on 2026-06-05; see .audit/b67f5cc-*.md.
task.implemented: Onchain.RPC now imports Onchain.RPC.Codegen and declares the uniform wrappers (eth_send_raw_transaction, get_balance, block_number, syncing, chain_id, get_transaction_count, eth_get_code + bangs) via defrpc/2 + defrpc_bang/2 instead of hand-written bodies; api/3, @doc, @spec stay hand-authored. rpc_codegen_test.exs asserts the macro call sites exist (catches the dead-macro regression).

task.title: Audit-surfaced: ERC-7730 tokenAmount renders wrong token symbol (clear-signing safety)
task.body:
`Onchain.ERC7730.Formatter.from_metadata/2` (lib/onchain/erc7730/formatter.ex:314) ignores its `_token` argument and unconditionally returns the descriptor's `metadata.token` decimals/symbol whenever `metadata.token.decimals` is present. When a `tokenAmount` field references a different token than the descriptor's `metadata.token` (e.g. via `tokenPath`, and the token is absent from `opts[:tokens]`), the amount is rendered with the WRONG token's symbol — e.g. a DAI amount shown as "1 USDC". For a clear-signing engine whose entire purpose is showing users what they sign, displaying the wrong token is a safety-relevant correctness bug.

Fix: `from_metadata` should only apply when the requested token matches `metadata.token`'s `address` (ERC-7730 `metadata.token` carries `name/ticker/decimals/address`), or only when the field has no explicit token reference (the implicit single-token case the resolution order documents). Add a guard + tests covering the explicit-token-mismatch path.

Corroborated by Codex + Claude (read formatter.ex, confirmed `_token` unused). Filed by audit-review against commit a82235d on 2026-06-05; see .audit/a82235d-*.md.
task.implemented: Onchain.ERC7730.Formatter.from_metadata/2 now only applies descriptor metadata.token decimals/ticker when the metadata token address matches the tokenPath-resolved token (Address.equal?/2); a tokenAmount pointing at a different token falls back to raw rendering instead of mislabeling with the wrong symbol (clear-signing safety). Test asserts DAI amount with USDC metadata renders raw (formatter_test.exs).

task.title: Audit-surfaced: ERC-7730 binding/descriptor hardening (domain match, EIP-712 type, malformed input)
task.body:
Codex second-opinion surfaced a cluster of ERC-7730 binding/descriptor robustness gaps (Claude verified the first two against source):

1. **Domain match too lax** — `Binding.match_domain/2` (binding.ex:167) skips any constrained domain key the payload omits (`not is_nil(actual_value)` guard), so a descriptor constraining `domain.name`/`verifyingContract` still matches a payload that omits that field. Decide whether a missing constrained field should be a `:domain_mismatch`.
2. **EIP-712 format-key matching reuses ABI selector parsing** — `find_format_by_type/2` (binding.ex:198) parses the format key via `ABI.FunctionSelector.decode/1` and matches `.function`; for EIP-712 the key is the `primaryType` and types should come from the payload's `types`/`encodeType`, not an ABI signature. `types_from_selector(fs)` yields `%{}` for a bare type name, so the Formatter loses type-aware coercion on EIP-712 messages. Nested `encodeType` keys (`Mail(...)Person(...)`) return `:no_format_match`.
3. **Duplicate format keys** — `find_format_by_selector/2` (binding.ex:184) silently picks the first of two formats sharing a selector instead of flagging the descriptor as invalid.
4. **Descriptor parse crashes on malformed input** — Codex reports `descriptor.ex` raises (FunctionClauseError / BadMapError / Protocol.UndefinedError) instead of returning `{:error, {:invalid_field, ...}}` for `"format": 1`, `"excluded": "#.x"`, `"params": "bad"`, and loads `{:ok}` for `"deployments": []`. Verify each against descriptor.ex and add validation + tests.

Corroborated: Codex (all) + Claude (items 1-2 verified in source). Filed by audit-review against commit a82235d on 2026-06-05; see .audit/a82235d-*.md.
task.implemented: Onchain.ERC7730 binding/descriptor hardening: domain constraints fail :domain_mismatch when a constrained field is missing; EIP-712 formats match by primaryType/encodeType (not ABI selector) with field types derived from payload types/descriptor schemas; duplicate calldata format selectors return {:invalid_descriptor,{:duplicate_format_selector,_}}; Descriptor returns validation errors (not crashes) for non-string format, non-list excluded, non-map params, empty deployments (binding_test.exs, descriptor_test.exs).

task.title: Audit-surfaced: ERC-4337 to_rpc_params validation can diverge from user_op_hash
task.body:
`Onchain.AA` derives the v0.7 packed `initCode`/`paymasterAndData` independently in two places — the hash path (`resolve_init_code`/`resolve_paymaster_and_data` in `pack/2`) and the RPC path (`maybe_put_factory_fields`/`maybe_put_paymaster_fields` in `rpc_map/3`). They handle invalid/malformed input inconsistently:

- `user_op_hash/4` rejects an invalid `factory`/`paymaster` address; `to_rpc_params/2` emits them verbatim with no validation (returns `{:ok, map}` with a malformed `"factory"`).
- An `init_code`/`paymaster_and_data` shorter than the 20-/52-byte split is hashed verbatim by the hash path but silently dropped by the RPC path (the `<<bin::binary-size(20), …>>` match fails → fields omitted), so the signed hash and the bundler payload can commit to different data.

Valid inputs agree (verified by the reference-vector + derivation-equivalence tests); the divergence is on malformed/invalid input. Extract one shared validator/derivation used by both paths so `to_rpc_params` and `user_op_hash` cannot disagree, and validate factory/paymaster addresses in `to_rpc_params`. Add tests for the mismatch cases.

Codex-flagged; Claude verified the inconsistency in aa.ex. Filed by audit-review against commits 3e58c57/222f3c0 on 2026-06-05; see .audit/3e58c57-*.md.
task.implemented: Onchain.AA v0.7 to_rpc_params and pack now single-source factory/paymaster fields through derive_v0_7_fields/1, so RPC params can no longer diverge from the hashed PackedUserOperation. Malformed factory/paymaster addresses and short init_code/paymaster_and_data surface identical {:invalid_*} errors from both user_op_hash and to_rpc_params (aa_test.exs).

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Onchain.MEV accepts block tags where a concrete block is required
task.body:
`Onchain.MEV` validates `max_block_number` (send_private_transaction) and `block_number` (send_bundle) through `Onchain.RPC.Helpers.normalize_block/1`, which permits block TAGS (`"latest"`, `"pending"`, `"finalized"`, …). Flashbots `eth_sendBundle` `blockNumber` and `eth_sendPrivateTransaction` `maxBlockNumber` require a concrete hex block-number quantity; passing `block_number: "latest"` shapes an invalid `"blockNumber": "latest"` the relay rejects, rather than failing fast with a clear error.

Add a stricter `normalize_block_number/1` (integer or 0x-hex quantity only; reject tags) for these fields and route MEV through it; keep `normalize_block/1` for tag-accepting call sites. Add tests asserting tags are rejected.

Codex-flagged; Claude concurs (normalize_block accepts tags by design). Filed by audit-review against commit 986a545 on 2026-06-05; see .audit/986a545-*.md.
task.implemented: Onchain.RPC.Helpers.normalize_block_number/1 added (non-neg integer→hex or valid 0x-hex quantity; rejects block tags). Onchain.MEV.build_bundle_params and normalize_optional_block now route blockNumber/maxBlockNumber through it instead of tag-accepting normalize_block/1 (still used by tag call sites). Tests assert tags rejected (mev_test.exs, rpc/helpers_test.exs).

task.title: Audit-surfaced: RPC batch + block decode crash on malformed node responses
task.body:
Two defensive-coding gaps where a non-spec node response raises instead of returning an error tuple (compliant nodes never trigger these; a buggy/hostile node can):

1. **batch** — `Onchain.RPC.decode_batch_responses/2` runs `Map.new(responses, &{&1["id"], &1})` before the graceful `other`/`nil` handling in `collect_batch_results/1`. A 200-body array containing a non-map element (e.g. `[1]`) raises on `1["id"]`. Guard `Map.new` to map items only so the existing "missing/unexpected batch item" error path is reachable.
2. **block decode** — `Onchain.RPC.Helpers.parse_block_transactions/1` and `parse_withdrawals/1` raise `FunctionClauseError` on a non-binary/non-map list member (`"transactions": [123]`); `parse_block_response` decodes an invalid hex `"number"` (`"0xZZ"`) to `nil`, masking it as a pending-like block. Add catch-all handling / surface a decode error.

Codex-flagged (3 items); Claude verified items 1-2 in source. Low severity (malformed-input only). Filed by audit-review against commits 3c39dd1/b3cc9b0 on 2026-06-05; see the corresponding .audit reports.
task.implemented: Two malformed-node-response guards. (1) Onchain.RPC.decode_batch_responses/2 filters non-map items before Map.new, restoring the graceful missing/unexpected-batch-item error path (rpc_batch_test.exs). (2) Onchain.RPC.Helpers.parse_block_response/1 now returns {:ok,_}|{:error,_}; parse_block_transactions/parse_withdrawals catch-all on non-binary/non-map members; invalid hex "number" surfaces a decode error instead of nil-masking as pending; decode_get_block_result threads the error tuple (helpers_test.exs).

task.title: Add eth_estimateGas RPC helper + auto-estimate gas in send_transaction
acceptance_criteria: An eth_estimateGas RPC wrapper exists and returns {:ok, gas} for a transaction-params map (to/from/data/value)
Signer.send_transaction auto-estimates gas (with a headroom multiplier) when :gas_limit is omitted
An explicit :gas_limit is still honored unchanged (no estimation call)
Integration test against a live node confirms a cold TIP-20 transfer is sized correctly and does not OOG-revert
out_of_scope: Changing the onchain_tempo Builder default (tracked in onchain_tempo's roadmap)
Per-chain gas-price oracle / EIP-1559 fee estimation (this task is gas LIMIT estimation only)
task.body:
Onchain exposes no `eth_estimateGas`. Every caller that builds a transaction — `Onchain.ERC20.transfer`, `Onchain.Signer.send_transaction`, and the downstream `onchain_tempo` Builder — must hardcode `:gas_limit`. Those constants go silently stale when on-chain gas accounting shifts: Moderato now charges a TIP-20 protocol fee (a Transfer to the `0xfeec…` collector) that pushed a cold-storage TIP-20 transfer from the old ~272k estimate to a measured ~560k, OOG-reverting at the hardcoded 400k/500k ceilings (`gas_used == gas_limit` exactly). The reference MPP SDKs (mppx) size every transaction via `eth_estimateGas` instead of a constant — see refs/mppx Session.ts / Charge.ts.

Add an `eth_estimateGas` wrapper at the RPC layer returning `{:ok, gas}` for a tx-params map. Then have `Signer.send_transaction` auto-estimate (apply a safety headroom multiplier, e.g. 1.25×) when `:gas_limit` is omitted, while still honoring an explicit `:gas_limit`. This is the foundational capability the onchain_tempo Builder will consume to stop hardcoding its own default.
task.implemented: eth_estimate_gas/2 + bang wrapper in Onchain.RPC; Signer.send_transaction auto-estimates gas (1.25x headroom) when :gas_limit omitted, honors explicit limit verbatim. Unit + integration tests; Signer 97% / RPC 88% coverage.

task.title: Migrate HTTP transport off cartouche's removed Finch seams (cartouche 0.5.0)
acceptance_criteria: mix.exs requires cartouche ~> 0.5 and the suite compiles
Onchain.RPC and Onchain.ENS no longer read :cartouche, :client / :finch_name and no longer dispatch against CartoucheFinch
No call to the removed Cartouche.HTTP.normalize_finch_result/1 remains (use the surviving normalize_response/1) — onchain compiles clean against cartouche 0.5.0
A live-node integration RPC call succeeds (no missing-pool crash)
onchain exposes its own transport-stub seam; the 6 listed test files stub via that seam and pass
Full offline suite green; dialyzer 0 warnings (drop the now-moot @dialyzer nowarn_function Finch suppressions in rpc.ex/ens.ex)
out_of_scope: onchain_tempo's builder_estimate_test.exs :cartouche,:client stub — tracked in onchain_tempo's own roadmap, depends on this task shipping first
Any change to cartouche itself (already shipped in 0.5.0)
task.body:
cartouche 0.5.0 swaps its HTTP transport from Finch to Req and, as part of that, **stops starting the `CartoucheFinch` connection pool** and removes the `config :cartouche, :client | :finch_name | :start_finch` seams. onchain has no Finch supervision of its own — `Onchain.RPC` (lib/onchain/rpc.ex, the `Finch.build/4` + `client.request(.., finch_name, ..)` path around the batch/single-request helper) and `Onchain.ENS` (lib/onchain/ens.ex, same pattern) both read `Application.get_env(:cartouche, :client, Finch)` / `Application.get_env(:cartouche, :finch_name, CartoucheFinch)` and dispatch against the now-unstarted `CartoucheFinch` pool. After the cartouche bump every onchain RPC and ENS call **raises at runtime** (no such pool).

Migrate onchain's transport off the removed seams. Preferred: move `Onchain.RPC` and `Onchain.ENS` to Req, mirroring `Cartouche.RPC.send_rpc/3`'s new approach (`Req.request/1` + the `Cartouche.HTTP.req_options/3`-style precedence merge, transport-error mapping). Alternatively, start and supervise onchain's own Finch pool from an `Onchain.Application` and stop reading cartouche's config. Either way, define onchain's own transport-override seam (a `config :onchain, :req_options` or per-module key) so consumers and tests stop depending on `:cartouche, :client`.

Bump `{:cartouche, "~> 0.5"}` in mix.exs. Update the test files that stub the old `:cartouche, :client` seam to onchain's new mechanism (Req.Test / function plug if Req, or the new onchain seam): onchain/test/onchain/signer_gas_estimate_test.exs, rpc_batch_test.exs, rpc_revert_test.exs, rpc_retry_test.exs, rpc_telemetry_test.exs, rpc_estimate_gas_test.exs.

REFINED SCOPE (2026-06-24, after reading cartouche 0.5.0 + onchain source) — three corrections to the above:

1. Production blast radius is exactly TWO functions, not "all RPC/ENS calls". The single-call path (`do_rpc` -> `Onchain.RPC.Helpers.do_rpc/3`, helpers.ex:29) ALREADY delegates to `Cartouche.RPC.send_rpc/3`, which is Req-based in 0.5.0 — single calls are production-safe after the bump with no code change. Only these drive Finch directly and must be rewritten to Req: `Onchain.RPC.send_batch_request/2` (rpc.ex:1033-1047, the JSON-RPC array-batch POST) and `Onchain.ENS.gateway_http/4` (ens.ex:783-803, the CCIP-read gateway).

2. Extra HARD COMPILE break, independent of the runtime-pool issue: both functions call `Cartouche.HTTP.normalize_finch_result/1`, but cartouche 0.5.0's `Cartouche.HTTP` exposes only `normalize_response/1` + `req_options/3` — `normalize_finch_result/1` is GONE. onchain will fail to compile on bump until both callsites move to `normalize_response/1` (or onchain's own normalizer). Also drop the two `@dialyzer {:nowarn_function, ...}` Finch suppressions (rpc.ex:1032, ens.ex:780).

3. The test-seam break is BROADER than the 2-function lib change. All 6 test files stub via a Finch-shaped StubClient + `Application.put_env(:cartouche, :client, ...)`. After the bump cartouche's `send_rpc` no longer reads `:cartouche, :client`, so even the SINGLE-CALL tests (rpc_revert, rpc_retry, rpc_estimate_gas, rpc_telemetry, signer_gas_estimate) break via a dead stub seam despite their production path being unchanged. All 6 migrate regardless of which lib path they exercise.

Concrete impl: add `Onchain.HTTP.req_options/3` mirroring `Cartouche.HTTP.req_options/3` (merge base <- `config :onchain, <owner>` <- `config :onchain, :req_options` <- per-call `:req_options`); reuse the still-public `Cartouche.HTTP.normalize_response/1`. Rewrite the 2 functions to `Req.request/1` (`method: :post, decode_body: false, retry: false`). Migrate the 6 tests to the Req.Test plug seam — copy cartouche's proven pattern verbatim from cartouche/test/filter_test.exs:16,38,136 and sleuth_test.exs: a plug fn doing `conn |> Req.Test.raw_body() |> Jason.decode!()` then `Req.Test.json(conn, resp)`, injected via `req_options: [plug: &StubClient.call/1]`.
task.implemented: Bumped cartouche ~> 0.5. Rewrote Onchain.RPC.send_batch_request/2 + Onchain.ENS.gateway_http/4 to Req.request/1 (decode_body: false, retry: false) via new Onchain.HTTP.req_options/3 (:onchain transport seam) + Cartouche.HTTP.normalize_response/1. Dropped @default_finch_name, :cartouche,:client/:finch_name reads, normalize_finch_result calls, and the Finch @dialyzer nowarn suppressions. Migrated 6 stub tests to Req.Test plugs via owner-config seams; added {:plug, only: [:dev,:test]}. Offline 808 pass, RPC integration 30/30, dialyzer 0.

task.title: Mutation-grade DEX math invariants
acceptance_criteria: DEX properties pin integer rounding, fee application, path monotonicity, minimum-output/slippage behaviour and quote semantics against official protocol formulas or deployed calls at the same block
A reproducible mutation campaign over packages/onchain/lib/onchain/dex/ changes arithmetic and boundaries; every survivor is classified with evidence
A wrong-rounding canary and a wrong-slippage canary are detected and make the verification run fail
A ledger records authorities, live block/evidence, configuration, mutations and survivor review; touched DEX modules stay at >=95% coverage
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: RPC construction and decoding, owned by 3099
Swap execution calldata, owned by 3094
task.body:
Put the DEX money math under property and mutation adequacy. Onchain.DEX.Router quotes v2 pools analytically and v3 through the on-chain QuoterV2 (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/dex/). An integer-rounding, fee-application or slippage fault produces a plausible quote that no round-trip test rejects. The authorities are the official protocol formulas and deployed contract calls at the same block. Self-built fixtures alone are not an independent authority.

(2026-09-29 review) Depends on 3094. Onchain.DEX.Router today only routes and quotes (route/5, quote_pool/4, amount_out_v2/4 in packages/onchain/lib/onchain/dex/router.ex); it carries no minimum-output or slippage code. The slippage properties and the wrong-slippage canary below have nothing to grade until 3094 adds the swap builders, and a campaign run before 3094 would mutation-grade code 3094 is about to change.

RPC wire construction was split out to 3099. It waits on the RPC unification (9035), because mutating Onchain.RPC today would measure code that is about to be merged or deleted.

muex is already a dev/test dependency of packages/onchain (0.11.2 locked). Reuse the campaign mechanics in packages/onchain/.mutation/cartouche/run.sh: one invocation, all 18 mutators, `--no-filter --no-optimize --coverage-guided`.

task.title: Onchain.RPC block-level reads — receipts, transaction counts, transactions by index, and the block access list
acceptance_criteria: All six methods are exposed on Onchain.RPC through the existing codegen/specs path, with the api/3 declarations and bang variants the module's conventions require

get_block_receipts returns the same receipt representation as get_transaction_receipt, proven by a live test that fetches one block's receipts in bulk and asserts a specific transaction's receipt is byte-identical to the one returned by the single-receipt call for the same hash

The two transaction-count methods and the two by-index methods are pinned by live tests against a known mainnet block, asserting concrete counts and a specific transaction hash at a specific index, not merely shape
A by-index call with an out-of-range index pins the node's actual observed response

eth_getBlockAccessList is verified against the live node and its real response shape is pinned; if the node does not implement it the test flunks naming the method and the node's error rather than skipping
Any Onchain.Block convenience added on top of these reads is documented in the module's moduledoc table
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: eth_createAccessList — call simulation, filed against cartouche
A block-indexing or caching layer
Changing the existing get_block_by_number/get_block_by_hash surface
task.body:
A completeness sweep of the whole stack against `ethereum/execution-apis` found six block-level reads that neither cartouche nor onchain implements. They form one surface — every one of them answers a question about a block — and onchain is the layer that owns block reads (`Onchain.Block`, `Onchain.RPC.get_block_by_number/2`), so they belong here rather than in the substrate.

- `eth_getBlockReceipts` returns every receipt in a block in one call. Today a caller fetches the block and then issues one `eth_getTransactionReceipt` per transaction, which for a full block is a few hundred round trips where one would do. This is the highest-value entry of the six.
- `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash` and `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber` return a transaction count without transferring the block body.
- `eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex` and `eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex` fetch a single transaction positionally, without the surrounding block.
- `eth_getBlockAccessList` returns the EIP-7928 block access list. This is a block read and unrelated to `eth_createAccessList`, which is a call-simulation method filed against cartouche; do not conflate the two.

All six are present in the vendored `priv/specs/openrpc-v1.0.0-beta.4.json`, so they should go through the existing `Onchain.RPC.Codegen` / `Onchain.RPC.Specs` path like their neighbours rather than being hand-rolled. Reuse the receipt and transaction deserializers the module already has; `eth_getBlockReceipts` in particular must produce the same receipt representation as `eth_getTransactionReceipt` so the two are interchangeable to a caller.

`eth_getBlockAccessList` is recent and client support is uneven — verify against the live node what it actually returns before pinning a shape, and record the observation.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787623789150-bfda45c6, fce343cefaa9eada19900ef931056ff0bfe9376a).

task.title: Multi-slot storage reads: many eth_getStorageAt calls in one batched round trip, with eth_getStorageValues only as a probed fast path
acceptance_criteria: A multi-slot, multi-account read returns every requested slot in one round trip through task 2137's batch primitive and works against a hosted endpoint (Alchemy); a live test at a pinned block asserts each value equals task 2130's single-slot eth_getStorageAt for the same account and slot

eth_getStorageValues is sent with the spec shape [{address => [slots]}, block] and used only when a capability probe succeeds; the hosted refusal is pinned by a live test, and reth's answer to the spec shape is pinned (a success, or the observed error recorded verbatim)
When the fast path is used, its per-account result map is returned in the caller's request order, and a live test asserts equality with the batched eth_getStorageAt path at the same block
The representation of a never-written slot and of an account with no code is established against the live node and pinned by a test
Tests that need an endpoint flunk with the exact env vars to export, never skip
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: EIP-1967 proxy-slot helpers or storage-layout decoding built on this read
eth_getProof
The single-slot eth_getStorageAt wrapper (task 2130)
task.body:
Task 2130 (a dependency) adds the single-slot eth_getStorageAt wrapper. Still missing is the multi-slot read. Reading five slots from three contracts costs fifteen requests today, and proxy-implementation detection (EIP-1967 slots) and packed-struct or mapping reads need many slots at once.

The portable construction comes first. Many eth_getStorageAt calls across many accounts go out in one round trip through the JSON-RPC array batch primitive that task 2137 puts on the shared transport.

eth_getStorageValues is a fast path only. It is in the tagged execution-apis spec since v1.0.0-beta.5 (src/eth/state.yaml). Its params are `[{<address>: [<slot>, …], …}, <block>]`, a map from address to slot list followed by a block, and its result is a map of the same shape (see the example in state.yaml). Spec presence is not availability. Alchemy mainnet refused it with `-32600 "Unsupported method"` (observed 2026-08-25). reth is unsettled: the `-32602 Invalid params` recorded in packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:95 is reth's answer to empty params, not to the spec shape, so re-probe it with the spec shape. Gate the fast path on a capability probe that uses task 2137's refusal classification.

Sequenced after 9035, which leaves one merged RPC module (Cartouche.RPC until the 9036 rename). Add the read there and follow its defrpc convention.

Authority: execution-apis v1.0.0-beta.7 src/eth/state.yaml plus the live node.

task.title: Mutation-adequacy campaign over the signing, key and address surface
acceptance_criteria: The Oeditus/muex#20 reproduction reports survived=2 and a 0% score on the installed muex version, recorded with that version alongside the campaign result. No survivor triage is started until this passes

A single-invocation campaign covers lib/onchain/signer.ex, private_key.ex, address.ex, hex.ex and abi.ex with all 18 mutators, no filtering and no sampling, from a reproducible script committed under .mutation/
Every survivor is dispositioned in writing as one of: killed by a new test added in this task, provably equivalent with the argument, or an accepted gap with the reason. None is left unclassified
Every no_coverage result is dispositioned too: either a new test reaches the line, or the line is justified in writing as unreachable from the public surface
A ledger under docs/ records muex version, mutator set, per-module counts and each disposition
mix ci passes and the touched modules stay at or above their current coverage
out_of_scope: RPC construction, DEX arithmetic and the live-node differential evidence. Task 84 owns those
Adopting muex as a mix ci gate. This stays an on-demand measurement plus the tests it produces
Patching muex under deps/ to work around #20. A measurement produced by a hand-patched tool is not a durable verification record
The subscription, ENS, ERC-7730 and account-abstraction surfaces
task.body:
Task 84 puts RPC construction and DEX arithmetic under mutation. It does not touch the other money-critical surface in this library, and nothing else does either: lib/onchain/signer.ex (416 lines), private_key.ex, address.ex, hex.ex and abi.ex are local implementations, not thin wrappers - grep reports zero defdelegate in signer.ex, private_key.ex and address.ex - so cartouche campaign over its own signing modules does not reach them. This task covers that gap.

Why this surface specifically: a signing fault is silent. A wrong recovery bit, a mis-derived address, a hex encoder that drops a leading zero - each produces well-formed output that a round-trip test accepts and only a counterparty rejects. Cartouche campaign on the equivalent surface found exactly that shape: V3.sign/1, the default-signer route, had no test reaching it at all. The coverage class exposed it; a mutation score never would have.

Blocked on the tool, not on the work. muex 0.8.2 cannot report a surviving mutant on Elixir 1.20: Muex.TestRunner.Port.count_failures/2 matches the pre-1.20 ExUnit summary wording (N tests, M failures), while 1.20 prints Result: N passed / Failed: N test. The regex misses, the fallback returns 1 failure, and the only path to :survived is unreachable - every survivor comes back killed and a suite that asserts nothing scores 100%. Filed as Oeditus/muex#20 (2026-08-23) with a four-file reproduction and a patch; upstream acknowledged it the same morning. Verified against cartouche task 114, which hit this and could not produce its central deliverable. Do not start the survivor half until an installed release passes the reproduction.

Note what is NOT blocked, because it is the half that already paid off elsewhere. The no_coverage and equivalent classes are decided before or without running a test - no_coverage from the coverage index in select_tests/2, equivalent by Trivial Compiler Equivalence bytecode comparison - so the defect does not touch them, and in cartouche they produced the campaign single most useful finding. If the upstream fix stalls, a coverage-class-only pass over this surface is still worth running, and the ledger must then say plainly that the survivor axis was not measured.

Add the dep in the same change (only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false, matching cartouche) at whatever release carries the #20 fix. Do not pin 0.8.2.

Copy the campaign mechanics rather than re-deriving them: ~/_DATA/code/cartouche/.mutation/run.sh runs ONE invocation over the whole surface with all 18 mutators and --no-filter --no-optimize --coverage-guided. Per-module invocations are not equivalent in cost - muex rebuilds its coverage line index by running the suite once per test file, serially, with no cache, so N invocations pay that N times over. In cartouche that is what exhausted a harness run lifetime budget.

Routing is left open on purpose. The surface is a dispatch trigger and the tool now works, so this is genuinely dispatchable - but rmap freezes assignee at creation, and nobody has yet measured what a campaign over this surface costs in wall-clock or in survivor-triage judgement. Decide the routing when the campaign is actually scheduled, not here.

Confirmed 2026-08-24 on muex 0.8.3 (released the same day; Oeditus/muex#20 closed 09:42Z): the four-file reproduction reports survived=2 and a 0.0% score on Elixir 1.20.2 / OTP 29, and the converse check - the same two mutants against a value-asserting test - reports killed=2 and 100%, so the tool is not simply calling everything survived now.
