task.title: Expose hieroglyph's strict decode mode through the Onchain.ABI, Contract and Log decode surface
acceptance_criteria: Onchain.ABI.decode_response, decode_types, decode_error and their bang variants accept an optional trailing keyword list forwarded to hieroglyph; existing arity call sites compile and behave unchanged
Onchain.Contract.call and Onchain.Log.decode_event accept and forward decode options the same way

With strict: true, each violation class hieroglyph documents — non-zero high padding on bool/uint/int, trailing bytes after the declared payload, length prefix exceeding available data — surfaces as a tagged error tuple consistent with each module's documented error table, asserted by unit tests with hand-built non-canonical payloads
Default behavior without opts is byte-identical to today, demonstrated by the existing suites passing unmodified
api() blocks and moduledoc error tables document the option
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Making strict decoding a default anywhere — defaults stay permissive
onchain_aave's adoption of strict decoding — its own roadmap tracks that
New strict semantics beyond what hieroglyph implements
task.body:
hieroglyph has shipped a strict decode mode since 1.5.0: `strict: true` rejects non-canonical ABI payloads — non-zero high padding on bool/uint/int, trailing bytes after the declared payload, string/bytes length prefixes exceeding the available data — as `{:error, {:strict_violation, detail}}` from ABI.decode/3, ABI.decode_call/3, ABI.decode_event/4 and ABI.decode_error/3. Through this library's wrappers the mode is unreachable except via decode_call: Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 and decode_error/2 take no options and call hieroglyph without any, and Onchain.Contract.call and Onchain.Log.decode_event give the caller no way to pass options either (verified by reading lib/onchain/abi.ex and lib/onchain/log.ex, 2026-08-25; decode_call/3 already forwards opts).

This is a published package whose consumers decode bytes they do not control: responses from whatever RPC endpoint they configure, revert blobs, third-party calldata, and event logs. Thread an optional trailing options keyword through the decode surface as additive arities, forwarding to hieroglyph unchanged. Strict violations surface as tagged tuples consistent with each module's documented error table; bang variants raise. Nothing about the permissive default may change.

Dispatch trigger: public API change on the family's core package, on the decode path every money-handling consumer sits on.

Related (was a cross_repo link before the monorepo roadmap merge, 2026-08-27): Task 4065 (onchain_aave, related).
task.implemented: Landed by grok via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1787623766261-0173b997, 3d7513524dd57489eeb3064c119612fe5bcb0277).

task.title: Route Onchain.Signer.sign_transaction through cartouche's {backend, config} carrier instead of the legacy MFA
acceptance_criteria: Cartouche.Signer exposes a public direct-signing path for a {backend, config} carrier that runs Backend.expect_algorithm/3 and backend.sign_payload/2; the MFA path keeps working for existing callers
Onchain.Signer.sign_transaction/3 dispatches through {Cartouche.Signer.Secp256k1, key_bin} rather than an MFA
The existing signer tests still recover the expected signer address from the signed V2
A unit test with a stub backend whose algorithm/1 returns :ed25519 gets a tagged error and no signature
Onchain.AA.sign_user_operation stays on sign_digest/2 and its :raw and :eip191 suites pass unchanged
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: CloudKMS, AWS KMS or any non-Curvy backend as a supported Onchain.Signer option
Changing Onchain.AA's digest scheme, or rescuing FunctionClauseError on a short digest — no public path can feed one
Cartouche.Transaction.V4 and EIP-7702
hieroglyph strict decode — task 88 owns that
task.body:
Onchain.Signer.sign_transaction/3 (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/signer.ex:204-218) builds mfa = {Cartouche.Signer.Secp256k1, :sign, [key_bin]} and calls Cartouche.Signer.sign_direct/4. sign_direct/4 matches only an MFA (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/signer.ex:335). It does apply(mod, fun, [message | args]) and never runs Backend.expect_algorithm/3 or sign_payload/2. Only the private backend_sign/4 clause for a {backend, config} carrier (:371) does both, and it is reachable only through the Signer GenServer. So the enforced signer contracts (32-byte digest in sign_payload/2's function head, curve check before dispatch) never reach direct transaction signing.

Add a public direct-signing entry point for a {backend, config} carrier. Either add a sign_direct clause for a 2-tuple, or add a sibling function sharing backend_sign's body. Then move sign_transaction/3 onto {Cartouche.Signer.Secp256k1, key_bin}, which implements algorithm/1 and sign_payload/2 after task 9026. The public API does not change: private key in, signed %V2{} out. The existing recovery assertions in the signer suite show the digest is unchanged.

Onchain.AA already signs a keccak digest via Secp256k1.sign_digest/2 (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/aa.ex:596) and stays as is.

task.title: Onchain.Filter (renamed Cartouche.Filter): Subscription-compatible delivery and optional ABI event decoding, so HTTP log/block/pending polling works on the default transport
acceptance_criteria: No new module wraps the filter GenServer: the changes live in Onchain.Filter itself (the post-9036 name of Cartouche.Filter), and `grep -rn 'Cartouche.Filter' packages/*/lib` is empty

An Onchain.Filter with kind: :log delivers the same message shape a Subscription {:logs, filter} consumer receives, and substitutes for it against an HTTP rpc_url on a known mainnet Transfer log, asserted on address and topic0

The :block kind either delivers headers in Subscription's :new_heads shape or the hash-vs-header divergence is documented next to Onchain.Subscription's message table and pinned by a test; :pending delivers a hash list in a tested shape
Stopping the filter uninstalls the node-side filter, asserted with a follow-up eth_getFilterChanges that the node rejects, not assumed
A kind: :log filter given an ABI event decodes matching logs through the surviving ABI event decoder before delivery, including an event with a tuple parameter
The delivered message shapes for both transports are documented side by side in the moduledocs
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Modifying or replacing Onchain.Subscription — the WebSocket path is unchanged

Named Onchain.RPC wrappers for cartouche 0.8.0's node-custody methods (accounts, coinbase, fill_transaction, sign, sign_transaction, send_transaction) — Onchain.RPC.call/3 already passes any method through, so wrappers are ergonomics with no capability behind them; file separately if a caller actually wants them
eth_createAccessList, eth_baseFee, eth_blobBaseFee, eth_config and eth_capabilities — other 0.8.0 additions, unrelated to filters
hieroglyph strict decode — task 88 owns that
A new facade or wrapper module over the filter GenServer; the re-scope of 2026-09-29 changes Onchain.Filter in place
Changing Onchain.RPC's default node URL (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:195); tests use an explicit rpc_url
task.body:
Onchain.Subscription is WebSocket-only: it drives :new_heads, :pending_transactions and {:logs, filter} through eth_subscribe (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/subscription.ex). A caller on an HTTP endpoint has no push path; the only log retrieval left is the one-shot Onchain.Transfer.fetch/2.

The HTTP sibling already exists: Cartouche.Filter (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/filter.ex) takes kind: :log | :block | :pending, delivers {:event, log} or {:hashes, hashes}, recovers from expired filters, and uninstalls the node-side filter in terminate/2 (filter.ex:100). Nothing outside its own module and tests starts it.

(2026-09-29 review, re-scoped) Do NOT add a new Onchain.* facade over it. That would create one more Cartouche.*/Onchain.* duplicate pair, the exact class 9035 removes. This task runs after 9036, when the module is Onchain.Filter, and changes that module in place:
1. Align its delivered message shapes with Onchain.Subscription's, so a consumer can switch transports without rewriting its receive loop. One mismatch is real, not cosmetic: an eth_subscribe newHeads subscription pushes block headers, while eth_newBlockFilter returns block hashes. Resolve it explicitly: either the :block poller fetches the headers, or the difference is documented and tested as the one intended divergence.
2. Add optional decoded contract-event delivery (the viem watchContractEvent shape) through the package's single surviving ABI event decoder after 9035, including tuple parameters. Do not revive Onchain.Log's comma-splitting parser (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/log.ex:1-12), which 9035 removes.

Known trap for the tests: Onchain.RPC's default node URL is `https://mainnet.infura.io` (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/rpc.ex:195) with no project id, so it does not answer. Every live test passes an explicit rpc_url. Fixing the default is out of scope here.

task.title: Normalize node-capability refusals into typed errors instead of passing the raw JSON-RPC code through
acceptance_criteria: A method the node does not implement returns a distinct, documented error term rather than the raw {:rpc_error, map} — verified by a live call to a real endpoint that genuinely refuses the method, with the observed code and message recorded in the test

A method whose namespace the provider has disabled and a call whose historical state has been pruned are each pinned against a real endpoint that actually produces them; if the response for one of these is indistinguishable from another case at the wire level, the task records that finding and does not invent a distinction the node does not make
An RPC error code the classifier does not recognize reaches the caller byte-identical to today, proven by a test asserting the existing shape is unchanged

The classification happens once on the shared result path, so a codegen'd wrapper, a hand-written wrapper and Onchain.RPC.call/3 all return the same classified term for the same refusal — asserted for one method through all three routes
Tests that need a limited endpoint flunk with the exact env var and setup instructions when it is not configured, and never silently skip
The moduledoc documents each classified error term and what a caller should do about it
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Retrying, falling back to another endpoint, or any automatic degradation — this task only makes the refusal legible, it does not react to it
Probing what the node supports ahead of a call — that is the eth_config / eth_capabilities task in this bundle
Changing the success-path return shape of any existing method
task.body:
This library develops and tests against a full archive node reachable at `localhost:8545` (see the `ethereum-rpc` section of CLAUDE.md), which serves the `trace`, `debug`, `eth`, `net` and `web3` namespaces and retains all historical state. That node is not representative of what consumers run. Someone taking this package as a dependency is typically pointed at Alchemy, Infura, a public endpoint, or a self-hosted pruned node, where three things routinely differ: a method is not implemented at all, an entire namespace is disabled by the provider's plan, or the method exists but the state it needs was pruned.

Today none of those are distinguishable to a caller. `grep` over `lib/` finds no handling of `-32601`, no `:method_not_found`, and no `:unsupported` anywhere, so every one of these surfaces as an opaque `{:error, {:rpc_error, %{code: -32601, message: "the method ... does not exist/is not available"}}}` that a caller has to string-match on. CLAUDE.md already records the concrete consequence for the pruned case: a hosted endpoint answers `-32001 Unable to complete request` for a historical-block `eth_feeHistory` at block 20,000,000, depending on plan and load, and that is documented as prose rather than as something the library reports in a form a caller can branch on.

Give `Onchain.RPC` a single place where a node refusal is classified before it reaches the caller, so the three cases above become distinct, matchable error terms rather than one raw map. The classification belongs on the shared `do_rpc` result path so every wrapper — the codegen'd ones, the hand-written ones, and the `call/3` passthrough — inherits it without each having to opt in. `-32601` is the JSON-RPC 2.0 standard "Method not found" code; the others are node-specific, so treat the standard code as the reliable signal and pin the non-standard ones from observed responses rather than from assumption. A code this library does not recognize must keep passing through unchanged — the goal is to name the cases that are actually distinguishable, never to flatten every error into a guess.

Then document the resulting contract in the module's moduledoc, because the point of this task is that a consumer on a weaker node can write a branch instead of a string match.

Measured evidence (2026-08-25, orchestrator QA pass) — three real refusals observed while reviewing the RPC surface. Each was taken against Alchemy mainnet with an `eth_blockNumber` sanity call succeeding on the same URL in the same session, so these are method refusals, not transport failures:

- `eth_getBlockAccessList` -> `-32600` `"Unsupported method: eth_getBlockAccessList on ETH_MAINNET"`
- `eth_getStorageValues` -> `-32600` `"Unsupported method: eth_getStorageValues on ETH_MAINNET"`
- `eth_baseFee` -> `-32600` (already recorded in the `base_fee/1` portability note in `lib/onchain/rpc.ex`)

Note the code. Alchemy answers `-32600` (JSON-RPC "Invalid Request"), NOT the `-32601` "Method not found" this body names as the reliable standard signal. A classifier keyed only on `-32601` would be blind on the most common consumer endpoint. This is an observation to pin, not a licence to read `-32600` as universally meaning "unsupported": it is a generic code other nodes use for genuinely malformed requests, so the message has to carry part of the signal. Our own reth node answers `-32602` `"Invalid params"` for `eth_getStorageValues` — a third code for the same underlying "you cannot use this here". Pin what each endpoint actually returns rather than unifying them by assumption.
task.implemented: Onchain.RPC.do_rpc/3 classifies node-capability refusals into {:method_not_found,_} / {:namespace_unavailable,_} / {:unavailable,_}; -32601 unconditional, -32600 and -32001 message-scoped from live Alchemy+reth responses; -32602 deliberately unclassified. Adds Onchain.RPCCase.limited_rpc_url!/0 and a hosted-endpoint refusal integration suite.

task.title: Node pre-flight: live evidence for eth_config/eth_capabilities and a documented retention check before historical queries
acceptance_criteria: Live tests against the archive node assert domain meaning: a known chain id and fork identifier from eth_config, and a concrete retention boundary from eth_capabilities, not merely that a struct came back

Both methods are exercised against a second, non-archive endpoint and the real response is pinned, whether a capabilities report or the actual refusal; an unimplemented method is recorded as such, not skipped

A documented, tested pre-flight reads the retention window for the resource the query needs (state, blocks, transactions/receipts or logs, per resource, never one global oldestBlock) and decides whether a historical query is servable before issuing it; a test asserts the decision for a servable and an unservable block
README and the RPC moduledoc cover both methods and the pre-flight check
Tests requiring an endpoint flunk with the exact env vars and setup instructions when unset
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

go-ethereum#35781 is pinned: either a live test shows a receipt lookup failing inside the reported receipts window, or the pre-flight documents that receipt-by-hash servability cannot be decided from eth_capabilities alone, with a test for the documented behaviour
out_of_scope: base_fee/1 and blob_base_fee/1 — delivered inline 2026-08-25, before this task. base_fee/1 deliberately does not wrap Erigon's eth_baseFee (Alchemy rejects it -32600); it reads baseFeePerGas from the pending block header instead. That decision is evidence FOR this task, not a substitute: it was made by hand-probing two endpoints, which is exactly the pre-flight check eth_capabilities/eth_config should make programmatic
Automatically routing, retrying or degrading based on what the node reports — this task exposes the facts, it does not act on them
Caching the capability report across calls
Cartouche.Filter and the filter-lifecycle methods — task 90 owns those
Re-implementing or re-decoding eth_config/eth_capabilities; the merged core already owns them
task.body:
`eth_config` (EIP-7910, status Final, https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7910: current/next/last fork configuration, each with chainId, forkId, precompiles, systemContracts, blobSchedule and activationTime) and `eth_capabilities` (effective historical-data retention: head, oldestBlock, deleteStrategy per resource) are already implemented in the merged core: `Cartouche.RPC.eth_config/1` and `eth_capabilities/1` (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:918, :942), decoding into `Configuration` and `Capabilities` structs that ignore unknown fields. After 9035/9036 merge and rename the RPC modules they are on Onchain.RPC by construction. This task does not wrap them again.

What is missing is what makes them useful to a consumer. A hosted endpoint answers `-32001 Unable to complete request` for a historical `eth_feeHistory` at block 20,000,000, and the caller cannot tell 'this node cannot serve that block' from 'this call is wrong'. Deliver the evidence that these methods answer that question on real nodes, plus a documented, tested way to decide before spending the round trip.

Both methods are recent and support is uneven. Verify against more than one endpoint and pin what each actually does, including refusal.

(2026-09-29 review) `eth_capabilities` is not an EIP. It is a geth-originated method (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33828), so expect other clients and hosted providers to refuse it, and treat that refusal as a result to pin. Its report is per resource (state, blocks, transactions/receipts, logs), and the pre-flight must read the resource the query needs, never one global oldestBlock. It has a known divergence: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/35781 reports that receipts.oldestBlock ignores the transaction-index tail, while eth_getTransactionReceipt depends on it. A receipt-by-hash pre-flight built naively on that field says 'servable' for receipts the node cannot find. Pin it.

task.title: eth_createAccessList end to end: the access list feeds Signer.build_transaction unmodified, with gas comparison and partial failure pinned live
acceptance_criteria: A live call against the archive node returns an access list for a call touching known storage, and a test asserts the specific addresses and storage keys
The returned list is passed unmodified into Onchain.Signer.build_transaction/3 as :access_list in a test, producing a valid signed transaction

A test compares eth_estimateGas for the same call with and without the access list and records both numbers; no saving is asserted, because an access list can raise gas (EIP-2930 charges 2400 per address and 1900 per storage key, while EIP-2929 already pre-warms tx.origin, tx.to and the precompiles)
The access-list-plus-execution-error case is pinned against a live reverting call and its documented return shape asserted
What a second, non-archive endpoint does with the method is recorded, as a real result or its real refusal, never a skip
The moduledoc documents the method, the partial-failure shape and the build_transaction handoff
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: eth_getBlockAccessList — the EIP-7928 block-level read, owned by task 85; do not conflate the two methods
Automatically computing an access list inside build_transaction or send_transaction — the caller decides whether the extra round trip is worth it
Adding EIP-2930 type-1 transaction support; the access list here rides on the existing EIP-1559 V2 transaction
task.body:
`Cartouche.RPC.create_access_list/2` already exists in the merged core (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/rpc.ex:808). It wraps `eth_createAccessList` and returns `%{access_list: V_2930.access_list(), gas_used: ..., error: optional}` (the `access_list_result` type, rpc.ex:284). `Onchain.Signer.build_transaction/3` already accepts an `:access_list` option (lib/onchain/signer.ex, passed into V2.new). After 9035/9036 the RPC method is on Onchain.RPC by construction. The gap is that nobody has proved the round trip works.

Make the connection real. The returned list must be usable directly as `build_transaction`'s `:access_list`. If it is not, that mismatch is the finding, and the task reconciles the shapes rather than adding a conversion helper. `eth_createAccessList` can return an access list and an execution error at once. Decide and document what a caller gets, and pin it against a live reverting call.

Support varies by provider. Verify against the archive node and record what a second endpoint does. An unsupported method surfaces through the typed refusal classification, not a second convention.

task.title: Onchain.DEX swap execution: encode an executable swap for a quoted route, with a slippage bound
acceptance_criteria: A quoted %Route{} produces executable SwapRouter02 calldata: v3 routes as exactInputSingle / exactInput, v2 routes as swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256,uint256,address[],address), each wrapped in multicall(uint256 deadline, bytes[] data) because the SwapRouter02 param structs have no deadline field; each carries an explicit minimum-out derived from the quote plus a caller-supplied slippage tolerance and an explicit recipient
Each builder is pinned by an encoded-calldata unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding

A fork integration test executes the built calldata and asserts token balances moved consistently with the quote within the stated tolerance, and a second run with a violated slippage bound reverts; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions
Every router address cites Uniswap's own deployment record
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
A route mixing v2 and v3 hops returns a tagged error rather than calldata, pinned by a unit test
The fork test includes a run with the deadline already past that reverts inside multicall, proving the deadline actually binds
out_of_scope: DEX aggregators, split routing, multi-venue routing
Atomic composition with lending operations — aave_sim's one-transaction-rail task owns that
Aerodrome routers — task 5028 owns Write.Router on Base
task.body:
Onchain.DEX.Router routes and quotes — v2 pools analytically, v3 via the on-chain QuoterV2 — and nothing in the stack executes what it prices: there is no SwapRouter02 or UniversalRouter calldata builder and no aggregator client (surveyed 2026-08-28; the only swap-execution hit anywhere is a Tempo TIP-20 selector). The consumer demand is concrete: aave_sim's boost action is borrow, then swap, then supply, and its execution tasks (aave_sim 118/119) need the swap leg as bare calldata a one-transaction rail can compose.

Build the missing half: encode an executable swap for a quoted route on the canonical Uniswap SwapRouter02, with the minimum-out derived from the quote and a caller-supplied tolerance, a deadline, and an explicit recipient.

(2026-09-29 review) Two SwapRouter02 facts shape the encoding. (1) SwapRouter02's ExactInputSingleParams and ExactInputParams carry no deadline field (swap-router-contracts contracts/interfaces/IV3SwapRouter.sol). The deadline is enforced by wrapping the swap in `multicall(uint256 deadline, bytes[] data)` from MulticallExtended. (2) Onchain.DEX.Router quotes v2 pools too. A v2 route encodes as SwapRouter02's `swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMin, address[] path, address to)` (V2SwapRouter, also without a deadline), inside the same deadline multicall. A route mixing v2 and v3 hops is rejected with a tagged error in this baseline. Baseline before optimization: single venue, no split routing, no aggregator.

AUTHORITY: Uniswap's own deployed router contracts and documentation. The Uniswap JS SDKs are reference material only and cannot define calldata correctness.

Fork evidence cannot live in packages/onchain. onchain_evm depends on onchain (packages/onchain_evm/mix.exs:93, sibling(:onchain)), so onchain cannot take onchain_evm as a test dependency without a cycle. Put the fork test in packages/onchain_evm/test/ against the onchain builders, or run it against an anvil --fork-url node from packages/onchain.

Dispatch trigger: money-path calldata construction requiring live fork evidence.

task.title: Onchain.Signer type-0x04: build, sign, and broadcast EIP-7702 transactions
acceptance_criteria: build_transaction/3 accepts an :authorization_list and returns a Cartouche.Transaction.V4; sign, encode and send handle the V4 struct end to end
Authorization-tuple signing is exposed at the Onchain level and pinned byte-exact against the viem-2.55.19 and ethers-6.17.0 V4 vector fixtures in packages/onchain/test

Gas estimation passes the authorizationList to eth_estimateGas, which already includes EIP-7702's intrinsic per-authorization cost (PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST 25000); no overhead is added on top of the estimate, and a test pins that the estimate with the list differs from the one without it

An integration test broadcasts a real type-0x04 transaction on a testnet, asserts the delegation designator (0xef0100 plus the address) is readable via eth_getCode afterwards, and pins one real send error; missing credentials flunk with the exact variables to export
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: The delegate contract choice and batched-call encoding — task 3096 owns those
Blob transactions (Cartouche.Transaction.V3)
task.body:
Cartouche.Transaction.V4 already implements the whole EIP-7702 wire format — new/10 with an authorization list, sign_authorization/2, authorization_signing_payload/1, recover_authority/1 — cross-checked byte-exact against viem 2.55.19 and ethers 6.17.0 vector fixtures and a real mainnet type-0x04 decode (task 2032, done). Onchain.Signer wraps none of it: the module is hardcoded to Cartouche.Transaction.V2 in five places (the alias, build_transaction_validated/3, sign_transaction/3, both encode_transaction/1 clauses), recognises no :authorization_list option, and every @spec names V2.t() (surveyed 2026-08-28). The onchain CHANGELOG explicitly deferred this wrapping until a consumer needs 7702 set-code auth. Status 2026-09-23: that consumer has not materialised. aave_sim decided its rail (task 132 plus the operator decision of 2026-09-15, recorded in aave_sim docs/one-transaction-rail.md): a user-owned Safe is the execution account; the EIP-7702/DeleGator path is an optional adapter, and its attended path sends an ordinary EIP-1559 transaction to the already-delegated EOA — no type-0x04 broadcast anywhere in the application. ERC-4337 and the flash-loan executor were rejected. This task stays open as the adapter's transport half, scored accordingly; do not dispatch it before a consumer names a type-0x04 send.

Sequencing: 3089 reroutes Onchain.Signer.sign_transaction through the {backend, config} carrier. Build the V4 branch on that, not on the legacy MFA path. After 9032, V4 encoding and the authorization signing hash come from alloy through the core NIF with Cartouche.Transaction.V4's public API unchanged, so this task wraps that API and does not touch encoding.

Wire it through: an :authorization_list option on build, V4 branches on sign, encode and send, authorization-tuple signing surfaced at the Onchain level, and gas estimation that sends the authorizationList to eth_estimateGas. (2026-09-29 review) A 7702-aware node already counts the per-authorization intrinsic cost in that estimate, so adding EIP-7702's 25000 per tuple on top would double-count it.

Constraint measured, not assumed: onchain_evm's revm NIF does not expose authorization lists (zero grep hits in native/src), so fork simulation cannot carry a type-0x04 — live evidence comes from a testnet send, not a fork.

AUTHORITY: EIP-7702 and live network behaviour; cartouche's vector fixtures are the encoding oracle.

Dispatch trigger: money-path transaction surface requiring live testnet evidence.
task.blocked_reason: consumer-gated: no consumer names a type-0x04 send

task.title: EIP-7702 batched execution: extract aave_sim's pinned-delegate batch encoding into Onchain.Delegate
acceptance_criteria: The pinned EIP7702StatelessDeleGator v1.3.0 deployment is re-verified: deployed runtime bytecode matches its published source with compiler settings recorded, and the audit reference is written down
ERC-7579 execute(bytes32,bytes) builders for the pinned delegate, single and batch mode, are pinned by selector-and-encoding unit tests; no executeBatch function is assumed

A fork integration test in packages/onchain_evm/test/ plants the delegation designator (0xef0100 plus the pinned address) on an EOA via state override, as aave_sim's delegate_proof.ex does, and executes at least two calls through execute(bytes32,bytes) in batch mode: an ERC-20 approve followed by a call that consumes the approval
A negative control on the same path: a batch whose second call deliberately reverts leaves no observable effect from the first call, so the atomicity claim is verified rather than asserted

task.body:
Reframed 2026-09-23 as an EXTRACTION, not a build. aave_sim shipped its rail (tasks 118, 132, 146, 147 done) and carries the whole DeleGator half app-locally in lib/aave_sim/execution/delegate.ex: the pinned MetaMask EIP7702StatelessDeleGator (v1.3.0, 0x63c0c19a282a1b52b07dd5a65b58948a07dae32b) with runtime identity, execute(mode, batch) encoding in EXECTYPE_DEFAULT, and fork proofs in delegate_proof.ex. The operator decision of 2026-09-15 made a user-owned Safe the execution account and kept 7702 as an optional adapter, so this is adapter code with exactly one consumer. Lift it into Onchain.Delegate so the pin and the encoding live once in the package, then aave_sim consumes it. Before 2026-09-23 this body claimed no delegate existed anywhere in the stack (surveyed 2026-08-28); that survey is stale.

The delegate is already chosen and must not be re-researched here. It is MetaMask's EIP7702StatelessDeleGator v1.3.0 at 0x63c0c19a282a1b52b07dd5a65b58948a07dae32b, as pinned by aave_sim. Re-verify the pin rather than trusting the extraction source: deployed runtime bytecode against published source with compiler settings, plus the audit reference. A delegate controls the authorizing EOA outright, which is why bytecode identity and the negative control are the substance of this task. Then encode its ERC-7579 `execute(bytes32 mode, bytes executionCalldata)` calldata with the batch call-type mode, so a single transaction runs a caller-supplied call list. aave_sim's delegate.ex:38-42 is the extraction source: `@batch_default_mode`, `execute(bytes32,bytes)` and the `batch((address,uint256,bytes)[])` execution encoding. The DeleGator has no `executeBatch`.

(2026-09-29 review) The atomicity proof does not need a type-0x04 send, and it does not wait on 3095. aave_sim already proves the delegate on a fork (lib/aave_sim/execution/delegate_proof.ex:63-72). It plants the delegation designator `0xef0100 ‖ impl` as the EOA's code through a state override and runs the batch through Onchain.EVM.simulate_batch. Do the same. revm not exposing authorization lists only matters for the authorization tuple itself, which 3095 owns. onchain cannot take onchain_evm as a test dependency (packages/onchain_evm/mix.exs:93, sibling(:onchain)), so the fork test lives in packages/onchain_evm/test/ against the onchain builders.

Every wrapper takes the position owner as an explicit required argument and never substitutes the signer address for it. A test signs with one key and encodes a different `on_behalf_of`, asserting the owner in the calldata is the supplied one.

ABI shape is confirmed against the deployed contracts rather than assumed: at least one `@moduletag :integration` test issues a live `eth_call` against a Taker view (e.g. `borrowAllowance` or `BORROW_PERMIT_TYPEHASH`) on the mainnet archive node and asserts a decoded value, flunking with the required env vars when RPC is unavailable.

`InsufficientBorrowAllowance` and `InsufficientWithdrawAllowance` revert data is surfaced as a tagged error tuple carrying both the allowance and required amounts, not as raw hex; a unit test decodes each from its custom-error selector.
Invalid input is rejected before any RPC call: bad spoke/owner/spender addresses and a negative or non-integer amount return tagged error tuples, with tests.

The `approveBorrowWithSig` / `approveWithdrawWithSig` EIP-712 permit variants on the Taker — they belong with the Signature Gateway work above.
Sending live V4 transactions on mainnet. Write paths are pinned by encoded-calldata unit tests; V4 has no Sepolia deployment (see Task 52, blocked on one).
task.body:
Primary user-facing write surface for V4. V4 has no `Pool`: supply/repay go through the Giver Position Manager (`:v4_giver_position_manager`) and borrow/withdraw through the Taker Position Manager (`:v4_taker_position_manager`), both already registered in `Onchain.Aave.Contracts`. Follow the V3 `Onchain.Aave.Pool` write convention (validate addresses, split network/signer opts, encode + sign + send) so the two trees read alike.

Verified against the provider-owned interfaces at https://github.com/aave/aave-v4 (`src/position-manager/interfaces/`) on 2026-08-21 — build against the deployed contracts, not against these notes:

- Giver: `supplyOnBehalfOf(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, uint256 amount, address onBehalfOf)` and `repayOnBehalfOf(...)`, same shape, both returning `(uint256, uint256)`.
- Taker: `borrowOnBehalfOf(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, uint256 amount, address onBehalfOf)` and `withdrawOnBehalfOf(...)`. The **caller** receives the assets and must already hold an allowance granted by `onBehalfOf`, so the allowance surface is part of this task, not a follow-on: `approveBorrow` / `approveWithdraw(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address spender, uint256 amount)`, `renounceBorrowAllowance` / `renounceWithdrawAllowance(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address owner)`, and the views `borrowAllowance` / `withdrawAllowance(address spoke, uint256 reserveId, address owner, address spender)`. Insufficient allowance reverts with the custom errors `InsufficientBorrowAllowance(uint256,uint256)` / `InsufficientWithdrawAllowance(uint256,uint256)`.

Two shape traps worth naming. First, V4 addresses a reserve by `uint256 reserveId` **scoped to a Spoke**, not by the asset address V3 used — the reserve id comes from the Spoke reads landed in Task 48, and passing an asset address where a reserve id belongs encodes silently and reverts on chain. Second, every entrypoint above is either `onBehalfOf`-parameterised or allowance-gated; none infers the position owner from `msg.sender`. That is what makes the Safe/DELEGATECALL constraint satisfiable, and it is also the thing an ergonomic wrapper is most likely to destroy by defaulting the owner to the signer address for convenience. Keep the owner an explicit, required argument on every wrapper.

Use the deployed Ethereum V4 contracts as the semantic authority. Pin all live and forked calls to a named block so configuration changes cannot turn exact-value assertions into noise. The former Sepolia blocker is obsolete. Aave launched a public Tenderly-based V4 testnet on 2025-11-19, and V4 is now deployed on Ethereum mainnet. A testnet lifecycle is therefore not an authority or availability dependency for this task.

task.title: Onchain.Aave.DebtToken — wrap approveDelegation + borrowAllowance on variable/stable debt tokens
task.body:
Aave V3 credit delegation (approveDelegation(delegatee, amount) on the variable/stable debt token) lets a position owner grant another address the right to Pool.borrow(..., onBehalfOf=owner) against the owner's collateral. Observed on-chain 2026-04-22 — a real migration-off-automation flow the current write surface doesn't support.

Onchain.Aave.Pool covers supply/borrow/repay/withdraw but the delegation mechanism lives on the debt-token contract, not Pool. Build a thin wrapper exposing approve_delegation/4 (write) and borrow_allowance/3 (read) against the variable and stable debt token addresses. Debt-token addresses come from Pool.getReserveData(asset).variableDebtTokenAddress / .stableDebtTokenAddress — consider a helper that resolves (asset, rate_mode) → debt_token_address. Introduce an `EModeCategory` struct in `lib/onchain/aave/types/`, converting ltv / liquidation threshold / bonus through `Onchain.Aave.Math.to_ltv/1`.

STATED FACTS (established 2026-09-29):
- Aave v3.7 has been live on Ethereum Core since 2026-05-29 (https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog). v3.7 adds a per-category `bool isolated` flag; upstream `DataTypes.EModeCategory` is now EIGHT fields: `(uint16 ltv, uint16 liquidationThreshold, uint16 liquidationBonus, uint128 collateralBitmap, bool isolated, string label, uint128 borrowableBitmap, uint128 ltvzeroBitmap)` (aave-dao/aave-v3-origin `src/contracts/protocol/libraries/types/DataTypes.sol`). Re-point the registry entry to the address-book value as part of this task, and check the other networks' `ui_pool_data_provider` entries against safe.csv in the same pass.

(2026-09-29 review) The drift is wider than Ethereum: none of the six mainnet `ui_pool_data_provider` entries in contracts.ex appears in safe.csv (safe.csv now lists e.g. AaveV3Arbitrum 0x91E04cf78e53aEBe609e8a7f2003e7EECD743F2B, AaveV3Base 0x0C6BC4a12039788be08F87e87Cff87FEDbd1D386, AaveV3Optimism 0x68100bD5345eA474D93577127C11F39FF8463e93, AaveV3Polygon 0x66E1aBdb06e7363a618D65a910c540dfED23754f, AaveV3Avalanche 0xFBa4Df643205c5400BC3e05a1E67E0dFaEeeb41F). task.body:
Add two Aave V3 Pool writes that close distinct position-management gaps. Both reuse the module's signed-write boundary, while their acceptance depends on real state transitions rather than calldata alone.

`setUserUseReserveAsCollateral(address asset, bool useAsCollateral)` — selector 0x5a3b74b9, confirmed against the deployed mainnet Pool. This is how a caller stops an asset from backing debt without withdrawing it. Today the library can supply an asset but cannot un-collateralize it, so a user isolating risk across positions has no path through this package at all.

`repayWithATokens(address asset, uint256 amount, uint256 interestRateMode) returns (uint256)` — selector 0x2dad97d4. It takes no `onBehalfOf` and repays for `msg.sender`. Fix the internal mode at the only deployed supported value, `2`; do not expose a rate-mode option.

The `type(uint256).max` convention works transparently for full repayment: Elixir's arbitrary-precision integers pass 2^256 - 1 straight through and the Pool contract interprets it, so no client-side special-casing is needed — document it in the parameter docs the way `withdraw/4` already does.

task.title: Make the integration gate settle: bound math_revm runtime so --include integration terminates
acceptance_criteria: mix test.json --include integration terminates on a healthy archive node and reports a summary, with the wall-clock ceiling stated in the test module or CLAUDE.md
An unreachable or mid-run-dropped archive RPC fails the affected math_revm test loudly within a bounded time instead of hanging; no test retains timeout: :infinity
The revm cross-validation still fails on a real divergence — a deliberately wrong expected value in one deterministic vector makes that test red
The chosen coverage/runtime tradeoff is recorded in the test module's moduledoc, including how to run the exhaustive variant
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Funding the Sepolia key or fixing the four sepolia_send tests that fail with rpc -32003
Changing Onchain.Aave.Math itself or its Solidity wrapper bytecode
Reworking harness' progress-stall reflex
task.body:
`mix test.json --include integration` does not terminate under any practical time cap, which makes the repo's own live gate unusable for dispatched agents and for CI.

Evidence, all from 2026-08-23: harness run-1787478012579-900e9275 was killed by the progress-stall reflex while idle-waiting on this suite, and its transcript shows the agent had its own module green and was blocked solely on the gate. The reviewer of run-1787481036522-9e92c0d9 recorded `Did not finish in 17m (0% CPU, ~27MB RSS, DirtyIo NIF ESTABLISHED to 127.0.0.1:8545)`, plus SIGALRM 142 at 90s on `--only math_revm` and at 120s on `--only integration --exclude math_revm`, and fell back to running the suite file-by-file. A local full run of test/onchain/aave/math_revm_test.exs alone took 3055 seconds.

Two compounding causes: the math_revm modules set `timeout: :infinity`, and `Onchain.EVM` calls run on a DirtyIo scheduler, so ExUnit cannot interrupt a stalled archive fetch — a flapping node turns into an unbounded hang rather than a failure. Independently, every property does `max_runs` live fork calls, so the wall-clock cost is inherently large even when the node is healthy.

Give the suite a bounded, interruptible runtime without giving up the cross-validation guarantee that makes `Onchain.Aave.Math` trustworthy. Decide and document the coverage/runtime tradeoff explicitly rather than silently shrinking the property space: options include a finite per-test timeout, a smaller default `max_runs` with an opt-in exhaustive mode, reusing one fork across vectors instead of one per call, or separating the revm cross-validation into its own tag that the ordinary integration gate does not pull in. Whatever is chosen, `--include integration` must terminate and a dead or flapping RPC must surface as a loud failure, never as a hang.

task.title: Decode deployed Aave V3 Pool events from logs with topic-filter fetch
acceptance_criteria: An events module decodes the deployed v3.7 Pool's protocol events — at minimum Supply, Withdraw, Borrow, Repay, LiquidationCall, FlashLoan, ReserveDataUpdated and UserEModeSet — from raw log maps into named-field maps, with signatures and indexed layouts taken from aave-v3-origin IPool, not a third-party client

A pinned-block integration test fetches real mainnet Pool logs via Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs against the archive node and decodes them, asserting known field values of at least one historical Supply and one LiquidationCall log; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions

Topic-filter construction produces eth_getLogs topics for an event with optional indexed-argument filters, and the integration test round-trips one filter: build it, fetch live, and every returned log decodes as that event
Indexed reference-type parameters surface as their topic hash and the behaviour is documented
Unit tests pin decoding against log fixtures recorded from the live observations
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

`Onchain.Log.encode_event_topics/2` exists in packages/onchain as a one-line delegation to the core ABI `encode_event_topics/2`, Descripex-annotated and unit-tested, and nothing under packages/onchain_aave/lib references a bare `ABI.` module
out_of_scope: Aave V4 Hub/Spoke event decoding
Streaming/subscription (eth_subscribe) support and any indexer or backfill machinery
aToken/debt-token ERC-20 Transfer logs — Onchain.Transfer already owns token transfer decoding
task.body:
onchain_aave has no event surface: nothing reads or decodes the logs the protocol emits, so a consumer can execute a supply or borrow through this library but cannot observe its effect — or anyone else's activity — from the chain. Add log decoding for the deployed V3 Pool's event set plus topic-filter construction for eth_getLogs. No consumer has asked for this yet.

The in-family precedent is Onchain.Transfer: it fetches with Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs and decodes per-event with Onchain.Log.decode_event/2 against signature strings with indexed markers. Topic filters with indexed-argument values come from the core ABI layer's `encode_event_topics/2` (packages/onchain/lib/abi.ex:966). (2026-09-29 review) This task no longer waits for 9036: onchain_aave already calls only the stable facades `Onchain.Log.decode_event/3` and `Onchain.Log.event_topic/1` (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/log.ex:77,132). Add the one missing facade — a one-line `Onchain.Log.encode_event_topics/2` delegating to the core ABI function, with a Descripex api() block and a unit test — and call only Onchain.* names from onchain_aave; 9036 then renames the delegate target mechanically.

The deployed Ethereum Core Pool runs Aave v3.7 (live since 2026-05-29, https://aave.com/docs/resources/changelog). Current aave-v3-origin IPool declares: Supply, Withdraw, Borrow, Repay, UserEModeSet, ReserveUsedAsCollateralEnabled/Disabled, FlashLoan, LiquidationCall, ReserveDataUpdated, DeficitCovered, MintedToTreasury, DeficitCreated, PositionManagerApproved/Revoked. Isolation-mode debt events from earlier versions are gone. Take the event set from that source, not from a pre-3.7 ABI.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum Pool at 0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2 and Aave-owned aave-v3-origin IPool event definitions. Prove decoding against real mainnet logs at pinned blocks before deriving fixtures; third-party ABIs and explorers are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: public API addition with live external-system evidence against the archive node.

task.title: Surface decoded revert reasons on Aave write and call failures
acceptance_criteria: A revert blob returned by the library's call/estimate/send paths decodes through the core ABI layer's Error(string)/Panic(uint256) recognition and through Aave-owned custom-error definitions; the decoded error name and arguments appear in the returned error tuple

The V3 custom-error definitions are generated from or verified against aave-v3-origin Errors.sol, not transcribed from memory; a test fails if a definition's selector does not match the source signature
A pinned-fork failing write per protocol generation (e.g. a V3 borrow exceeding collateral capacity, a V4 Spoke borrow beyond allowance) pins the raw revert blob and its decoded form
Existing error-tuple shapes remain matchable by current consumers, or the shape change is recorded in CHANGELOG as a breaking change with the migration
PositionManager.decode_revert/1 routes through the same shared decode path instead of its module-local definitions
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Retry or error-classification policy on top of decoded reasons
Event/log decoding — its own task
onchain core changes — its decode_error surface is consumed as-is
task.body:
Today one call site decodes a revert: `Onchain.Aave.V4.PositionManager.decode_revert/1` matches two hand-defined Taker allowance errors. Every other write and simulated call returns the revert payload as an opaque rpc_error blob, so a consumer learns "execution reverted" but not why — on a money path that is the difference between a diagnosable rejection and a dead end.

STATED FACT: the deployed Aave V3 Pool (v3.7 on Ethereum Core since 2026-05-29) reverts with Solidity custom errors, not numeric string codes. aave-v3-origin `src/contracts/protocol/libraries/helpers/Errors.sol` declares 84 `error X()` definitions (e.g. `error CallerNotPoolAdmin();`), and this package's own v0.5.0 CHANGELOG already records the `InvalidInterestRateModeSelected()` revert. Aave V4 uses custom errors too.

The core ABI layer decodes the Solidity built-ins Error(string) and Panic(uint256) with no definitions supplied and accepts error definitions for custom errors. Route every Aave write/call revert path through one shared decode step whose definitions are taken from the Aave-owned Errors.sol (V3) and the V4 contract error declarations, yielding a structured reason. (2026-09-29 review) No 9036 wait: the facade `Onchain.ABI.decode_error/3` already exists (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/abi.ex:335) and keeps its name through 9036; onchain_aave already aliases `Onchain.ABI` (pool.ex:52).

AUTHORITY: the deployed contracts — pinned-fork failing writes provide the live error evidence — and aave-v3-origin / aave-v4 sources for the error definitions.

Dispatch trigger: money-path error surface with live external-system evidence.

task.title: Adopt strict ABI decoding across Aave response decode paths
acceptance_criteria: The uniform-strict vs opt-in decision is made and recorded in the affected moduledocs, and the chosen behaviour is implemented across the library's response decode paths
A hand-built non-canonical response (trailing bytes, dirty padding) surfaces as a tagged decode error from a representative read function, asserted by unit test

Live pinned-block integration reads across the V3 and V4 surfaces stay green under strict decoding, confirming deployed responses are canonical — or the finding that they are not is recorded and the approach revised
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Changing onchain core's decode surface — onchain task 88 owns that
Event and revert decoding — their own tasks
task.body:
Every byte this package decodes comes from an RPC endpoint the consumer configured but does not control, and responses from deployed Aave contracts are canonical ABI — a payload that fails strict decoding is corrupt or hostile, yet today it decodes permissively and silently.

Onchain core exposes strict decoding: `Onchain.ABI.decode_response/3` and `Onchain.Contract.call` accept `strict: true`, returning `{:error, {:decode_error, {:strict_violation, detail}}}` (task 3088). Its current implementation lives in the hand-written ABI decoder that task 9031 replaces with alloy-dyn-abi. Adopt strict decoding here after 9031, so this library turns it on once, against the implementation that will ship. (2026-09-29 review) 9036 is not a prerequisite: the `strict:` option is already public on the `Onchain.ABI` facade (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/abi.ex:24-35,141), whose name 9036 keeps.

Verify the canonicality premise against live pinned-block reads across the V3 and V4 surfaces before committing to uniform strict; record the outcome either way.

task.title: Execute the V4 Tokenization Spoke: ERC-4626 writes and the share token's ERC-20 surface
acceptance_criteria: The deployed Tokenization Spoke is confirmed against aave-v4 source (ERC20Upgradeable base, no transfer restriction, EIP-2612 permit) and the moduledoc records the confirmation with the pinned block, or records the observed deviation

deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem execute against a pinned-block mainnet fork and move both share balance and underlying balance in the direction and magnitude the matching preview_* read predicted, within the documented rounding direction
A share transfer between two accounts is exercised on the fork and both balances reflect it
Each new write is pinned by an encoded-calldata unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding, matching the existing V4 position-manager test pattern
Share-token reads and approve/transfer route through Onchain.ERC20 rather than module-local reimplementations
Missing RPC or fork prerequisites flunk with the exact export commands, never skip
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

The deposit and mint fork scenarios first approve the underlying asset to the Tokenization Spoke through Onchain.ERC20 and show the write fails without that approval; the withdraw and redeem scenarios include one call where caller ≠ owner, spending and asserting the share allowance, and one where the allowance is insufficient, pinning the deployed revert
out_of_scope: Hub-level writes and the Hub/Spoke configurators
The signed-intent *WithSig writes and depositWithPermit — record their requirements only
Off-chain APY or share-price timeseries derivation
task.body:
The Tokenization Spoke is the one V4 object other protocols can hold: an ERC-4626 share per (Hub, asset), which is what makes a V4 supply position portable into a vault, a lending market, or trading collateral elsewhere. This library can currently only look at it: lib/onchain/aave/v4/tokenization_spoke.ex wraps the ERC-4626 previews and caps, the EIP-712 typehashes and domain separator, balance_of/2 and total_supply/1, but has no deposit, mint, withdraw or redeem and no transfer, approve, allowance or permit. A consumer can compute what a deposit would mint and cannot make the deposit.

STATED FACT from source: aave/aave-v4 `src/spoke/TokenizationSpoke.sol` declares `abstract contract TokenizationSpoke is ITokenizationSpoke, ERC20Upgradeable, IntentConsumer` with no transfer or `_update` override, so the share is a standard transferable ERC-20. `ITokenizationSpoke` extends IERC4626 and IERC2612 and adds `depositWithSig`, `mintWithSig`, `withdrawWithSig`, `redeemWithSig`, `depositWithPermit`, `permit`, `usePermitNonce` and `renounceAllowance`. Confirm the deployed instances match that source before wrapping; a mismatch is a finding to record, not to paper over.

Wrap the four direct ERC-4626 writes and the share token's ERC-20 surface. Onchain.ERC20 already provides balance_of/allowance/decimals/symbol/total_supply/approve/transfer; delegate to it instead of reimplementing token calls. Record what the signed-intent (`*WithSig`) and `depositWithPermit` paths would additionally require; wrapping them is out of scope.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum Tokenization Spokes registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts and Aave-owned aave-v4 ITokenizationSpoke / TokenizationSpoke source. Fork execution at a pinned block is the evidence for every write.

Dispatch trigger: money-path write surface requiring live external-system evidence.

task.title: Wrap V4 position configuration and position-manager authorization, and close the Taker fork-evidence gap
acceptance_criteria: A user can authorize and revoke a position manager on a Spoke and toggle a reserve's collateral flag through this library's public API, without hand-encoding calldata

The Config Position Manager's on-behalf-of configuration surface is wrapped with the owner as an explicit required argument, consistent with the Giver/Taker wrappers' rule that no entrypoint infers the owner from msg.sender
withdraw, approve_withdraw and both renounce_* paths are exercised on a pinned-block mainnet fork with balance and allowance assertions, not only by calldata-shape unit tests
A withdraw attempted beyond the granted allowance fails on the fork and surfaces the tagged insufficient_withdraw_allowance tuple carrying allowance and required amount
Each new write is pinned by an encoded-calldata unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding
The raw encoded_call usages in the V4 deployed integration test are replaced by the new wrappers
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: INativeTokenGateway and ISignatureGateway
The governance surfaces: IHubConfigurator, ISpokeConfigurator, IAaveV4ConfigEngine, IAccessManagerEnumerable
Tokenization Spoke ERC-4626 writes — its own task
task.body:
V4's delegation surface is what makes a position programmable — Aave ships the three Position Managers explicitly so third-party contracts can act on a position without governance listing, gated by per-reserve allowances the user grants and can revoke. This library wraps only two thirds of it, and one gap blocks ordinary use: there is no way to enable a position manager or to toggle a reserve as collateral. IConfigPositionManager has zero coverage, and ISpoke's setUserPositionManager / setUsingAsCollateral are reachable today only by hand-encoding — the V4 deployed integration test calls them through raw encoded_call rather than through Spoke (verified 2026-08-26 by reading test/onchain/aave/v4/deployed_integration_test.exs and grepping lib/ for the interface names).

The second half of this task closes an evidence gap on a money path already shipped: of the Taker surface, supply, approve_borrow, borrow and repay are exercised on a fork at a pinned mainnet block, but withdraw, approve_withdraw and the renounce_* counterparts are pinned only by calldata-shape unit tests against an RPC stub. A selector assertion proves the call encodes; it does not prove the deployed contract moves the assets or enforces the allowance. Both halves live in the same module and the same fork test, so they are one session's work.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum V4 Spokes and Position Managers registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts, plus Aave-owned aave-v4 ISpoke / IConfigPositionManager / ITakerPositionManager source. Fork execution at a pinned block is the evidence; the existing stub tests are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: authorization and money-path write surface requiring live external-system evidence.

task.title: Decode V4 Hub, Spoke and Tokenization Spoke events from logs
acceptance_criteria: The V4 protocol events actually emitted by the deployed Hubs, Spokes and Tokenization Spokes are enumerated from Aave-owned aave-v4 source (the Hub's IHubBase declares Add, Remove, Draw, Restore, RefreshPremium, ReportDeficit and TransferShares) and each is decoded from a raw log map into a named-field map

A pinned-block integration test fetches real mainnet V4 logs via Onchain.RPC.eth_get_logs and decodes them, asserting known field values of at least one Hub Draw or Restore event, one Spoke position event and one ERC-4626 Deposit or Withdraw; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions
Topic-filter construction scopes a fetch to one Spoke or one Hub asset, and every log the filter returns decodes as the expected event
Spoke-local reserveId values in decoded events are resolvable to their underlying asset through the existing Spoke reads, and the moduledoc shows that path
Decoding shares the module and conventions task 4063 establishes for V3 rather than forking a parallel implementation
Unit tests pin decoding against log fixtures recorded from the live observations
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: V3 Pool events — task 63 owns them
Streaming via eth_subscribe, and any indexer, backfill or storage machinery
Revert decoding — task 64 owns it
task.body:
Nothing in this library can observe what V4 did. The wrappers can read current Hub and Spoke state and execute writes, but there is no way to see a supply, a borrow, a liquidation, a credit-line draw or a share mint after the fact — and V4 makes that gap worse than it was in V3, because state that used to be one Pool's is now spread across three Hubs and their Spokes, with credit lines moving liquidity between them. Point-in-time reads cannot reconstruct that movement; only the logs can.

Task 63 builds the event surface for the deployed V3 Pool and explicitly excludes V4. This task extends that work to V4 and should reuse its module, its signature-string conventions and its topic-filter construction rather than starting a second implementation. It depends on 63 landing first.

Two things are V4-specific and worth attention. Hub liquidity events have no V3 analog — Add/Remove/Draw/Restore (aave-v4 src/hub/interfaces/IHubBase.sol:23-85) are the only externally visible record of a Spoke supplying to, drawing on or restoring Hub liquidity, which is the flow that makes the Hub-and-Spoke design observable at all. (2026-09-29 review) The 9036 dependency is dropped with 4063's; this task inherits the Onchain.Log facade 4063 adds. And Spoke events carry Spoke-local reserveId rather than an asset address, so a decoded event is not self-describing: resolving an id back to its underlying is part of making the output usable.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Ethereum V4 contracts registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts and Aave-owned aave-v4 IHub / ISpoke / ITokenizationSpoke event definitions. Establish each signature and indexed layout from that source and prove decoding against real mainnet logs at pinned blocks before deriving any fixture; explorers and third-party ABIs are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: public API addition with live external-system evidence against the archive node.

task.title: Re-sync the V4 address registry with the deployed surface and stop hardcoding three Hubs
acceptance_criteria: Every AaveV4 entry the address book lists for Ethereum and for Avalanche resolves through this library's public API — Hubs, Spokes and their oracles, Tokenization Spokes, Position Managers, gateways, Treasury Spoke, configurators and the access manager

A Hub is no longer restricted to three hardcoded atoms: the fourth deployed Ethereum Hub resolves and works through the Hub read functions with no code change beyond registry data, and an unknown hub still returns the tagged unknown_hub error
networks/0 reports networks that exist in the V4 registry, not only those present in the V3 registry, and a test pins that a V4-only network would be listed

A pinned-block integration read against at least one newly registered Ethereum Hub and one Avalanche Spoke returns live data, proving the addresses are real and the Avalanche endpoint is reachable; missing RPC env vars flunk with exact export instructions
V4_SCOPING.md and CHANGELOG no longer state that V4 is Ethereum-mainnet-only, and V4_SCOPING.md records the date and address-book commit its enumeration was re-derived from
CLAUDE.md's address-verification recipe names the address book's current canonical org
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Wrapping the configurator, config-engine or access-manager interfaces — registering their addresses is enough here
Avalanche-specific write paths or a second fork-simulation target
Chainlink price-feed address space, which is separate from the Aave registry
ether.fi Cash on Optimism — DAO-licensed whitelabel, not in safe.csv; follow-on after this task (see V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md)
Base V4 lending — announced, not in the address book
task.body:
The V4 registry describes a deployment that has moved on twice, and one of the two gaps is structural rather than data.

Verified against the address book on 2026-08-26: the AaveV4Ethereum namespace has grown from 150 entries at commit 10c4e9d (2026-04-16, the snapshot V4_SCOPING.md was built from) to 304 today. That includes a fourth Hub, GLOBAL_DOLLAR_HUB at 0x62d63197660c080236193CA60b70E49A08E90368, two additional Spokes, four additional Tokenization Spokes and their interest-rate strategies. Onchain.Aave.V4.Hub types a hub as :core | :prime | :plus and resolves it through a closed case, so the fourth Hub is not merely missing from the registry — it cannot be named. Opening that up is the substance of this task; the rest is data.

Second: V4 is no longer Ethereum-only. It deployed to Avalanche (chainId 43114) on 2026-07-15 with 73 entries — one Core Hub, Main / Forex / AVAX-Correlated Spokes with their oracles, seven Tokenization Spokes, the full Position Manager set including both gateways, and a Treasury Spoke. The contract kind labels are identical to Ethereum's, so no new registry shape is needed. Both @v4_addresses and @v4_tokenization_spokes are already keyed by network, and address/2, v4_contracts/1 and v4_tokenization_spoke/3 are network-generic — adding a network is additive data. The one function that would silently omit it is networks/0, which walks only the V3 map.

Two documentation claims are now false and are load-bearing for other sessions: V4_SCOPING.md and the v0.4.0 CHANGELOG entry both state V4 is Ethereum-mainnet-only, and a task in the aave_sim repo cites that claim as its reason to exclude V4 from multi-chain work. Also note the address book repo has been transferred from the bgd-labs org to aave-dao; the raw URL in CLAUDE.md still resolves, but the recipe should name the canonical org.

Upstream also renamed some keys without changing addresses (ETHERFI_E_SPOKE became ETHERFI_ESPOKE, and price-feed keys gained a _SPOKE infix). Our atoms need not mirror upstream naming, but where they were derived from it, keep them resolvable and say which convention this registry follows.

Address book today has only AaveV4Ethereum and AaveV4Avalanche. The ether.fi Cash instance on Optimism is a DAO-licensed whitelabel and is not in safe.csv; Base V4 lending is announced, not deployed. Both are out of this task — see V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md.

AUTHORITY: the address book at aave-dao/aave-address-book (safe.csv, the AaveV4Ethereum and AaveV4Avalanche namespaces) for the address set, and a live read against the deployed contracts for proof that a registered address is the contract we think it is. Explorers, blog posts and this repo's existing V4_SCOPING.md snapshot are reference material only.

Dispatch trigger: the library's stated coverage disagrees with deployed reality on a money surface, and the fix needs live external-system evidence.

task.title: Register the unserved V4 deployments: ether.fi Cash on Optimism, plus AaveV4Base and AaveV4Arc from the address book
acceptance_criteria: For each new instance — ether.fi Cash on Optimism, AaveV4Base, AaveV4Arc — the Hubs, Spokes, Spoke oracles, Position Managers and Tokenization Spokes that actually exist resolve through this library's public API under that network key
Each new instance's Hub atoms are distinct from the Ethereum/Avalanche Hub atoms and from each other, and looking each up after registration does not return an unknown_hub error

A pinned-block integration read against one Hub per new network (Optimism Cash Hub, Base, Arc) returns {:ok, _} for at least one Hub view (member Spokes or asset count); missing RPC env vars flunk with the exact export commands, never skip

V4_DEPLOYMENTS.md records the observed Optimism addresses with the AIP/explorer/repository source and date, and the Base and Arc addresses with the safe.csv commit; it no longer lists any of the three as unregistered
The Ethereum Core Hub EtherFi Spoke (weETH e-Mode) remains a distinct lookup — registering Cash does not alias or overwrite it
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

Every AaveV4Base and AaveV4Arc safe.csv row the registry's V4 key vocabulary covers resolves through the public API to the safe.csv address, and those rows join the committed offline snapshot the registry test asserts (test/fixtures/v4_safe.csv or its successor) with the pinned commit recorded
out_of_scope: Writes through the Cash borrow-whitelist (Cash-user only)
GHO GSM on Optimism and the EtherFi card product
Aerodrome, and any V4 deployment beyond Optimism (Cash), Base and Arc
Re-syncing AaveV4Ethereum / AaveV4Avalanche — Task 69
task.body:
(2026-09-29 review) Widened to every V4 deployment the registry cannot name, because all three are the same registry shape (Hub, Spokes, Spoke oracles, Position Managers, Tokenization Spokes keyed by network in the @v4_addresses map, lib/onchain/aave/contracts.ex): aave-address-book safe.csv now carries AaveV4Base (48 rows, chainId 8453) and AaveV4Arc (50 rows, chainId 5042; e.g. HUBS CORE_HUB, SPOKES MAIN_SPOKE / FOREX_SPOKE, TOKENIZATION_SPOKES CORE_USDC / CORE_EURC), and safe.csv is the authority for those two. ether.fi Cash on Optimism stays observation-sourced as below, because safe.csv has no AaveV4Optimism namespace (0 rows, re-checked 2026-09-29).

Open decision for Optimism (default unless observation contradicts it): key this instance as network: :optimism. V3 already uses :optimism for the V3 pool; V4 lives in a separate map so that does not collide. Switch to a named instance key (e.g. :etherfi_cash) only if a second V4 deployment on Optimism is already listed in the address book or an AIP — one V4 per chain is the default.

ether.fi Cash is a live Aave V4 market that this library cannot name. It is not a Spoke on Ethereum Core Hub (that is v4_etherfi_spoke, weETH→WETH e-Mode, already registered). It is a DAO-licensed, EtherFi-operated whitelabel on OP Mainnet: one Liquidity Hub (Cash Hub), one Spoke at launch (Cash Spoke), borrow-whitelisted to Cash cardholders, isolated from every other Aave market. It went live in August 2026 (https://optimism.io/blog/etherfi-upgrades-to-aave-v4-on-op-mainnet). No consumer has asked for it yet; it tests whether the open Hub model carries a non-DAO deployment.

There is no AaveV4Optimism namespace in aave-dao/aave-address-book safe.csv (verified 2026-08-26), so the address book is not the authority here. Task 4069 opened the Hub type (`@type hub :: atom()` in lib/onchain/aave/v4/hub.ex), so registering this instance is additive registry data plus live evidence.

Do not invent addresses. Observe them from the executed AIP, the Optimism explorer, EtherFi's own aave-v4 fork (github.com/etherfi-protocol/aave-v4), and a live eth_call that proves each contract is what it claims, then register what was seen.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Optimism instance itself (eth_call at a pinned block) plus the Aave governance ARFC that authorized it (https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-deploy-a-dedicated-aave-v4-whitelabel-instance-fully-managed-by-etherfi-on-op-mainnet-to-power-ether-fi-cash/25314).

Dispatch trigger: the library's stated V4 coverage disagrees with a live deployed market, and the fix needs live evidence from a source that is not the DAO address book.

task.title: Calldata-only mode for every Aave write: build without sending
acceptance_criteria: Every existing write in Pool, V4.PositionManager, DebtToken and Faucet has a public calldata-building counterpart returning the target address and calldata (and value where applicable) with no RPC, nonce, key or signing dependency
The existing send functions route through the same builders, so the encoding exists exactly once and the send path's contract is unchanged
Each builder is pinned by a unit test asserting the 4-byte selector and argument encoding
A fork integration test via onchain_evm executes at least one built calldata (a supply) by impersonating a real holder and asserts the domain effect on balances, not the shape

A unit test in this package proves byte-equality between the package's supply and borrow builders and the calldata aave_sim's `lib/aave_sim/execution.ex` produces for the same asset, amount, on-behalf-of, rate mode and referral inputs, and pins the repay and withdraw builders against recorded reference vectors (aave_sim has no committed calldata fixtures; record the vectors as fixtures here); ERC-20 `approve` is not an onchain_aave write — aave_sim's approve maps to Onchain.ERC20, not to a builder here; the one-for-one replacement is filed as a follow-up in aave_sim's roadmap
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: New protocol operations — tasks 4058, 4060, 4066 and 4067 own those; this task changes the shape of existing writes only
Batching, atomicity or any execution rail — aave_sim's one-transaction-rail task owns that
task.body:
Every write in this library fuses encoding and sending: Pool, V4.PositionManager, DebtToken and Faucet each build calldata via Onchain.ABI.encode_call and immediately hand it to Onchain.Signer.send_transaction — no public surface returns the calldata alone (surveyed 2026-08-28 across lib/). That shape is correct for a server that holds the key and wrong for every consumer that does not: a browser wallet that signs client-side, an EIP-7702/4337 batch that composes several calls into one signed object, and a fork simulation that wants to execute the call without any key. aave_sim's execution milestone (tasks 111 and 118) shipped in the meantime with its own copies — see the 2026-09-23 note below.

Expose a public calldata-building counterpart for each existing write and re-route the send functions through it, so the encoding lives once. The builders' argument contracts mirror the existing writes — owner stays an explicit required argument everywhere the current wrappers demand it.

AUTHORITY: the deployed contracts already registered in Onchain.Aave.Contracts; the existing send-path tests define the encoding the builders must reproduce.

Dispatch trigger: money-path write-surface reshape requiring fork evidence.
(2026-09-29 review) 4058 and 4060 now depend on this task so their new writes are born builder-first instead of being reshaped afterwards.

Keep the contract minimal — a fixed small action vocabulary, no recipe DSL, no registry, no upgradeability.

The evidence lane is measured and available: onchain_evm executes undeployed runtime bytecode on forked mainnet state via code override, and the whole flash-loan round trip is one top-level call, so atomicity is provable on a fork without deploying anything.

task.title: Close the reach layer-gate holes so analytics-never-touches-the-network is enforced, not documented
acceptance_criteria: deps in .reach.exs uses mode: :allowlist with an explicit allowed: entry per declared layer (types -> [], base -> [], bindings -> [:types, :base], analytics -> [:types, :base], read -> [:types, :base, :bindings, :analytics], write -> everything below); the forbidden list is gone

mix reach.check --arch FAILS on a deliberately introduced Onchain.RPC.eth_call/3 call inside an Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.* module, and the captured failure output is pasted into the task write-up before the probe is reverted
mix reach.check --arch FAILS on a deliberately introduced alias plus call of Onchain.Aerodrome.Bindings.* inside an Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.* module (legal today, must not be)
mix reach.check --arch PASSES for a Bindings.* module that uses a Types.* struct, which the current {:bindings, :types} rule wrongly forbids
calls: [forbidden: ...] names at minimum Onchain.RPC.*, Onchain.Contract.*, Onchain.Multicall.*, Req.* and :httpc.* as unreachable from Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.* and Onchain.Aerodrome.Math*
A .reach.exs comment records that Mix.Tasks.* is intentionally outside the layer graph because the fixture generators must reach the network

CLAUDE.md's layer-contract section is corrected to describe what the gate actually enforces, its dependency table stops presenting Onchain.Solidity and Onchain.Contract.Generator as runtime-available (they live in onchain_evm, dev/test only), and AGENTS.md is regenerated so mix agents.check passes
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Writing any Analytics.* or Math.* module — the probes are temporary and reverted
Adding anything to a smells ignore list; smell findings are fixed, never ignored
Effects-policy tuning beyond recording the finding (see body)
task.body:
CLAUDE.md asserts that mix reach.check --arch fails the build when an analytics module makes an RPC call. Verify that claim before changing anything: it is false as configured, and the entire analytics-is-testable-with-zero-network guarantee rests on it.

Two concrete defects, both readable in deps/reach/lib/reach/check/architecture.ex.

First, layer_graph/2 only emits an edge when BOTH caller and callee resolve to a declared layer (module_layer(callee, layers); nil drops the edge). Onchain.RPC, Onchain.Contract, Onchain.Multicall and Req belong to no declared layer, so a direct RPC call from analytics produces zero violations.

Second, forbidden_dependency_rule_matches?({from, to}, edge) reads as layer from must not call layer to. {:analytics, :bindings} is missing from the forbidden list, so analytics may call bindings freely, which is a second network path. And {:bindings, :types} IS present, which forbids exactly the dependency the documented layer table requires; it will block every bindings task until fixed.

Convert deps to mode: :allowlist and enumerate what each layer may reach. An allowlist is exhaustive by construction, so a future layer cannot silently open a hole. Then add calls: [forbidden: ...] for the out-of-layer network modules. Reach.Config.valid_forbidden_calls?/1 accepts {caller_patterns, call_patterns} and {caller_patterns, call_patterns, except: [...]} with glob strings.

Evaluate, do not assume, whether effects: [by_layer: [analytics: [:pure, :exception]]] is usable. Reach.Effects.classify/2 falls back to :unknown for unresolvable calls and the architecture check subtracts the allowed list from function_effects/2, which includes :unknown. If :unknown floods the report, drop the effects policy and record in a .reach.exs comment why the forbidden-calls rule is the load-bearing mechanism instead. Do not ship a noisy gate.

Prove each rule by introducing the violating line, capturing the failure output, and reverting. A gate nobody has seen fail is not a gate.

OPEN DECISIONS settled 2026-08-26 (do not re-ask): (a) types is forbidden from reaching base — Types are pure structs and the table's "depends on nothing" is the allowlist; (b) Onchain.Aerodrome.Contracts and Math.* stay one `base` layer, because analytics must reach Contracts.constants() and same-layer edges are exempt.

AUTHORITY: deps/reach/lib/reach/check/architecture.ex and deps/reach/lib/reach/config.ex in this checkout are the authority on what the gate enforces. Not CLAUDE.md, not the reach README. Read the matcher functions before writing config.
