task.title: Onchain.Aerodrome.Epoch — weekly ve(3,3) epoch arithmetic
acceptance_criteria: Epoch.start/1 returns floor(ts / 604_800) * 604_800, and a stream_data property test asserts the returned instant is a Thursday 00:00:00 UTC (DateTime.from_unix!/1 plus Date.day_of_week/1 == 4) for at least 500 timestamps spanning 2020 to 2030

Epoch.epochs_per_year/0 returns the integer 52, and its @doc states that 52 * 604_800 is about 364 days and that this is the annualiser Analytics.APR uses, because annualising from a daily rate overstates by roughly 7x
start/1, end/1, next/1, previous/1, index/1, bounds/1, contains?/2, range/2 and seconds_remaining/1 are exported with @spec and doctests
Epoch.end/1 is documented as exclusive (the start of the next epoch) and a test asserts contains?(Epoch.end(ts), ts) is false — an off-by-one here silently double-counts an epoch of emissions
range(from_ts, to_ts) returns epoch starts ascending, inclusive of the epoch containing from_ts, and returns [] when to_ts precedes from_ts rather than raising
A test asserts Epoch.start(t) equals Contracts.constants().epoch_seconds * div(t, Contracts.constants().epoch_seconds) so the constant is never forked into a second literal
Negative and pre-1970 timestamps return {:error, {:timestamp_out_of_range, ts}} rather than a negative epoch index
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Any RPC read of epoch state; RewardsSugar.epochsByAddress belongs to the read layer
The LpEpoch struct, which is task 7
Timezone handling beyond UTC — Aerodrome epochs are UTC-only
task.body:
Pure weekly-epoch arithmetic for Aerodrome's ve(3,3) schedule. Epoch length is 604_800 seconds and epochs flip Thursday 00:00 UTC — not because of a hardcoded offset, but because Unix epoch 0 was itself a Thursday, so floor(ts / 604_800) * 604_800 lands on Thursday midnight with no correction term. Do not add an offset constant; if you feel the need to, your test timestamps are wrong.

The read layer will consume range/2 to build the epoch series for RewardsSugar.epochsByAddress pagination, and Analytics.APR will consume epochs_per_year/0 as its annualiser. Those two are this module's contract with the rest of the package; keep them stable and say so in the moduledoc.

This module is claimed by the analytics lane. No other module may define a second epoch helper; if a caller needs epoch boundaries, it calls here. Epoch is already declared in the base layer of .reach.exs, so it may depend on nothing but Onchain.Aerodrome.Contracts.

OPEN DECISION settled 2026-08-26 (do not re-ask): index/1 is an absolute epoch number since the Unix epoch. It is large, stable, and joins cleanly against on-chain data. Do not pin an Aerodrome genesis timestamp. Record that choice in the moduledoc.

AUTHORITY: the deployed RewardsSugar at 0x1b121EfDaF4ABb8785a315C51D29BCE0552A7678. cast call WEEK()(uint256) returned 604800 on 2026-08-26, recorded as check 6 in priv/abis/README.md. That contract, not a calendar library, defines the epoch length. If WEEK() ever disagrees with Contracts.constants().epoch_seconds, the contract wins.

task.title: Decode strategy and Bindings.Abi signature plumbing from priv/abis
acceptance_criteria: Bindings.Abi.signature/2 and Bindings.Abi.return_type/2 produce canonical Solidity type strings for every function in all nine priv/abis/*.json files, handling address, string, bool, uintN, intN, tuple, tuple[], type[] and type[N]
A test iterates every ABI file and asserts each produced call signature yields the same 4-byte selector as the one computed independently through Onchain.ABI.encode_call/2

Every ABI file consumed is declared with @external_resource and parsed once into a module attribute at compile time, not re-parsed per call; a test proves touching a priv/abis/*.json file forces recompilation
A test proves Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 never raises across a decoded golden fixture

A second test proves hieroglyph's ABI.decode/3 RAISES ArgumentError with decode_structs: true against a synthetic non-interned field name — the atom-interning hazard demonstrated, not asserted in prose

The moduledoc records the decode-strategy decision and its evidence: hex-released onchain 0.13.0 exposes Onchain.Contract.call/5 and Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 at 2-arity with no opts forwarding, so decode_structs is unreachable through the project's own wrappers; positional decode plus hand-written from_raw/1 constructors is the chosen path, matching onchain_aave precedent

CLAUDE.md, priv/abis/README.md and the README ABI paragraph stop presenting decode_structs: true as the package decode path; they record positional decode, name Sourcify's named tuple components as the input to field-order drift tests (not to decode_structs), and AGENTS.md is regenerated so mix agents.check passes
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Struct definitions, which are tasks 6 and 7
Any RPC call, which starts at task 8
The calldata encode path for writes, which is task 26
Using onchain_evm's Onchain.Solidity or Onchain.Contract.Generator — both are dev/test-only Rust NIFs, and the Generator's struct codegen only fires for sol: input, not abi_json:
task.body:
Settle the decode strategy for the whole package in one place, then build the plumbing every binding task consumes.

The reachability fact this task exists to encode: hieroglyph 1.7.0 is a runtime dependency and its ABI.decode/3 does support decode_structs: true, which returns a map keyed by snake_case atoms. But hex-released onchain 0.13.0 exposes Onchain.Contract.call/5 and Onchain.ABI.decode_response/2 at 2-arity with no opts forwarding, so decode_structs cannot be reached through the project's own wrappers. Reaching past them straight into hieroglyph would mean bypassing our own abstraction, and decode_structs additionally raises at runtime on any un-interned field atom. Verify the arities yourself in deps/onchain before building on this.

Therefore: positional decode. Onchain.RPC.eth_call plus Onchain.ABI.decode_response(return_type, hex), then a hand-written from_raw/1 per struct in tasks 6 and 7. This is the shape onchain_aave already uses in production. It sidesteps atom interning entirely, because defstruct field atoms are literal source and nothing calls String.to_existing_atom/1 on dynamic input. The residual risk is silent field-order drift on a Sugar redeploy, which tasks 6 and 7 defend with per-struct field-count and order tests read directly from the ABI JSON.

Build Bindings.Abi: given an ABI file and a function name, return the canonical call signature and the canonical return-type signature by walking inputs, outputs and components recursively with Jason. Cache per file in a module attribute with @external_resource so a re-captured ABI forces a recompile.

Write the atom-interning demonstration test. It is the standing defence against a future engineer helpfully adding decode_structs: true somewhere it will raise in production.

CLAUDE.md, priv/abis/README.md and the README ABI paragraph currently still tell implementers to intern field atoms for decode_structs: true. That is the discarded path. Correct those three files in this task so a dispatched agent loading CLAUDE.md first does not follow it. Named tuple components in the Sourcify captures remain useful — they are the input to the field-order drift tests in tasks 6 and 7, not a reason to call decode_structs. Regenerating AGENTS.md is required because mix agents.check diffs it against CLAUDE.md.

OPEN DECISIONS settled 2026-08-26 (do not re-ask): (a) there is no runtime dependency on an unreleased onchain fix — mix.exs is hex-only, no path or git deps; (b) the type-string builder covers exactly what the nine captured ABIs need, not a general Solidity grammar.

AUTHORITY: priv/abis/lp_sugar.json and the other eight captured ABIs (Sourcify v2, deployed bytecode, named tuple components) are the sole source of truth for every signature. Not velodrome-finance/sugar's README, which is proven stale — it documents all(limit, offset) while the deployed contract is all(uint256,uint256,uint256) and the two-argument form reverts.

acceptance_criteria: test/fixtures/aerodrome/manifest.json records block_number, chain_id 8453, captured_at and rpc_endpoint
Every fixture's eth_call was made with an EXPLICIT block parameter equal to manifest.block_number, never latest, proven by a test asserting every fixture file's recorded block matches the manifest
mix aerodrome.capture_fixtures --block N re-captures all fixtures; running it twice at the same block produces byte-identical files (idempotency test)

Fixtures exist for every Sugar read function across lp_sugar, rewards_sugar, ve_sugar, relay_sugar and token_sugar, at minimum: all (two or more normal pages), count, forSwaps, positions, positionsByFactory, positionsUnstakedConcentrated, tokens from both lp_sugar and token_sugar, almEstimateAmounts, epochsLatest, epochsByAddress, rewards, rewardsByAddress, forRoot, VeSugar all/byAccount/byId, RelaySugar all/registries, and TokenSugar safe_balance_of/safe_decimals/safe_symbol

One fixture is an all(500, offset, non_zero_filter) call that demonstrably returns fewer than 500 rows — the proof artifact task 8's pagination test consumes. A second short-page proof fixture captures positions (or positionsByFactory) returning fewer rows than its limit at an offset with more pools remaining past it, because the position reads walk the pool index space rather than the returned-row space and their mid-enumeration short pages need the same committed evidence
The offline decode suite loads fixtures and decodes with ZERO network calls and is NOT tagged :integration, so it runs in the default mix test.json and in mix ci
The capture Mix task lives under lib/mix/tasks/ so it resolves to no declared reach layer and may reach the network without tripping the task-1 gate
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: The per-contract Bindings.* modules, which consume these fixtures
Tick-math and liquidity goldens, which tasks 13 and 14 generate with their own manifest
Auto-remediation on drift — the detector in task 32 reports, a human re-captures
task.body:
Capture real eth_call response hex for every Sugar read function at one pinned Base block, commit it, and build the loader that tests consume. This is the package's only defence against Sugar redeploy drift once bindings land: a decode that starts returning nil or misaligned fields against these fixtures is drift, not a flaky test.

The capture tool needs a live BASE_RPC_URL (falling back to https://mainnet.base.org per the README) and is explicitly not part of mix ci — it is a dev workflow. What mix ci exercises is the committed fixtures plus the loader, with zero network.

Pin the block explicitly on every call. A fixture captured at latest is not a fixture; it is a snapshot of an unrecorded moment, and it makes every later mismatch unattributable.

Make sure at least one all(500, offset, non_zero_filter) capture returns fewer than 500 rows. That single fixture is what makes task 8's pagination-trap regression test possible, and without it that test can only assert the happy path.

AUTHORITY: live eth_call responses from the addresses in lib/onchain/aerodrome/contracts.ex, captured yourself at a block you record in the manifest. Not any remembered Sugar response shape, and not the Sourcify ABI alone — the ABI gives you the shape, not real field values to sanity-check against (for example that Lp.type really does take -1, 0 and positive values in practice).

acceptance_criteria: Onchain.Aerodrome.RPCCase in test/support exposes primary_rpc_url!/0 reading BASE_RPC_URL and falling back to https://mainnet.base.org, and secondary_rpc_url!/0 reading BASE_SECONDARY_RPC_URL with NO silent fallback, since it must be a genuinely different unprivileged provider

mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Upstreaming the seam into onchain core
A third endpoint
Retry or backoff logic beyond the retry: option Onchain.RPC already provides
task.body:
node-portability.md names this gap explicitly: no multi-endpoint test seam exists yet, and whoever builds one builds it first. Build it locally in this repo, not in onchain core, so every read and write integration test here can assert portability instead of it being a manual step that is easy to skip.

Model it on onchain core's existing single-endpoint Onchain.RPCCase but generalise to two named endpoints plus a helper that runs the same closure against both. Note that test/support is already on elixirc_paths(:test) in mix.exs, so no build config change is needed.

Never skip on a missing endpoint. A suite that reports zero failures from zero tests is a lie; flunk with the exact export command.

AUTHORITY: the public https://mainnet.base.org endpoint and a genuinely separate hosted provider of Alchemy or Infura class are the two authorities. Agreement between them, not agreement with our own archive node, is what portable means. Our node's ok result is not evidence; a hosted endpoint's real refusal is.

acceptance_criteria: Types.Lp defstruct carries every field of lp_sugar.json's all output components in ABI order — the expected field list is derived from the ABI JSON inside the drift test, never transcribed as a hardcoded count — and from_raw/1 maps a positional decode result one to one

Each struct has a drift test that reads the ABI JSON DIRECTLY in the test (not via Bindings.Abi, since the layer contract forbids types depending on bindings) and asserts the struct's field list matches the ABI components in count and order — a Sugar re-capture that adds, removes or reorders a field must fail this test rather than silently mis-decode downstream

Money fields are integers with no float anywhere; every from_raw/1 has an @spec
Every struct decodes correctly against the task-4 fixtures

out_of_scope: APR, valuation or any analytics logic
Any RPC call
The veAERO structs, which are task 7
task.body:
Define the four structs the pool and token read surface decodes into. They are one task because they share one load-bearing invariant, not because they are each small: positional decode means ABI source order is semantic, so every one of them carries the same field-count and order drift test, and one reviewer verifies that pattern once across a single coherent diff.

Do not reorder fields for readability. Under positional decode, order is the contract.

The drift test is what replaces decode_structs entirely (see task 3's decision). It is the thing that actually protects against a Sugar redeploy quietly reordering Lp's fields, and it must read the JSON itself rather than going through Bindings.Abi, because a Types.* module and its test must not depend on the bindings layer.

Types.Token is shared across two ABIs. Confirm the shapes are byte-identical with a test; if a future capture makes them diverge, that test is where it surfaces.

AUTHORITY: priv/abis/lp_sugar.json and priv/abis/token_sugar.json — specifically the outputs[0].components arrays of all, positions, forSwaps and tokens. Not velodrome-finance/sugar's struct documentation, which is exactly the source already proven stale by the all/2 versus all/3 arity mismatch.

task.title: Types.VeNFT, .Vote, .Relay, .LpEpoch and .Reward — the veAERO structs, with ABI drift tests
acceptance_criteria: Types.VeNFT carries every field of ve_sugar.json's byId output components, with votes decoded as a list of Types.Vote
Types.Vote is the {lp, weight} nested shape, defined ONCE and reused by both VeNFT and Relay; a test asserts no duplicate field-shape definition exists between the two modules

Types.Relay carries every field of relay_sugar.json's all(address) output components — the field list is derived from the ABI JSON inside the drift test, never transcribed: hand-counted totals for this struct have already been wrong more than once, and RelaySugar's function count is a different number again — with votes as [Types.Vote] and account_venfts as its own small nested type
Types.LpEpoch carries ts, lp, votes, emissions, bribes and fees, with bribes and fees decoded as lists of a shared {token, amount} nested type that is explicitly NOT conflated with Types.Reward
Types.Reward carries the flat fields venft_id, lp, amount, token, fee and bribe, drift-tested against rewards_sugar.json like the others
Each struct has a drift test reading the ABI JSON directly in the test (not via Bindings.Abi) asserting field count and order against the captured components
Every struct decodes correctly against the task-4 fixtures, including the nested tuple arrays
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Epoch boundary arithmetic, which is task 2
APR or reward accounting logic
Any RPC call
The pool and token structs, which are task 6
task.body:
Define the five structs the veAERO side decodes into. They are one task because they share the same positional-decode drift invariant and the same fixture set, and because two of them share a nested type that must be defined exactly once.

Two shape facts to get right, both verified against the captured ABIs rather than inferred. Types.Vote ({lp, weight}) is byte-identical between VeSugar's VeNFT.votes and RelaySugar's Relay.votes, so it is defined once and aliased. And Relay is materially larger than its function count suggests: a wide struct with two nested arrays, one of them ({id, amount, earned}) unique to it. Record in the moduledoc that the field list is read from the ABI JSON, so nobody re-derives it from memory or from the function count later.

LpEpoch's bribes and fees are {token, amount} pairs; Reward is a flat six-field record. They are not structurally related. Do not merge their field lists.

task.title: Bindings.LpSugar — the full read surface and the count()-driven pagination driver
acceptance_criteria: count/1 and single-page all/4 (limit, offset, filter) are implemented via Onchain.RPC.eth_call plus a Bindings.Abi-derived signature, decoding positionally into [%Types.Lp{}]

The pagination driver drives offset TO count(), never terminating on a short page; a test using the task-4 non-zero-filter fixture (which returns fewer than limit rows mid-sequence) asserts the loop CONTINUES past that short page and the final offset reached equals or exceeds count()

An explicit anti-regression test encodes the bug by name: a naive stop-when-length(page)-is-less-than-limit implementation is asserted to UNDER-COUNT against the same fixture set, so the suite fails against the bug this task exists to prevent rather than merely passing against the fix

forSwaps/3, positions/4, positionsByFactory/5, positionsUnstakedConcentrated/4, tokens/5 and almEstimateAmounts/4 are implemented, decoding into [%Types.Swap{}], [%Types.Position{}], [%Types.Token{}] and a three-element amount tuple respectively

Each of those functions carries an @doc naming which index space its offset walks and the correct termination rule. positions, positionsByFactory, positionsUnstakedConcentrated, forSwaps and tokens iterate a SCANNED index space (pool index or NFT index) that is not the returned-row space — entries are filtered, deduplicated or skipped upstream, so a page shorter than limit is normal mid-enumeration and short-page termination is the same silent-data-loss bug as on all/4; enumeration ends only when the offset has walked the full scanned space. A pagination test consumes the task-4 positions short-page fixture and asserts enumeration CONTINUES past the short page

The filter argument on all/4 is an opaque non_neg_integer passthrough with an @doc warning that its semantics are undocumented upstream and that fixture drift detection is the only available verification
Decode correctness is proven against the task-4 fixtures for every function
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: The ergonomic Sugar.Pools wrapper, which is task 23

The MAX_* cap getters and the internal wiring getters (voter, registry, convertor, cl_helper, alm_factory, alm_map, launcher_map, token_sugar, lp_helper, locker_factory_map) — Contracts.constants() carries the verified pagination caps; further caps the ABI exposes (MAX_FACTORIES, MAX_ITERATIONS) are deliberately unwired, and re-fetching any of them live adds no v0.1 value
Analytics of any kind
task.body:
This is the highest-risk read task in the package, and the risk is a silent one.

LpSugar.all/3 applies its filter argument AFTER fetching the page. With a non-zero filter a full page returns fewer than limit rows while offset still indexes the UNFILTERED space. The obvious loop-until-short-page termination is therefore not a crash but silent data loss: it stops early and reports success. Drive offset to count() unconditionally. count() answered 35,156 on 2026-08-26 and only grows, so the real shape is roughly 71 sequential pages at limit 500.

Write both tests. The positive one proves the driver reaches count(). The negative one proves a naive implementation under-counts against the short-page fixture, so the trap cannot silently return via a future refactor that looks like a simplification.

Multicall does not help the page loop. One all(500, ...) already returns about 1.1 MB and dominates the eth_call budget; Onchain.Multicall.aggregate3/2 is for per-pool enrichment. Do not parallelise pagination with it.

limit: 500 is verified working against both the public https://mainnet.base.org and an Alchemy Base endpoint, so it is not a privileged-endpoint assumption. An endpoint with a tighter per-call gas or response cap can still refuse it; document that requirement rather than silently lowering the limit.

The remaining reads land in the same module and the same diff because they share the module, the signature plumbing and the fixture set; splitting them would force a second full cycle over one file for no coupling gain.

AUTHORITY: priv/abis/lp_sugar.json's all(uint256,uint256,uint256) signature and the task-4 fixtures, specifically the one demonstrating a non-zero filter returning a short page. task.body:
The two smallest Sugar contracts, wrapped together. RelaySugar.all takes only an address and returns everything in one call. TokenSugar.tokens, though, carries the same family of pagination trap as LpSugar.all despite having no filter argument: its offset walks the pool index space while the returned rows are deduplicated tokens, so later pages are mostly dedup hits and far shorter than the limit. A short-page-terminating loop returns roughly the first page's unique tokens and reports success.

The one piece of real work beyond mechanical wiring is the cross-binding consistency proof. lp_sugar.tokens and token_sugar.tokens are byte-identical ABI shapes, so decoding the same token through both must produce identical Types.Token records. It is a cheap, high-value check that the shared-type bet holds where it actually matters, and it is the test that will fail first if a future Sugar redeploy diverges the two.

acceptance_criteria: sqrt_ratio_at_tick/1 and tick_at_sqrt_ratio/1 are exported with @spec, return {:ok, integer()} or {:error, {:tick_out_of_bounds | :sqrt_ratio_out_of_bounds, value}}, and use integer arithmetic only — a grep test asserts no float literal, no Kernel./ and no :math call appears in the module

A committed manifest test/fixtures/tick_math/sweep_manifest.json records the SlipstreamHelper address 0x9c62ab10577fB3C20A22E231b7703Ed6D456CC7a, chain id 8453, the pinned block number, the capture date, the tick set specification, and a SHA-256 digest over the FULL usable int24 domain (all 1_774_545 ticks in [-887272, 887272], concatenated 20-byte big-endian uint160 values in ascending tick order)

An offline test with no network recomputes that full-domain digest from the Elixir port and asserts equality with the committed digest; it is the swept-not-spot-checked evidence and runs inside mix ci. Measure its runtime: above 10 seconds it carries a :slow tag (still run by mix ci, never excluded) and the measured timing is recorded in the manifest and beside the tag

A committed per-tick fixture covers every multiple of 10 in the usable range — which by divisibility exhaustively covers five of the six live tick spacings 10, 50, 100, 200 and 2000 — plus every integer tick in the dense band [-10_000, 10_000] for spacing 1, so a digest mismatch localises to a specific tick rather than a shrug

A live probe confirms getSqrtRatioAtTick reverts one step outside the usable range, and the port returns {:error, {:tick_out_of_bounds, _}} for the same inputs and for the raw int24 wire bounds -8_388_608 and 8_388_607
A live probe of getSqrtRatioAtTick at the most negative usable tick succeeds and matches the fixture, proving two's-complement int24 encoding — a sign bug is invisible on positive ticks only

An inverse fixture covers, for every lattice sqrt ratio, the values r, r-1 and r+1 with the deployed getTickAtSqrtRatio answer committed for each; a stream_data property asserts round-trip identity and that perturbing down by one decrements the tick. getTickAtSqrtRatio requires MIN_SQRT_RATIO <= r < MAX_SQRT_RATIO (Uniswap v3 TickMath, which Slipstream ports), so MIN_SQRT_RATIO - 1, MAX_SQRT_RATIO and MAX_SQRT_RATIO + 1 are committed as live-probed expected reverts, the property generator excludes them, and the port returns {:error, {:sqrt_ratio_out_of_bounds, r}} for each

task.body:
Port Slipstream's TickMath to pure Elixir and prove it equals the deployed Solidity — not by spot checks, but by sweeping the domain.

The deployed helper is the oracle. SlipstreamHelper.getSqrtRatioAtTick(int24) and getTickAtSqrtRatio(uint160) are pure, so they grade our port against real deployed bytecode. Two ways to execute them are equally authoritative: plain eth_call with Multicall3 batching (roughly 1,775 aggregated calls, once), or running the helper's deployed bytecode locally in a pinned Base fork through onchain_evm, which supports Base (chain id 8453) with its OP-stack hardfork schedule and has no RPC rate limit. Pick one for the generator and record the choice and the block in the manifest.

Three tiers of evidence, each doing a job the others cannot. The full-domain SHA-256 digest is 64 committed characters, impossible to satisfy by accident, and it is what makes the word swept true. The packed lattice makes a mismatch localisable to a tick instead of a shrug. The live boundary probes catch what in-range values cannot show you: revert behaviour, and int24 sign handling.

Implementation notes that will save a day. The Solidity port relies on truncating integer division and 128-bit right shifts, all fitting inside 256 bits with no intentional overflow, so Elixir bignums are safe — but never a float, and match the division semantics to the EVM operation in play: the unsigned getSqrtRatioAtTick pipeline uses truncating division (div/2), while getTickAtSqrtRatio's signed tail shifts with sar, which is FLOOR division — floor and truncate differ by one on negative intermediates, so a blanket div/2 port is off by one on the negative side there; use arithmetic right shifts (Bitwise) or explicit floor division for those steps. getTickAtSqrtRatio computes a most-significant-bit and a log base sqrt(1.0001) with signed intermediates, which is exactly where ports break; that is why the inverse fixture perturbs each ratio by plus and minus one.

The generator lives under lib/mix/tasks/ on purpose: Mix.Tasks.* resolves to no declared layer, so it may reach the network without violating the task-5001 gate. Math.Tick itself must never call RPC, and after task 5001 lands mix reach.check --arch will refuse it.

OPEN DECISIONS to settle and report with measured numbers, not guesses: (a) fixture weight — the per-tick lattice is about 4 MB of uint160s and the full r, r-1, r+1 inverse set roughly triples that; gzip with :zlib at test time, and narrow the inverse set if the digest plus the lattice already localise every mismatch — decide and measure before generating; (b) confirm MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK from the deployed helper's own revert boundary rather than assuming Uniswap v3's values.

AUTHORITY: the deployed SlipstreamHelper at 0x9c62ab10577fB3C20A22E231b7703Ed6D456CC7a on Base, Sourcify exact_match, ABI at priv/abis/slipstream_helper.json. Its return values ARE the specification. getSqrtRatioAtTick(0) equals 79228162514264337593543950336, which is 2 to the 96th, already verified live as check 11 in priv/abis/README.md. Where our port and the helper disagree, the helper is right.
Dependency note 2026-09-23: the former dependency on 5011 (Bindings.Factories) was removed. The golden generator calls getSqrtRatioAtTick and getTickAtSqrtRatio directly through Onchain.Contract.call with priv/abis/slipstream_helper.json; the typed SlipstreamHelper bindings from 5011 are a convenience, not a prerequisite, and the math lane (5013 → 5014 → 5016) must not queue behind the bindings lane.

task.body:
The liquidity half of Slipstream's math: converting between an L value plus a price range and the token amounts backing it. Analytics.Position and every valuation function downstream depend on this being exactly right, and exactly is not rhetorical — these functions carry a round-up flag precisely because a one-wei error in the wrong direction is a solvency bug upstream.

Two traps to plan for. First, the deployed helper swaps sqrtRatioA and sqrtRatioB internally when they arrive out of order; a port that assumes A is less than B returns zeros for callers who pass upper-then-lower, and it will look like a data problem rather than a math problem. Second, getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta each have two overloads with different semantics — the uint128 plus round-up form, and the int128 signed form whose sign tracks mint against burn. Implement both. The signed form is not derivable from the unsigned one without care around negating the rounding.

Reuse task 5013's generator harness rather than writing a second one, and draw sqrt ratios from the committed tick lattice so the two fixture sets agree on the same tick domain and all six live spacings are represented.

OPEN DECISIONS to settle and document: (a) whether liquidity_for_amounts returns only the raw min of the two single-sided liquidities like the Solidity does, or additionally reports which side bound it, which is useful to a caller sizing a mint; (b) whether int128 liquidity at its boundary values is accepted or rejected — check what the deployed helper does before choosing.

AUTHORITY: the deployed SlipstreamHelper at 0x9c62ab10577fB3C20A22E231b7703Ed6D456CC7a. getAmountsForLiquidity, getLiquidityForAmounts and both getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta overloads are pure and reachable by plain eth_call. Its answers are the specification.

task.title: Math.Stable — the Solidly stable invariant and v2 constant-product quoting
acceptance_criteria: k/4 implements both invariants — x*y for volatile, and x^3*y + x*y^3 on decimals-normalised reserves for stable — dispatching on an explicit :stable or :volatile argument, never on a guessed heuristic
amount_out/6 matches the deployed pool's getAmountOut within 0 wei for at least 200 committed (pool, token_in, amount_in) fixtures spanning one real stable pool and one real volatile pool

The Newton-Raphson get_y solver is bounded at 255 iterations, matching Pool.sol's _get_y loop, and non-convergence returns {:error, {:no_convergence, 255}} where the deployed pool reverts — never a plausible-looking wrong number

marginal_price/4 returns the instantaneous price as a Decimal for both curve kinds, and a test asserts that for a stable pool the marginal price is NOT reserve1/reserve0 on a real IMBALANCED fixture — the classic Solidly stable-pool pricing bug, made to fail loudly
Decimals normalisation to 18 is applied before the invariant and reversed after, with tests covering a 6/18 pair and an 8/18 pair

Zero-reserve, single-sided and zero amount_in inputs return error tuples, never a division-by-zero crash; a positive dust amount_in for which the deployed getAmountOut returns 0 returns {:ok, 0}, matching the pool, and a fixture covers that case

A committed fixture records pool address, block number, reserves, decimals, fee, token_in, amount_in and the deployed getAmountOut answer per case; an integration-tagged test re-probes 20 of them live
Line coverage of Onchain.Aerodrome.Math.Stable is at least 95 percent

Contracts.constants() gains v2_fee_denominator 10_000, cl_fee_denominator 1_000_000 and v2_zero_fee_indicator 420, each with a provenance comment citing Pool.sol / PoolFactory.sol / LpSugar.vy and the date of the confirming live probe
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Multi-hop routing — Onchain.DEX.Router in onchain core already does it; do not reimplement
Concentrated-liquidity swap math, which is tasks 5013 and 5014
Any Bindings.Pool module — this task reads a deployed pool only inside its fixture generator
task.body:
Aerodrome's v2 side has two curves and Lp.type picks between them: 0 is stable, -1 is volatile (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy: `type: int24 = -1`, then `type = 0` when pool.stable()), and anything positive is a concentrated-liquidity tick spacing belonging to the tick-math modules. This task owns the two v2 curves.

The volatile curve is the ordinary constant product, and Onchain.DEX.Router.amount_out_v2/4 in onchain core already implements it. Use it as a cross-check, not as the implementation, because it takes fee in true basis points and Aerodrome's fee units need verifying separately.

The stable curve is Solidly's x^3*y + x*y^3, solved for the output side by Newton-Raphson on decimals-normalised reserves. Two things go wrong in every port: normalising to 18 decimals gets skipped (the invariant is not scale-invariant, so a 6-decimals token silently produces nonsense), and the iteration bound gets copied from a different fork.

The marginal-price function matters beyond quoting — it is what the price layer uses to price a token against a stable pool. Near balance, reserve1/reserve0 happens to be close to right, which is exactly why that bug survives review; it diverges precisely when the pool is imbalanced and the price is most interesting. The acceptance criterion for it is deliberately a test that would pass trivially against the naive version, so pick a fixture imbalanced enough that it does not.

ESTABLISHED FACTS, from source — record them in Contracts.constants() with a provenance comment and confirm each with one live probe; task 5019 consumes them and must not re-derive them. (a) v2 fees are basis points over 10_000: aerodrome-finance/contracts Pool.sol applies getFee(address(this), stable) / 10000; PoolFactory has stableFee = 5, volatileFee = 30, MAX_FEE = 300 and ZERO_FEE_INDICATOR = 420 (getFee maps 420 to 0). (b) Sugar's Lp.pool_fee is NOT normalised across pool types: for v2 it is PoolFactory.getFee(pool, is_stable), in basis points; for CL it is pool.fee(), in pips over 1_000_000 (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, the v2 and CL Lp builders). (c) Pool.sol's _get_y runs Newton-Raphson for at most 255 iterations and reverts when it does not converge; _k is x^3*y + x*y^3 over reserves normalised by the pool's decimals0/decimals1, which are stored as 10**token_decimals.

AUTHORITY: a deployed Aerodrome v2 pool created by PoolFactory 0x420DD381b31aEf6683db6B902084cB0FFECe40Da. Pick one stable and one volatile pool, pin a block, and grade amount_out/6 against the pool's own getAmountOut(uint256,address). The deployed pool's answer is the specification; a Solidly reference implementation on GitHub is not.

task.title: Math.Price — decimals-aware price conversion from sqrtX96, reserves and the stable invariant
acceptance_criteria: from_sqrt_ratio_x96/3 returns a Decimal for (sqrt_ratio, decimals0, decimals1), computing the square in INTEGER arithmetic before any Decimal division so no precision is lost to an intermediate Decimal square

A test asserts from_sqrt_ratio_x96 applied to Math.Tick.sqrt_ratio_at_tick(t) agrees with 1.0001^t within a relative error of max(1e-12, 4 / sqrt_ratio_at_tick(t)) — the second term is the Q64.96 quantisation bound, which dominates at negative ticks — for t in a spread including both usable-range extremes, tying the price layer to the tick oracle rather than to a second unverified constant

from_reserves/4 (volatile) and from_stable_reserves/4 (delegating to Math.Stable.marginal_price/4) both return Decimal and both normalise decimals; a test asserts the two DISAGREE on an imbalanced stable fixture
invert/1 round-trips within a declared precision, and that precision is a module attribute that is asserted, not left implicit

The module sets and documents an explicit Decimal precision of at least 28 significant digits, and a test asserts that for sqrt ratios at both usable tick extremes with (18, 6) and (6, 18) decimals the result is nonzero and its leading 28 significant digits equal an exact integer-rational computation of sqrt_ratio^2 * 10^(decimals0 - decimals1) / 2^192
A grep test asserts no float literal, no Kernel./ and no :math call appears in the module, and every public function has a doctest
Line coverage of Onchain.Aerodrome.Math.Price is at least 95 percent
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Anything touching %Lp{} — this module takes integers and decimal counts only, so it belongs in the base layer alongside Math.Tick
Routing, numeraires and USD, which are task 5017
TWAP or observation-window pricing, which needs a CL pool's observe() and therefore the network
task.body:
The shared vocabulary of the entire price layer: turning raw pool state into a Decimal price with token decimals handled correctly and exactly once.

Small module, outsized blast radius. Three consumers depend on it — Analytics.Price, Analytics.Pool and Sugar.Prices — and each would otherwise open-code the decimals adjustment, which is where token-decimals bugs live. A USDC/WETH pool priced without its 10^(6-18) correction is off by twelve orders of magnitude, which is obvious. A WBTC/WETH pool without its 10^(8-18) correction is off by ten, also obvious. A DAI/USDC pool is off by 10^12 and still looks like a number someone might believe.

Order of operations is load-bearing. Square the uint160 as an integer, then divide by 2 to the 192nd as a Decimal. Squaring a Decimal that has already been divided throws away half the significant digits. Money stays integer; only the ratio becomes Decimal.

The tick-consistency criterion exists so this module cannot drift from the tick oracle. Its tolerance must respect Q64.96 quantisation: sqrtPriceX96 is an integer, so its relative precision is about 1/sqrtRatio. At MIN_TICK sqrtRatio = 4295128739 (about 2^32), which alone gives about 2.3e-10 relative error in sqrt and about 4.7e-10 in price, so a flat 1e-12 bound is unmeetable at the negative extreme. Decimal has no integer power function; compute the 1.0001^t reference by repeated squaring at raised Decimal precision (for example 60 digits), never with :math or a float. Rather than testing against a hardcoded price table, it asserts that price-at-tick derived through our own verified sqrt_ratio_at_tick matches the mathematical definition. If task 5013's port were wrong this test would not save you, but task 5013 is graded against deployed bytecode, so the chain of authority holds.

OPEN DECISION to settle and name in the moduledoc: whether prices are canonically quoted as token1-per-token0 (the Uniswap convention, matching sqrtPriceX96 directly) or token0-per-token1. Pick one and make invert/1 the only way to get the other. A module that returns the price without saying which direction is a bug generator.

AUTHORITY: transitively, the deployed SlipstreamHelper at 0x9c62ab10577fB3C20A22E231b7703Ed6D456CC7a and a deployed Aerodrome v2 pool. This module has no on-chain counterpart of its own, so its correctness is anchored to Math.Tick, graded against that helper, plus Math.Stable, graded against a real pool. Do not introduce an independent price constant; derive everything from those two.

task.title: Types.Price and .PriceMap plus Analytics.Price — pure spot pricing and numeraire route resolution
acceptance_criteria: %Types.Price{} carries at minimum token, numeraire, value (Decimal), source (:chainlink | :cl_spot | :v2_spot | :stable_spot | :caller), route (a list of pool addresses, empty for an anchor), hops, block, updated_at, and the minimum routing depth along the route
%Types.PriceMap{} wraps a map of address to Price plus the numeraire, the block, and a list of tokens that could NOT be priced, each with a reason

Analytics.Price.spot/1 takes an %Lp{} and dispatches purely on Lp.type — 0 to the stable marginal price, -1 to constant-product (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy sets -1, then 0 when pool.stable()), positive to the sqrt ratio — and a test asserts a stable pool is NOT priced by reserve1/reserve0

Analytics.Price.resolve/3 takes [%Lp{}], a list of anchor prices and opts, returns {:ok, %PriceMap{}}, and makes ZERO RPC calls — proven both by mix reach.check --arch under the task-5001 rules and by a unit test that runs the whole resolver with the application RPC config pointed at an unroutable host

Unpriced tokens appear in PriceMap.unpriced with a reason (:below_liquidity_floor, :no_route, :hop_limit_exceeded, :zero_reserves) and are ABSENT from the price map; a test asserts fetching an unpriced token returns :error and never a zero Decimal, because a zero price silently zeroes every downstream TVL and APR denominator

Resolution is deterministic: a property test over shuffled input orderings asserts identical PriceMaps, and the documented tie-break (higher routing depth in the numeraire, then lexicographically smaller pool address) is exercised by a fixture where two pools tie on depth

The liquidity floor applies to routing depth (priced-side reserve value doubled for v2; priced-side value of the active current-slice liquidity doubled for CL), is a required documented opt with a stated default, and a test asserts that lowering it admits a token the default rejects, so the floor is demonstrably load-bearing rather than decorative
The hop limit is enforced with a default of 3, and a fixture with a four-hop-only token asserts it lands in unpriced with :hop_limit_exceeded

disagreement/2 returns the relative difference between two Price structs for the same token from different sources, and the moduledoc states plainly that single-block spot prices are manipulable and that this library does not defend against that
Line coverage of Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.Price is at least 95 percent
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

A CL fixture whose all-tick reserves clear the default floor but whose active current-tick liquidity does not is REJECTED as a routing edge, proving CL depth is measured from active liquidity and not from Lp.reserve0/reserve1
out_of_scope: Any RPC call, any Chainlink read, any Sugar page fetch — all of that is tasks 5018 and 5036; this module receives structs
TWAP or time-weighted pricing, which requires observe() and therefore the network
Cross-protocol price sources such as Uniswap on Base or off-chain APIs — Aerodrome pools plus supplied anchors only
task.body:
This is the half of the price layer that must stay network-free, and its design exists specifically to make that possible. The package ships a built-in price source; the layer contract forbids analytics from making RPC calls. The resolution is that pricing is a pure function of a pool set plus a set of anchors — tasks 5018 (anchors) and 5036 (Lp pages) fetch them, this module turns them into prices. No .reach.exs layer change is needed: Math.Price is base, Types.Price is types, Analytics.Price is analytics, and the network lives one layer up in read.

Algorithm. Seed the map with the supplied anchors, typically Chainlink USD feeds plus a stablecoin. Then relax outward by breadth-first search over the pool graph, tokens as nodes and pools as edges, at most max_hops deep. At each step traverse only a pool whose routing depth clears the liquidity floor. For a v2 pool, routing depth is the pool's reserve on its already-priced side, valued in the numeraire and doubled. For a CL pool it is NOT the reserves: Sugar's CL reserve0/reserve1 are safe_balance_of(token, pool) across all ticks (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, CL builder), so liquidity parked out of range would clear the floor while the spot price is thin. CL routing depth is the active liquidity at the current tick — the priced-side amount that Lp.liquidity (pool.liquidity()) backs over the current tick-spacing slice, via Math.Liquidity.amounts_for_liquidity/4 from task 5014 — valued and doubled. It is deliberately not Analytics.Pool.tvl/2, which refuses a pool with an unpriced side — at the moment an edge is first reached, exactly one side is priced by construction. Price each edge with spot/1, which dispatches on Lp.type. Record the route and the minimum routing depth along it in the Price struct so a caller can judge the number rather than merely consume it.

Two ways this goes wrong quietly. Pricing a stable pool by the reserve ratio is correct near balance and badly wrong when imbalanced, which is exactly when someone is looking. And returning zero for a token nobody could price is worse: a zero propagates into TVL, into an APR denominator, and out the other end as an infinite yield. PriceMap therefore has no default — unpriceable tokens are enumerated with reasons and absent from the map.

Determinism is not a nicety. If the price map depends on the order Sugar happened to return pools in, then every downstream golden is flaky and every APR regression test becomes noise. Pin the tie-break and property-test it against shuffled inputs.

OPEN DECISIONS to settle and record: (a) the default liquidity floor — sanity-check a candidate against the actual TVL distribution across the roughly 35,156 pools before writing it down as a default; (b) whether the numeraire is USD (anchored) or a stablecoin token, which differ whenever that stablecoin depegs. USD with the stablecoin treated as a priced token like any other makes a depeg visible instead of definitional.

AUTHORITY: the deployed LpSugar at 0x69dD9db6d8f8E7d83887A704f447b1a584b599A1 defines the Lp struct this module consumes; the named fields in priv/abis/lp_sugar.json are the contract, and Lp.type is the discriminator. Fixtures must be real captured pages from that contract at a pinned block, not hand-written structs.

task.title: Bindings.Chainlink — verified Base anchor feeds with a sequencer-aware staleness policy
acceptance_criteria: Bindings.Chainlink latest_round_data/2, decimals/2 and description/2 wrap AggregatorV3Interface against a feed address, with the ABI captured into priv/abis/chainlink_aggregator_v3.json and its provenance recorded in priv/abis/README.md in the same table shape as the existing entries

Every feed address added to Contracts, including the sequencer uptime feed 0xBCF85224fc0756B9Fa45aA7892530B47e10b6433, is verified by a live call (description() for price feeds, latestRoundData() for the uptime feed) and the verified description, decimals and documented heartbeat are recorded as a comment beside it. No address is added from memory or from a single explorer label

The staleness policy returns a tagged error rather than a number for: a round older than max_staleness_s (defaulting to twice the feed's recorded heartbeat), a non-positive answer, the sequencer uptime feed reporting down, and a read within the documented grace period after the sequencer's last restart. A unit test drives each rejection path with synthetic round tuples
answeredInRound is not used as a validity check, and the moduledoc states that it is deprecated on OCR feeds
The moduledoc states which calls require archive access (any pinned-block query) and which do not, per the node-portability law
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Price arithmetic and PriceMap materialisation — task 5036 and Analytics.Price

Tokenized-equity Chainlink feeds (Coinbase B20 stocks: 24/5 publishing, frozen updatedAt off-hours, Total Return Value units — see docs/protocol-context.md); file via rmap new when a consumer needs equity anchors
Caching, GenServers or any long-lived process — this is a request-scoped read
Optimism or Velodrome feed addresses; Base only
Upstreaming the AggregatorV3 binding into onchain core — it lives here until a second family consumer exists, and that move is a decision to make then
task.body:
Chainlink aggregators on Base give USD anchors for the major assets; the Aerodrome pool graph routes everything else to them (task 5036 materialises the PriceMap). This task is the anchor source alone: the AggregatorV3 binding, the verified feed registry, and the policy that decides whether an anchor may be used at all.

Chainlink has no FeedRegistry on Base, so feed addresses are hardcoded, which makes verification the whole game. Every aggregator exposes description(); call it and assert the pair. Read decimals() from the contract — feeds are not uniformly 8.

Staleness produces a confident wrong answer: latestRoundData returns a six-hour-old price during an outage and every APR built on it looks normal. Reject rather than report. On an L2 there is a second outage mode the heartbeat check cannot see: when the Base sequencer is down, feeds stop updating and prices resume from a stale state after restart. Chainlink recommends gating every L2 read on the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed; on Base it is 0xBCF85224fc0756B9Fa45aA7892530B47e10b6433 (docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds). Its answer is 0 when the sequencer is up and 1 when down, and startedAt is when the status last changed; reads within a grace period after a restart are rejected too. answeredInRound is deprecated on OCR feeds (it always equals roundId), so it is not a validity check.

This task edits lib/onchain/aerodrome/contracts.ex, which tasks 5019 and 5025 also edit. A feed lookup returning a map with address, description, decimals and heartbeat_s, rather than a bare address, gives the policy data to work with.

OPEN DECISION to settle and record: which feeds ship — an ETH and a USDC feed are the minimum for a USD numeraire; check whether an AERO/USD feed exists on Base, since it lets emission APR be USD-denominated without routing.

AUTHORITY: the deployed AggregatorV3 feeds and the sequencer uptime feed on Base. Each feed grades its own address through description(), decimals() and a live latestRoundData(). Cross-check against Chainlink's published Base feed list; an explorer label alone is never sufficient, per this repo's address-verification rule.

task.title: Analytics.Pool — pool typing, TVL, staked share and verified fee-unit semantics
acceptance_criteria: pool_type/1 returns :v2_stable for Lp.type 0, :v2_volatile for -1 (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy v2 builder: type = -1, then 0 when pool.stable()) and {:cl, spacing} for any positive value, and a test asserts every value in Contracts.constants().tick_spacings maps to a {:cl, _} result

tvl/2 takes an %Lp{} plus a %PriceMap{} and returns {:ok, Decimal.t()} from reserve0/reserve1, or {:error, {:unpriced_token, addr}} when either side is unpriced — NEVER a partial TVL counting only the priced side; for CL pools the moduledoc labels it as all-ticks reserves

staked_tvl/2 returns the v2 pro-rata staked value computed from reserve0/reserve1 * gauge_liquidity / liquidity — NEVER from staked0/staked1, which Sugar zeroes once emissions lapse — and a fixture with a live gauge, nonzero gauge_liquidity and lapsed emissions (Lp.emissions 0, staked0 0) asserts a nonzero staked TVL; for a CL pool it returns {:error, {:not_a_tvl, :cl_current_tick_slice}}, and a separate staked_slice_value/2 values CL staked0/staked1 under a name and @doc that say they cover only Sugar's tick-spacing slice, including its truncation-toward-zero tick_low; a real captured CL row with a negative tick that is not a multiple of its spacing asserts the slice lies above the current tick and staked1 is 0

staked_fraction/1 returns gauge_liquidity / liquidity as a Decimal in the closed unit interval for both pool types, price-free, and returns {:error, :zero_liquidity} for an empty pool rather than a NaN or a zero; a test asserts it is NOT computed from staked0/staked1 over reserves for a CL fixture

unstaked_fee_rate/1 returns Lp.unstaked_fee over 1_000_000 as a Decimal, a test asserts the default 100_000 pips maps to exactly 0.10, and the moduledoc states that an unstaked concentrated-liquidity LP keeps one minus that rate of trading fees with the remainder going to the gauge

fee_rate/1 dispatches on pool_type/1 — v2 pool_fee over 10_000, CL pool_fee over 1_000_000, both divisors read from Contracts.constants() — and a test asserts fee_rate for one real v2 pool and one real CL pool against the fee read from the corresponding deployed factory at the fixture's pinned block
Every function is pure: mix reach.check --arch passes under the task-5001 rules, and no function in this module accepts an rpc_url or block option
Golden fixtures are real captured LpSugar.all rows at a pinned block covering at minimum one stable pool, one volatile pool, one CL pool with a live gauge and one CL pool with gauge_alive false
Line coverage of Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.Pool is at least 95 percent
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

A real captured stable pool row (pool.stable() true, confirmed by a live probe recorded in the fixture manifest) decodes to Lp.type 0 and pool_type/1 :v2_stable, and a real volatile row decodes to -1 and :v2_volatile — the repo docs carried this inverted until 2026-09-29, so the captured fixture, not a doc, is the evidence
out_of_scope: APR of any kind, which is task 5021
Position-level valuation, which is task 5020
Liquidity depth and tick distribution, which needs getPopulatedTicks and therefore the network
Impermanent loss, which needs an entry price no struct here carries
task.body:
Pool-level valuation over an %Lp{} and a %PriceMap{}.

Fee units are settled (task 5015 records them in Contracts.constants(); consume them, do not re-derive): Sugar's Lp.pool_fee is PoolFactory.getFee(pool, is_stable) for v2 pools — basis points over 10_000 — and pool.fee() for CL pools — pips over 1_000_000 (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, v2 and CL Lp builders; aerodrome-finance/contracts Pool.sol divides by 10000). fee_rate/1 must dispatch on pool_type/1; a single shared divisor is a bug. Lp.unstaked_fee is pool.unstakedFee(), also in pips.

Staked semantics differ by pool type, and that is the trap in this module. For v2, Sugar sets staked0/staked1 = reserve * gauge.totalSupply() // pool.totalSupply() ONLY inside `if gauge_alive and gauge.periodFinish() > block.timestamp` (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, v2 builder, around L577-582); once emissions lapse they are 0 even though LP tokens are still staked. The v2 staked TVL is therefore derived here from reserve0/reserve1 * gauge_liquidity / liquidity (both set unconditionally in that builder), never from staked0/staked1. For CL, staked0/staked1 are getAmountsForLiquidity(sqrtPriceX96, tick_low, tick_low + spacing, stakedLiquidity) with tick_low = (tick // spacing) * spacing (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, CL builder, around L1185). Vyper's // on signed integers truncates toward zero, not floor (docs.vyperlang.org/en/stable/types.html): for a negative tick that is not a multiple of spacing, Sugar's slice is the one ABOVE the current tick and excludes it, so staked0/staked1 come out entirely in token0. They are the token amounts of active staked liquidity inside that tick-spacing slice only. They are not a staked TVL and must never be divided by reserves. The price-free staked share works for both types: Lp.liquidity is pool.totalSupply() for v2 and active pool.liquidity() for CL, and Lp.gauge_liquidity is gauge.totalSupply() for v2 and pool.stakedLiquidity() for CL, so gauge_liquidity / liquidity is the staked fraction of LP tokens (v2) or of active in-range liquidity (CL).

The TVL functions have a smaller trap: a pool where only one token is priced. Returning the priced side's value as TVL halves the number and nothing complains. Return an error.

TVL for a CL pool is reserve0/reserve1, which spans all ticks — the Lp struct has no in-range total — and it must be labelled as such because CL fee yield accrues only to in-range liquidity.

This task edits contracts.ex only if a constant 5015 recorded is missing; coordinate with 5018 and 5025, which also edit it.

AUTHORITY: the deployed LpSugar at 0x69dD9db6d8f8E7d83887A704f447b1a584b599A1 for Lp field semantics (its Vyper source is the definition), the deployed CLFactory at 0x5e7BB104d84c7CB9B682AaC2F3d509f5F406809A and PoolFactory at 0x420DD381b31aEf6683db6B902084cB0FFECe40Da for fee values at a pinned block.

task.title: Analytics.Position — principal, range state and valuation, cross-graded against Sugar's own amounts
acceptance_criteria: principal/2 takes a CL %Position{} plus a current sqrt ratio and returns integer token0 and token1 amounts for liquidity + staked via Math.Liquidity.amounts_for_liquidity/4 using the position's own sqrt_ratio_lower and sqrt_ratio_upper; principal_v2/2 takes a v2 %Position{} plus its %Lp{} and returns the LP share of reserves; calling principal/2 on a v2 row returns {:error, :v2_position}, never zeros

A test asserts that for at least 50 real captured positions, including at least 10 staked and 10 unstaked CL positions and at least 5 v2 positions, the computed principal reproduces amount0 + staked0 and amount1 + staked1 EXACTLY, with the Lp page captured at the same block
An integration-tagged differential calls the deployed SlipstreamHelper.principal(nfpm, token_id, sqrt_ratio_x96) for 20 real position ids at a pinned block and asserts the pure result matches
in_range?/2 returns true exactly when tick_lower is at most lp.tick and lp.tick is strictly below tick_upper, with explicit tests at BOTH boundaries

value/3 returns position value in the numeraire from principal plus a PriceMap; unclaimed/3 values unstaked_earned0, unstaked_earned1 and emissions_earned SEPARATELY, returning a map with those three keys and never a single summed figure

staked_fraction/1 returns staked / (liquidity + staked); a test asserts that every staked CL fixture row has liquidity 0 and every unstaked one has staked 0, and the moduledoc states the all-or-nothing CL rule and the partial v2 rule with the LpSugar.vy source
Positions with zero liquidity and positions whose range lies entirely on one side of the current tick return correct single-sided or zero results rather than errors, with a fixture for each
All functions are pure: mix reach.check --arch passes and no function accepts an rpc_url
Line coverage of Onchain.Aerodrome.Analytics.Position is at least 95 percent
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Impermanent loss or PnL against an entry price — the Position struct carries no entry data and inventing one would be fabrication
Fee-growth accounting from tick data, which needs pool state beyond the struct
ALM and locker position semantics beyond exposing the alm and locker fields verbatim
Position APR, which is task 5021
task.body:
Position-level math over the 18-field %Position{} Sugar returns. Its oracle is nearly free: Sugar computes the position's token amounts on-chain from the same liquidity and range our principal uses, so a captured positions page is both input and expected output.

Sugar's position semantics are established from source (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy) and must be modelled, not rediscovered. CL: amount0/amount1 come from SlipstreamHelper.principal(nfpm, id, slot0.sqrtPriceX96) and liquidity from the NFPM; when the NFT is staked in the gauge, Sugar moves everything across — staked = liquidity, staked0/staked1 = amount0/amount1, then amount0 = amount1 = liquidity = 0. A CL position is therefore all-or-nothing staked per NFT. A differential that compares principal(liquidity) against amount0 alone passes vacuously on every staked position (0 = 0); compare liquidity + staked against amount + staked instead. v2: liquidity is the account's unstaked LP-token balance and staked its gauge balance, so partial staking exists; amount0 = liquidity * reserve0 / pool.totalSupply() and staked0 likewise from staked — v2 principal is an LP share of reserves and needs the %Lp{} (reserves, and Lp.liquidity = totalSupply), not ticks.

The range-inclusion convention: pools treat the lower tick as inclusive and the upper as exclusive, so a position exactly at its upper tick is out of range. Test both edges.

unclaimed/3 returns a map, not a total: emissions_earned is denominated in the emissions token and the earned fees in the pool's two tokens. Summing requires prices and a stated numeraire; the caller does that deliberately with the PriceMap.

The committed nonempty positions fixture holds about one position, so capturing a real page of at least 50 — staked and unstaked, CL and v2 — at the same block as the Lp rows it is priced against is part of this task; extend the existing capture task rather than writing a new one.

task.title: Analytics.APR — separate fee and emission rates, each carrying its denominator as data
acceptance_criteria: The return type is %Analytics.APR.Rate{} carrying at minimum kind (:fee or :emission), rate (Decimal), basis (an atom naming the denominator), numerator (with amount, unit, period and epochs_per_year 52), denominator (with amount, unit and label), and inputs recording the exact Lp, LpEpoch and price entries used. A bare Decimal is never returned from any APR function
Rate.combine/2 raises Analytics.APR.IncomparableBasisError whenever the two rates' basis values differ, and it is the ONLY combining function in the module's public API

Emission APR is computed from Lp.emissions * 604_800, annualised by Epoch.epochs_per_year/0; a regression test asserts the rate is NOT the weekly-treated-as-daily variant (weekly * 365), and a comment records that per-day * 365 versus weekly * 52 differ by only 0.27% and is not the error being pinned
emissions_cap is ALWAYS recorded in Rate.inputs and NEVER applied as a token-amount minimum; a grep test asserts no min() of a weekly emission against emissions_cap exists in the module

gauge_alive false yields {:unavailable, :gauge_not_alive}; a zero gauge address yields {:unavailable, :no_gauge}; Lp.emissions 0 on a live gauge yields {:unavailable, :no_active_emissions}; a zero denominator yields {:unavailable, :no_staked_liquidity}. None of these is a zero rate

Emission APR supports two bases and records which was used: price-free (weekly emissions over gauge_liquidity), exercised by a test with an EMPTY PriceMap; and USD, whose basis atom is distinct for v2 (staked TVL) and CL (current tick slice) — a test asserts a CL rate never carries the v2 basis, and the CL USD basis @doc states Sugar's truncation-toward-zero slice bounds

The v2 fee Rate takes a completed-epoch %LpEpoch{} (its ts is before the current epoch start; an in-progress epoch returns {:error, :epoch_in_progress}) and divides its fees, valued through the PriceMap, by the staked TVL from Analytics.Pool.staked_tvl/2 (reserves * gauge_liquidity / liquidity, never Lp.staked0/staked1); its basis records that, a test asserts the denominator is NOT total reserves, and a fixture with lapsed emissions (staked0 0, gauge_liquidity nonzero) still yields a fee Rate rather than {:unavailable, :no_staked_liquidity}

fee_apr for a CL pool returns {:unavailable, :cl_fee_flow_not_separable}, and the moduledoc states in one sentence why (LpEpoch.fees mixes staked in-range fees with the unstaked rake); Lp.token0_fees/token1_fees appear only in Rate.inputs, never as a flow
No function returns or accepts a float — a grep test enforces it — and all money stays integer until the final Decimal ratio

task.body:
This is the module most likely to be silently wrong, because a wrong APR is still a plausible-looking number. The brief is not compute an APR but make it impossible to report one without its denominator.

The invariant: fee APR and emission APR are emitted separately, each tagged with its explicit denominator, and never summed. Neither function returns a number. Both return a %Rate{} carrying the rate, the basis, the numerator with its period and annualiser, the denominator with its unit, and the exact inputs used. The only combining function refuses mismatched bases. (2026-09-29 review) This task absorbs superseded task 5022: the banned-name manifest test and the synthetic 7.53 percent golden are acceptance criteria here; the live-captured golden moved to task 5033. The harness reviewer is the independent grader.

Facts established from source (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy and RewardsSugar.vy), each of which a formula must respect:

Emissions. Lp.emissions is gauge.rewardRate(), per second, and Sugar sets it to 0 whenever gauge.periodFinish() is not in the future — even for a live gauge. Zero emissions on a live gauge is therefore 'no active emissions', not a zero rate. Weekly = emissions * 604_800; annualise with Epoch.epochs_per_year/0 = 52. Annualising a correctly computed per-day figure by 365 differs from the weekly * 52 figure by only 0.27% (31,536,000 s against 31,449,600 s) and is not an error class; the real 7x error is treating a weekly amount as a daily one and multiplying by 365.

Emission denominators. The price-free basis is weekly emissions (emissions-token units) over gauge_liquidity — for v2 the gauge's LP-token supply, for CL pool.stakedLiquidity(), the active staked liquidity. The USD basis differs by pool type: for v2, the staked TVL is reserve0/reserve1 * gauge_liquidity / liquidity, as Analytics.Pool.staked_tvl/2 (task 5019) computes it — NOT Lp.staked0/staked1, which Sugar sets only while gauge.periodFinish() > block.timestamp (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, v2 builder, around L577-582) and leaves 0 once emissions lapse; for CL, staked0/staked1 are the amounts of active staked liquidity in one tick-spacing slice only, [tick_low, tick_low + spacing), where Sugar computes tick_low with Vyper's truncating // (velodrome-finance/sugar contracts/LpSugar.vy, CL builder, around L1185; docs.vyperlang.org/en/stable/types.html), so for a negative tick off the spacing grid the slice lies above the current tick and holds only token0. A CL USD emission rate is per unit of value in that slice, and its basis atom must say so (for example :usd_staked_current_tick_slice).

emissions_cap is not a bound to apply. Where gauge factories expose a cap it is a relative share in basis points of MAX_BPS(), several gauge factories revert on the cap selectors (Sugar's _safe_emissions_cap then yields 0), and Lp.emissions is the post-notification rate the cap has already shaped. Record it in Rate.inputs; never subtract it or min() it against the weekly rate.

Fees. LpEpoch.fees is the FeesVotingReward amount credited to an epoch: VOTER revenue. On Aerodrome, staked LPs forfeit trading fees to voters, and CL unstaked positions pay Lp.unstaked_fee into the same reward. epochsLatest returns the current, in-progress epoch (epoch_start_ts = block.timestamp // WEEK * WEEK), so its fees are partial. Lp.token0_fees/token1_fees are accrued balances (v2: claimable scaled by supply; CL: pool.gaugeFees()) over an unknown window and are not a flow. Consequences: the v2 fee Rate uses a COMPLETED epoch's LpEpoch.fees (via epochsByAddress) over the staked TVL — the fee flow of the staked share divided by the staked share's value, which estimates the per-unit fee yield of the pool; dividing it by total reserves understates by the staked fraction. For CL the voter fee flow mixes staked in-range fees with the unstaked rake and cannot be separated from Sugar data, so no CL fee Rate is produced in this task.

(2026-09-29 review) Which LP class earns the v2 fee flow — PREMISE UNVERIFIED, confirm against aerodrome-finance/contracts Pool.sol and Gauge.sol before building on it. The reading above is that LP tokens staked in the gauge forfeit their trading fees (the gauge claims them into the FeesVotingReward), so LpEpoch.fees is the fee flow of the staked share, while unstaked LPs keep theirs through Pool.claimable0/claimable1. If that holds, the v2 fee Rate is the per-unit yield an UNSTAKED LP earns (and a staked LP gives up), and its basis atom and @doc say so rather than implying staked LPs receive it. If the source says otherwise, stop and file the correction instead of building on this paragraph.

Dead gauges return an unavailable tuple, not zero. Zero averages, charts and ranks; a tagged tuple forces a decision.

AUTHORITY: the deployed LpSugar at 0x69dD9db6d8f8E7d83887A704f447b1a584b599A1 and RewardsSugar at 0x1b121EfDaF4ABb8785a315C51D29BCE0552A7678 (their Vyper sources define the fields), RewardsSugar.WEEK() = 604800, and the deployed Voter at 0x16613524e02ad97eDfeF371bC883F2F5d6C480A5 for gauge liveness. task.body:
The consumer-facing pool and token read API — the most visible surface in the package, and the one an agent or a human actually calls.

The one thing this layer must not do is quietly reintroduce the pagination trap while simplifying the call. Re-prove the invariant here with its own test against the short-page fixture; do not trust the binding-level test in task 5008 to cover a rewrite that happens in this file.

Tokens ride along with pools rather than getting their own dispatch: they share the fixture set, the option conventions and the error shape, and a reviewer verifies both in one pass over one diff.

task.body:
The four account-scoped ergonomic wrappers, landed as one dispatch. Each is a thin delegation over a binding built in phase 3; pagination and termination semantics stay in the bindings, which own the offset-walks-a-different-index-space rules, and this layer must not reimplement any loop. Splitting them into four dispatches would spend four implement, review and land cycles on work a reviewer verifies in one glance.

The one substantive obligation is naming discipline in Sugar.Rewards. RewardsSugar.rewardsByAddress is veNFT-scoped, taking a veNFT id and a pool, not an account. Preserve that in the wrapper's name and @doc. This is the ground-truth correction most likely to be quietly fixed into an account-scoping assumption by a future refactor if the naming here is ambiguous.

task.body:
Capture the ABIs and verify the addresses for the three contract families the write surface needs and that are absent from this repo: the Aerodrome Router (swaps and v2 liquidity), the Slipstream NonfungiblePositionManagers (CL position lifecycle), and the Gauge contracts (stake, unstake, claim).

Follow the Sourcify v2 capture protocol in priv/abis/README.md exactly, and flag any null or partial Sourcify match rather than smoothing it over.

Two facts shape the address work. First, the Sugar team's deployments/base.env lists VOTER, REGISTRY, SLIPSTREAM_HELPER, the V2 and CL factories, launchers, SWAPPER and the Sugar contracts — it has NO Router and NO NFPM entry, so it cannot be one of the two sources for them. The Router's sources are the aerodrome-finance/contracts deployment list and a live probe (Router.defaultFactory() must return PoolFactory 0x420DD381b31aEf6683db6B902084cB0FFECe40Da, Router.voter() the Voter). Second, the NFPM is per CL factory, not global: LpSugar resolves it with lp_helper.fetch_nfpm(factory), and every Lp row carries its own nfpm. There are three CL factories (CL_FACTORIES_8453), so there can be up to three NFPMs, and a single :nfpm key is the wrong model. Resolve each factory's NFPM, confirm it against Lp.nfpm on a live row from that factory, and probe NFPM.factory() back to it.

Gauges come in two shapes: the v2 Gauge stakes an LP-token amount, the Slipstream CLGauge stakes an NFPM token id. Capture a representative of each through a live Lp.gauge read, and check whether CL gauges from different CL factories share one selector set.

Every downstream write task inherits these addresses. A wrong one does not fail loudly; it produces calldata aimed at the wrong contract.

task.title: Golden-calldata evidence harness: an independent cast oracle plus eth_call impersonation, proven on Voter
acceptance_criteria: A CalldataFixture test helper shells out to the local Foundry cast binary to produce REFERENCE calldata for a given signature and arguments, and that reference — never our own Onchain.ABI.encode_call/2 output — is what assertions compare against
If cast is not on PATH the test FLUNKS, never skips, naming the exact install command

A second helper performs eth_call-as-impersonation: it sets the JSON-RPC from field to a real address discovered through a Sugar read, obtaining a genuine simulated return value or revert reason from the deployed contract without that address's private key and without broadcasting anything

A demonstration test against Voter reset(uint256) — whose ABI is already captured, so this task does not depend on task 25 — proves the golden assertion byte-exact against cast calldata output, AND a negative-control eth_call against the deployed Voter with a veNFT id the impersonated address does not own returns a real, SPECIFIC on-chain revert rather than a generic execution-reverted string

The helper's @doc states in one paragraph what this evidence model CANNOT prove — that a state-mutating call actually succeeds and commits on-chain — and why: Base simulation is blocked and broadcasting a real transaction is out of scope for a test suite
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Router, Gauge and NFPM specific tests, which land with each contract's write task reusing this harness
Signing or broadcasting any transaction
eth_call state-override tricks, which are non-portable per node-portability rule 1 and explicitly not used here
task.body:
This is the shared piece every write task depends on, and it must exist before those tasks write a single test that grades our encoder against our encoder — which is a false green, not weak evidence.

Build two things.

First, an independent encoder oracle. Shell out to Foundry's cast to encode the same call the library encodes, and assert byte-for-byte equality. cast is a different codebase in a different language implementing the same ABI specification, which is what makes it an oracle rather than a mirror.

Second, eth_call impersonation. The from parameter of eth_call lets you simulate a call as if any address sent it, without owning that address's key and without broadcasting, because eth_call never mutates state or requires a valid signature. Use it for real positive evidence (a decoded return from a state-mutating function's simulated execution) or real negative evidence (a specific revert from crafted bad inputs) straight from the deployed bytecode.

Prove the whole harness end to end against Voter.reset(uint256), whose ABI is already captured, so this task is not blocked on task 25.

Be honest in the docs about the ceiling. With Base simulation blocked, no test here can prove a write succeeds and commits. Say so, once, plainly, rather than letting a reader infer more from a green suite than it can support.

AUTHORITY: Foundry's cast, independently implementing ABI encoding, is the oracle for calldata-shape correctness. The deployed Voter at 0x16613524e02ad97eDfeF371bC883F2F5d6C480A5, verified in priv/abis/README.md on 2026-08-26, is the oracle for on-chain revert semantics. Neither is this repo's own encoder.

Build the write surface for the already-captured Voter contract. This is deliberately the first write module, because its ABI provenance is already settled — priv/abis/README.md carries its row and its live probe — so it does not wait on task 5025 and it validates the task-5026 harness against a real contract early.

Low risk on provenance does not mean low stakes. Misdirected votes cost a whole epoch of emission weighting, and vote takes parallel arrays whose length mismatch is exactly the kind of caller bug worth catching before it becomes an on-chain revert someone paid gas for. Check it locally, and still test that the contract rejects it too.

Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

task.body:
The Router write surface: swaps and v2 liquidity provision, in one module and one dispatch because they share a file and a deadline discipline, and separating them would sequence two full cycles over one file.

Swap calldata is the easiest write to get subtly wrong — route ordering, and the stable flag on each hop — and the failure mode is that a caller trusts calldata encoding the wrong route. The stable boolean deserves the sharpest test in this task: it selects between two entirely different deployed pools for the same token pair, mirroring the Lp.type discriminator, so wrong flag equals wrong pool. Assert it against real deployed addresses, not against our own routing logic.

Every function takes a deadline. Treat never-a-stale-deadline as a domain invariant worth an explicit negative control rather than something exercised incidentally.

This module does not compute expected amounts or a fair slippage minimum. It takes caller-supplied minimums as-is and says so in the @doc, so nobody mistakes it for a safety layer it is not.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Router at the address task 5025 verifies — specifically its revert behaviour on a crafted expired-deadline eth_call and on a slippage-minimum breach — grades this task. Not our own encoder, and not the Solidly or Velodrome reference implementation source, which is reference material only.

acceptance_criteria: mint, increaseLiquidity, decreaseLiquidity and collect all return calldata by default with the same Signer opt-in contract; a grep test asserts no System.get_env call reads anything key-shaped

mint's tick arguments are checked locally before encoding — tick_lower < tick_upper, both within [-887272, 887272] and both multiples of the MintParams tickSpacing — and the @doc states that this is a courtesy to save wasted gas and NEVER a substitute for the contract's own enforcement; membership in Contracts.constants().tick_spacings is not the check, since that list comes from the primary CL factory only
