Replacing aave_sim's copy is filed as a follow-up in aave_sim's roadmap
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: MetaMorpho / Morpho Vaults, rewards, the public allocator
Writes of any kind
Editing aave_sim — the adoption is its own follow-up there
task.body:
aave_sim task 114 is done: it manages a Morpho Blue position end to end with its own reads in `lib/aave_sim/protocols/morpho_blue.ex` and `lib/aave_sim/protocols/morpho_blue/{market,shares,contracts,history}.ex`. That code is the consumer and the starting point for the raw reads. This task moves the protocol-level read layer into a new package, onchain_morpho, and makes aave_sim able to delete its copy.

(2026-09-29 review) Only part of this is an extraction. aave_sim has the raw reads (market, position, idToMarketParams, oracle, and a 20-line shares.ex with to_assets_down only). It has no interest accrual: no borrowRateView call and no Taylor compounding anywhere in lib/aave_sim/protocols/morpho_blue*. Accrued-to-now balances are new work. Their oracle is Morpho's own view math in morpho-blue src/libraries/periphery/MorphoBalancesLib.sol (expectedMarketBalances / expectedBorrowAssets / expectedSupplyAssets): interest = totalBorrowAssets.wMulDown(borrowRate.wTaylorCompounded(elapsed)); the fee split feeShares = (interest.wMulDown(fee)).toSharesDown(totalSupplyAssets - feeAmount, totalSupplyShares); borrow shares convert with toAssetsUp and supply shares with toAssetsDown, over SharesMathLib's VIRTUAL_SHARES = 1e6 and VIRTUAL_ASSETS = 1. A live cross-check is available through onchain_evm (dev/test only): simulate_batch of accrueInterest(marketParams) followed by market(id) on a fork must equal the computed accrual at that block.

The protocol choice was verified against live data on 2026-08-28: DeFiLlama puts Morpho at roughly $9.5B TVL, about double Spark, deployed on Ethereum mainnet and Base, where it is the largest lending protocol on any L2. Its market model is isolated markets with one collateral asset, one loan asset and a fixed LLTV each.

Morpho Blue surface, from the morpho-blue repository and docs.morpho.org: the singleton exposes `idToMarketParams(id)` → (loanToken, collateralToken, oracle, irm, lltv), `market(id)` → (totalSupplyAssets, totalSupplyShares, totalBorrowAssets, totalBorrowShares, lastUpdate, fee) and `position(id, user)` → (supplyShares, borrowShares, collateral). State accrues only on interaction, so current borrow assets require the IRM's `borrowRateView(marketParams, market)` and Morpho's Taylor-expansion compounding over the time since `lastUpdate`, then share-to-asset conversion with Morpho's rounding. Oracle `price()` is scaled by ORACLE_PRICE_SCALE = 1e36 adjusted for token decimals. Take formulas and rounding from Morpho's contracts, not from the Aave shape or from memory.

This runs after 9036 so the new package is founded on the final onchain 0.16 Onchain.* API. Package count after 9029 is seven; this is the eighth, and its task ids keep the 9001 id already assigned.

AUTHORITY: the deployed Morpho Blue singleton and Morpho's own documentation and deployments record (docs.morpho.org, the morpho-blue repository). Verify every address and unit against the chain.

Dispatch trigger: new package founding with live mainnet evidence.

task.title: Normalize ECDSA signatures to low-s before Curvy recovery in Onchain.Tempo.Transaction and report the curvy recover_key recid bug upstream
acceptance_criteria: Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.sender/1 returns the same address for the low-s and complement-s encodings of one signature, or rejects the high-s encoding with an explicit error — the choice is documented in the moduledoc
A unit test constructs the complement-s encoding from a known-good signed 0x76 envelope and pins the chosen behaviour
Every Curvy recovery call site across packages/ is listed in the delivery with its normalization status
An upstream issue against libitx/curvy is opened with a minimal reproduction and its URL recorded in the task's implemented note
mix ci passes
out_of_scope: Changing mpp's canonicalize_transaction/1 (already normalizes before recovery, mpp Task 114)
Forking or vendoring curvy
task.body:
curvy 0.3.1 `Curvy.recover_key/3` (deps/curvy/lib/curvy.ex:187-197) binds `recid` from the input struct, calls `Signature.normalize/1` (which for s > n/2 replaces s with n - s AND flips recid), then passes the PRE-normalization recid to `Point.from_signature/3`. For a high-s signature the recovery therefore pairs the normalized s with the wrong recovery id and returns a well-formed but wrong public key instead of the signer's. Observed 2026-09-11 in the mpp repo (harness review of mpp Task 114): `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction.sender/1` on the complement-s encoding of a signed 0x76 envelope returned a different address than on the canonical encoding. Verified by reading the curvy source; premise confirmed.

Consequence today is fail-closed (a verifier comparing the recovered address to an expected signer rejects), and it is not a forgery vector — an attacker can submit any (r, s, recid) triple directly, so the mis-recovered point is already reachable. It IS a correctness defect at the boundary this package owns: `sender/1` must recover the same address for every valid encoding of one signature. Moderato itself rejects high-s at broadcast (-32602 'invalid transaction signature', observed live 2026-09-11), so the fix affects verification of never-broadcast envelopes, not chain state.

Do: normalize to BIP-62 low-s (flip s and recid together) at the recovery boundary in `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction` before calling Curvy, or reject high-s outright with an explicit error — pick one and document it; audit `builder.ex` and any other Curvy recovery call in the eight packages for the same pattern; add a test that feeds the complement-s encoding and asserts either the identical sender or the explicit rejection. Report the bug upstream to libitx/curvy with a minimal reproduction (the maintainer-facing issue text is public-safe; nothing here is embargoed).
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1789498849292-d581df42, 36a9d91bd016c5aa07b0afd91b84a60d70964825).

task.title: Put secp256k1 sign and recover behind a native backend — curvy costs ~2.8 ms per signature on the DEX order path
acceptance_criteria: A NIF-backed secp256k1 backend implements Cartouche.Signer.Backend and is selectable by configuration; Cartouche.Signer.Curvy remains the default and every existing test passes unchanged

Byte-equality proof against curvy: for a fixed corpus of private keys and digests (including a digest whose low-s normalization changes s, and at least one 0x00-prefixed key), the new backend's r/s/recovery-id and the recovered address are identical to curvy's — asserted in a test, not reported in prose
The low-s invariant task 2118 established holds on the new backend, including the sign_direct/4 path

Recovery goes through the same backend seam: Cartouche.Recover no longer calls Curvy.recover_key/3 directly when a non-curvy backend is selected, and the recovered address matches curvy's over the same corpus
A benchmark in the repo reports sign and recover timings for both backends on the same inputs; the CHANGELOG quotes the measured numbers rather than an expected speedup
mix ci passes, and the existing keccak and EIP-712 doctests still pass byte-for-byte
out_of_scope: Changing the default signer backend
Any change to Cartouche.Hash or Hieroglyph's keccak path — already landed in 54539cb
Batching, async signing, or a signing process pool
CloudKMS behaviour changes beyond whatever a new recover callback forces
task.body:
Cartouche's default signer runs secp256k1 in pure Elixir through `curvy`, and that is now
the dominant cost of every signature it produces.

Measured 2026-09-15 from `bourse` (the DEX client consuming this package) against its
signing path, as synchronous scheduler time:

    Cartouche.Signer.Curvy sign_hash          2.788 ms
    Cartouche.Recover recover_signer_address  2.030 ms
    one signed hyperliquid order (end to end) 5.657 ms

The keccak half of that figure is already gone: commit 54539cb swapped both
`Cartouche.Hash.keccak/1` and `Hieroglyph`'s `ABI.Math.kec/1` from `ex_sha3` onto the
`ex_keccak` Rust NIF, taking a 32-byte keccak from 181.96 us to 0.306 us. What remains in
the 5.657 ms is curvy's ECDSA. A consumer that signs on request — bourse places orders
per-call, synchronously — pays that per order.

Tasks 2104, 2116 and 2118 built and hardened the contract this work plugs into:
`Cartouche.Signer.Backend` is a behaviour with `sign_payload/2`, `public_key/1` and
`algorithm/1`, implemented by `Cartouche.Signer.Curvy` and `Cartouche.Signer.CloudKMS`.
What none of them supplied is a native implementation. `ex_secp256k1` is the obvious
candidate: it ships precompiled through `rustler_precompiled`, which this repo already
depends on for `ex_keccak` and for revm in `onchain_evm`, so it adds no new toolchain
requirement.

Recovery does not sit behind that contract yet: `Cartouche.Recover.recover_public_key_from_digest/2`
calls `Curvy.recover_key/3` directly. Recovery is 2.030 ms of the measurement above, so
leaving it on curvy captures barely half the win.

Open decisions, decided here so an implementer does not answer them silently:

1. **The NIF backend is additive, not the default, in this change.** Curvy stays the
   default so no consumer's signatures change shape without opting in. Flipping the default
   is a separate decision once the equivalence evidence below exists.
2. **`ex_secp256k1` unless a live probe disproves it.** If it cannot produce a recoverable
   signature carrying the recovery id that `Cartouche.Recover` and EIP-155/EIP-712 need,
   say so in the delivery with the observed output and use `libsecp256k1` instead — do not
   paper over it with a curvy fallback inside the backend.
3. **Recovery moves behind the same behaviour.** Splitting sign and recover across two
   mechanisms is what made this cost hard to see. Say so in the delivery if a `recover/2`
   callback cannot be shaped for CloudKMS, which cannot recover at all.

Low-s stays a library-wide invariant per task 2118 — a new backend must not reintroduce the
bypass that task closed.

The measurement is the reason this is worth doing; it is not a claim that anyone has
complained about latency.
task.implemented: Delivered by 9026 (baa290d). Curvy is gone: secp256k1 signing and recovery run on ex_secp256k1 (RustCrypto k256, precompiled Rustler NIF), with signatures byte-identical to curvy 0.3.1 on pinned vectors and EIP-2 low-s preserved. This task's 'additive, curvy stays default' decision is moot. One piece was not delivered: an in-repo sign/recover benchmark. 9031's bench/ script is the natural home for it.

task.title: advisory_freshness/1 resolves the freshness prover through ~/_DATA/code/onchain-stack, so every other checkout skips the gate
acceptance_criteria: `OnchainMonorepo.MixHelpers.advisory_freshness/1` resolves `bin/advisory-freshness.sh` relative to the monorepo root it is loaded from (the file lives at `<root>/shared/mix_helpers.exs`, so `__DIR__` names the root), not through a hardcoded `~/_DATA/code/onchain-stack` path
A `mix ci` run from a clone at any path — the server mirror `/data/postgresql/code/onchain-stack` included — runs the prover instead of printing the `[skip] ... absent in CI` line

The decision about harness worktrees is explicit and written into the helper's comment: either the gate runs there too (and the serial-`mix ci` rule is what keeps the shared advisory clone from racing), or the skip is deliberately retained behind a named predicate — not an accident of an absolute path

The stale comment claiming both gates shell out to scripts that live OUTSIDE this repo is corrected: only the AGENTS.md renderer does; `bin/advisory-freshness.sh` has been in-repo since the monorepo migration
`cd packages/onchain && mix ci` passes
out_of_scope: Any change to bin/advisory-freshness.sh itself — the script is already checkout-agnostic, it only ever operates on $MIX_AUDIT_ADVISORY_PATH
agents_check/1, whose renderer genuinely does live outside this repo
Adding deps.audit.gated to check.dispatch
task.body:
`shared/mix_helpers.exs` resolves the advisory-freshness prover as an absolute path into
the canonical developer checkout:

    def advisory_freshness(_args) do
      host_script("~/_DATA/code/onchain-stack/bin/advisory-freshness.sh", [], ...)
    end

That path predates the monorepo: before 2026-08-27, `onchain-stack` was a separate
coordination repo and each of the eight packages genuinely had to reach outside itself to
find the script. It does not anymore — `bin/advisory-freshness.sh` is a tracked file in
this repo, two levels up from any package, and `shared/mix_helpers.exs` sits at the root
that owns it.

Why it matters. The prover exists because `mix_audit` discards its own sync exit status
(mirego/mix_audit#61): a database that can no longer sync still prints "No vulnerabilities
found" and exits 0. `deps.audit.gated` runs the prover first so a dead database fails
loudly. With the path hardcoded, any checkout that is not literally
`~/_DATA/code/onchain-stack` — the server mirror `/data/postgresql/code/onchain-stack`
that harness registers as this project's source, every dispatch worktree, any fresh clone
— takes the `File.regular?/1` false branch and prints

    [skip] advisory-mirror freshness check: ... not found (developer-host script, absent in CI).

So the anti-silent-green gate is itself skipped, and `mix deps.audit` goes on to report
green against whatever the mirror happens to hold. It is a visible skip rather than a
silent one, which is the only reason this is a 3 on difficulty rather than a defect.

The script itself needs no change: it operates entirely on
`$MIX_AUDIT_ADVISORY_PATH`/`$HOME/.local/share/elixir-security-advisories-mirego` and never
inspects the checkout it was invoked from, so running the in-repo copy is behaviourally
identical to running the canonical checkout's copy.

The one judgement call is harness worktrees. `check.dispatch` deliberately omits
`deps.audit.gated` because the shared advisory clone cannot take concurrent worktrees, so
the reviewer never reaches this code — but a `mix ci` inside a worktree would, once the
path resolves. Decide that deliberately and write the decision into the comment; the
current behaviour is the accidental consequence of an absolute path, which is the thing
worth removing whichever way the decision goes.

Found by the post-merge audit of e750a22.
task.implemented: advisory_freshness/1 resolves bin/advisory-freshness.sh off __DIR__ (Path.expand("../bin/...", __DIR__)) instead of the hardcoded ~/_DATA/code/onchain-stack path, so every checkout runs the prover instead of printing the skip line. agents_check/1 keeps its absolute host path (the AGENTS.md renderer genuinely lives outside the repo). The harness-worktree question is answered explicitly in the comment: the gate does run there, the serial-mix-ci rule guards the shared advisory clone, and check.dispatch omits deps.audit.gated anyway. Verified by running deps.audit.gated (prover fired: 'advisory-freshness: OK - at upstream tip 5246bcc') and by a fake-clone probe from cwd=/ resolving to the clone's own bin/.

The root CLAUDE.md Open Item that tracked this migration's completeness is closed out, and its AGENTS.md render updated to match
`cd packages/<name> && mix ci` passes for each of the six edited packages, run serially

Changing any coverage threshold
Changing the `--exclude integration` / `--exclude dev_node` filters

task.body:
Six of the eight packages still pass `--summary-only` to `test.json --cover` in their
`precommit.full` / `ci` alias:

    packages/hieroglyph/mix.exs:189     --cover-threshold 95  --summary-only
    packages/cartouche/mix.exs:312      --cover-threshold 85  --summary-only
    packages/onchain/mix.exs:227        --cover-threshold 70  --summary-only
    packages/onchain_evm/mix.exs:226    --cover-threshold 85  --summary-only
    packages/onchain_js/mix.exs:224     --cover-threshold 25  --summary-only
    packages/onchain_tempo/mix.exs:216  --cover-threshold 90  --summary-only

Only `onchain_aave` and `onchain_aerodrome` have dropped it. The flag was being removed
package-by-package during the standalone era; the monorepo merge did not finish the sweep,
and the root CLAUDE.md has carried it as an unverified Open Item ever since. This audit
measured it: 6 of 8, listed above.

What the flag costs, quoting the rationale onchain_aerodrome's mix.exs already carries:
`--summary-only` is in ex_unit_json's `retry_disqualified_opts?/1` list, so passing it
silently disables the tool's own automatic retry-on-flaky. Two things are lost at once —
a real flake no longer retries and heals (it blocks the gate instead of being reported in
a `flaky` array), and a confirmed failure prints a bare summary line instead of the
assertion detail that names which test failed and why. The default output mode is already
quiet on a green run (an empty `tests` array), so dropping the flag costs nothing when
nothing fails.

Straight mechanical sweep. The only care needed is running each package's `mix ci` serially
afterwards — never two at once — because every package's `deps.audit.gated` step pulls the
one shared advisory clone at ~/.local/share/elixir-security-advisories-mirego, and
concurrent pulls interleave into one FETCH_HEAD and red a package whose code is fine.

Found by the post-merge audit of e750a22.
task.implemented: Dropped --summary-only from the test.json step in hieroglyph, cartouche, onchain, onchain_evm, onchain_js and onchain_tempo, carrying onchain_aave's rationale comment (the flag is in ex_unit_json's retry_disqualified_opts?/1, so it silently disables retry-on-flaky and hides which test failed) into each. task.title: Normalize high-s signatures at Cartouche's recovery boundary — recover_public_key_from_digest/2 still hits the curvy#8 recid bug
acceptance_criteria: `Cartouche.Recover.recover_public_key_from_digest/2` returns the same public key for the low-s and complement-s encodings of one signature, or rejects the high-s encoding with an explicit error — the choice is documented in the function's @doc, matching whatever `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction` chose in task 8014 (it normalizes; it does not reject)

A test constructs the complement-s encoding (s -> n - s, recid bxor 1) of a known-good signature over a fixed digest and asserts the pinned behaviour for BOTH input shapes the function accepts: a `%Curvy.Signature{}` struct and a 65-byte binary

`Cartouche.Transaction.V1/V3/V4/V_2930.recover_signer` inherit the fix (they route through `Recover.recover_eth/2`), proven by at least one envelope-level test that recovers the same address from a complement-s encoded signed transaction

`normalize_low_s/1` is either reused or explicitly left alone with the reason recorded: it sets `recid: nil` for the signing path's recid re-derivation, so it is NOT directly usable at the recovery boundary, where `s` and `recid` must flip together

`Onchain.AA.recover_address/2` (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/aa.ex:613) is either fixed the same way or documented as safe with the argument — today it only ever sees locally generated low-s signatures during the recid search
CHANGELOG entry under cartouche's Unreleased section; touched critical modules stay at >=95% coverage; `mix ci` passes in every package touched
out_of_scope: Replacing curvy with a native secp256k1 backend — that is task 9002, which explicitly keeps curvy as the default and must not be pre-empted here
Rejecting high-s on the signing/emission side — the library-wide low-s emission invariant is task 3149's territory
Any change to Onchain.Tempo.Transaction — already fixed in task 8014 (shipped 36a9d91bd016)
task.body:
Sibling check (DD-8): 8014 is the same DEFECT CLASS but a different surface and is already done
— it fixed onchain_tempo only. 2091/2092 are Solana signature-count guards, unrelated. This task
states the class invariant once for the packages 8014 left untouched: no recovery path in the
family may call `Curvy.recover_key/3` on a signature it has not normalized.

Task 8014 fixed the curvy high-s recovery defect in `Onchain.Tempo.Transaction` and reported it
upstream as libitx/curvy#8 (issue confirmed open, titled "recover_key/3 uses pre-normalization
recovery ID for high-s signatures"). That task's delivery also audited every Curvy recovery call
site in `packages/` and found one still unnormalized — then the write-up carrying that finding was
deleted as a stray file in 36a9d91 without a task replacing it. This is that task.

`Cartouche.Recover.recover_public_key_from_digest/2` (recover.ex:126-130) pipes the caller's
signature straight into `Curvy.recover_key/3`. curvy 0.3.1 binds `recid` from the input struct,
then calls `Signature.normalize/1` — which for `s > n/2` replaces `s` with `n - s` AND flips
`recid` — and passes the PRE-normalization recid to `Point.from_signature/3`. A high-s input
therefore recovers a well-formed but WRONG public key.

This is the shared recovery API, not a leaf: `recover_public_key/2` and `recover_eth/2` both
funnel through it, and `Cartouche.Transaction.V1/V3/V4/V_2930.recover_signer` call `recover_eth/2`
on signatures that arrive from outside the library. Every one of those inherits the defect.

Consequence is fail-closed, as in 8014 — a verifier comparing the recovered address against an
expected signer rejects a valid complement-s encoding rather than accepting a forgery. An attacker
can already submit any (r, s, recid) triple directly, so the mis-recovered point is reachable
without this bug. It is a correctness defect at a boundary cartouche owns: one signature has two
valid encodings and both must recover the same key.

The fix in 8014 was three lines: `CurvySig.normalize(%CurvySig{...})` before the recovery call
(onchain_tempo/lib/onchain/tempo/transaction.ex:412-419). Watch the trap that makes this more than
a copy-paste: cartouche's own `Recover.normalize_low_s/1` (recover.ex:143-147) deliberately sets
`recid: nil`, because the signing path re-derives the recid afterward via `find_recid_from_digest/3`.
At the recovery boundary the recid must be FLIPPED, not dropped — reusing `normalize_low_s/1`
unchanged would break recovery for every high-s input instead of fixing it.

Ordered after task 2134, which is in flight on the same file (recover.ex) — do not dispatch both
against the same write set concurrently.

Discovered 2026-09-15 by the post-merge audit of 428556c.
task.implemented: Normalize decoded signatures with Curvy.Signature.normalize before recovery, retaining correct recid parity; signing-path normalize_low_s unchanged. Regression matrix covers low/complement-s across binary and struct forms, digest/message/personal-sign and legacy transaction recovery; 44 focused tests and package mix ci pass. AA recovery consumes only locally normalized signer output. Independently reviewed by aave_review.

task.title: Reconcile Cartouche release notes against everything landed since 0.9.1
acceptance_criteria: The next release notes describe all four task 2134 changes and the packed signature width contract.

The notes carry a BREAKING entry for the task 2133 bytesN padding flip in Cartouche.Typed.Type.encode_data_value/2,3, deserialize_value!/2 and serialize_value/2: a short bytesN value previously left-padded and now right-pads, so a consumer relying on the old behaviour gets different struct hashes, digests and signatures with no error.
The notes also record task 2133's int8..int256 support, uintN/intN range rejection, array-of-struct encoding, and the encode_type/2 termination fix.
The version bump chosen for the release reflects the breaking encoding change rather than treating it as a patch.
The CHANGELOG is reconciled against `git log packages/cartouche` since the 0.9.1 cut, not only against the two tasks named here, so no further landed change is left unrecorded.
task.body:
Two consecutive audits (408b2b6, 0f5ad9b) found landed Cartouche work with no
release-note entry, so this is a class, not two incidents: harness reserves CHANGELOG
edits during dispatch, and nothing reconciles them afterwards. Close the class in one
release-preparation pass rather than one entry at a time.

Audit 408b2b6: no entry for task 2134's EIP-191 byte-length fix, recover_personal_sign/2,
variable-width packed signatures, or explicit chain-id normalization.

Audit 0f5ad9b: no entry for task 2133 (c3c6ff1a61f4 / 81944554ab4e), which is not
additive. EIP-712 fixed-bytes encoding was wrong before (left-padded) and is right now
(right-padded), so every consumer that passed a short `bytesN` value gets a different
digest and therefore a different signature, silently and without an error. Cartouche is a
signing library; a consumer discovering this from a rejected on-chain signature is the
failure mode to avoid.

Walk the git log for `packages/cartouche` since the 0.9.1 cut and write entries for
everything found, not only the two tasks above. Decide the version bump against the
published 0.9.1 baseline with the breaking behaviour in mind. Do not rewrite historical
entries.
task.implemented: Superseded by 9036. Cartouche will not release again after the fold (9030) and rename (9036); it gets hex.retire. 2134's items are already in the 0.9.1 notes (recover_personal_sign, sign_message). The remainders move into 9036's migration section: 2133's bytesN padding flip shipped unannounced in cartouche 0.9.1 (c3c6ff1 is an ancestor of cartouche-v0.9.1), and the docs/cartouche/CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] heading mislabels the already-published 0.10.0 (tag at a6981d9), which still contains Cartouche.Solana.

task.title: Detect Aave address-book drift against upstream (V4 registry and V3 periphery), not only against the committed snapshot
acceptance_criteria: An integration-tagged check fetches safe.csv from aave-dao/aave-address-book at HEAD and fails when an upstream AaveV4Ethereum or AaveV4Avalanche entry is missing from, or resolves differently in, Onchain.Aave.Contracts — naming each drifted label and both addresses, not just a count; every other upstream AaveV4* namespace (today AaveV4Base and AaveV4Arc) is reported as unserved, listing its row count, without failing unless the registry claims that network

The same check covers every V3 mainnet network the registry serves (ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, base, polygon, avalanche), for each V3 key the registry holds (pool, pool_addresses_provider, oracle, ui_pool_data_provider, and any other periphery key), comparing against the matching AaveV3 + network-name (e.g. AaveV3Ethereum) safe.csv label; all six `ui_pool_data_provider` entries are in scope (none appeared in safe.csv on 2026-09-29)
The check also fails when upstream has REMOVED or re-pointed a label the registry still serves
The pinned commit and its row counts live in exactly one place that both the drift check and V4_SCOPING.md read from
Missing network access flunks with an explicit message and does not silently pass; the default offline test run is unaffected in duration
test/fixtures/v4_safe.csv keeps its role as the offline snapshot the fast registry test reads; this task adds the upstream comparison rather than replacing it
The re-sync procedure (fetch, diff, regenerate, bump the pinned commit) is written down in V4_SCOPING.md
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

Testnets are exempt from the safe.csv comparison because safe.csv carries no testnet rows; sepolia and base_sepolia are instead compared against aave-address-book src/AaveV3Sepolia.sol and src/AaveV3BaseSepolia.sol at HEAD, and the check names that authority in its output
out_of_scope: Auto-regenerating the address maps from a fetched CSV at compile time — the registry stays committed source a human reviews
Fixing drifted entries found by the check — each becomes a data change of its own (the mainnet ui_pool_data_provider entry is fixed by task 4058)
Chainlink price-feed address space, which is a separate namespace
Adding the check to check.dispatch or the default offline run — it needs network access
task.body:
Task 4069 re-derived the whole V4 registry from aave-dao/aave-address-book safe.csv at commit fdaecf26 and committed the 390 rows it consumed as test/fixtures/v4_safe.csv. registry_test.exs then asserts every fixture row resolves through the public API with the right address. That test compares the registry against the same snapshot the registry was generated from, so it cannot notice that upstream has moved on.

The drift rate is measured. The AaveV4Ethereum namespace went 150 entries (2026-04-16) -> 304 (2026-08-26) -> 317 (fdaecf26, 2026-09-15), and 4069 found CONFIG_ENGINE re-pointed from 0xe8096f93... to 0xa1673fbD... in that window. V3 drifts too: the mainnet `ui_pool_data_provider` entry in Onchain.Aave.Contracts is 0x56b7A1012765C285afAC8b8F25C69Bf10ccfE978, while safe.csv lists AaveV3Ethereum UI_POOL_DATA_PROVIDER = 0x2dAd8162A989cd99D673dE4425Bb2298Db1E1aA2 — the v3.7 helper whose getEModes layout differs (verified live 2026-09-29; task 4058 fixes that entry). (2026-09-29 review) Wider than first measured: none of the six mainnet `ui_pool_data_provider` entries appears in safe.csv, and safe.csv now carries AaveV4Base (48 rows) and AaveV4Arc (50 rows) that the registry does not serve (task 4070 registers them). Testnets are absent from safe.csv; their authority is src/AaveV3Sepolia.sol / src/AaveV3BaseSepolia.sol in the same repo. Pool and PoolAddressesProvider are stable, but periphery helpers (UI data providers, oracle, protocol data provider) are redeployed on protocol upgrades.

Serving a stale address is worse than serving none: address/2 returns {:ok, addr} and callers sign against it or decode with the wrong layout.

The check has to be network-tagged — the default gate is offline — so it is an `@moduletag :integration` comparison or an operator-run mix task, run on demand. What matters is that "has upstream moved?" becomes one command with a diff.

AUTHORITY: aave-dao/aave-address-book safe.csv at HEAD for the upstream set; this package's own V3 and V4 address maps for the served set. The committed fixture is the snapshot under test, never the authority for what is current.

task.title: TypesCase resolves overloaded Sugar ABI entries by name alone — disambiguate by input types like the drift test does
acceptance_criteria: Onchain.Aerodrome.TypesCase resolves an ABI function entry by name AND input-type list, matching the disambiguation abi_drift_test.exs already performs, so an overloaded Sugar function cannot silently resolve to the wrong entry

A named test proves the disambiguation works: given an ABI capture carrying two same-named functions with different input types, the helper selects the one the caller asked for and fails loudly when no entry matches — not silently on hd/1 of an empty match
Every existing assert_one_to_one/4,5 call site passes its overload's input types (relay_sugar.json all(address) is the live case); the change is confined to test support and test files
mix check.dispatch passes in packages/onchain_aerodrome
out_of_scope: Changing Onchain.Aerodrome.Types.* production modules
Re-capturing any priv/abis/*.json
Refactoring abi_drift_test.exs's own ABI reader, which already disambiguates correctly
task.body:
Found during the post-merge audit of ead58bc (task 5007's veAERO structs).

`Onchain.Aerodrome.TypesCase.abi_entry/2` (test/support/types_case.ex) finds an ABI entry with `Enum.find(&(&1["type"] == "function" and &1["name"] == abi_function))` — name only. `abi_drift_test.exs` reading the same JSON takes an optional `input_types` argument and matches on it too, and Relay's drift test passes `["address"]` explicitly because `RelaySugar` exposes `all` in more than one arity upstream.

Today the captured `priv/abis/relay_sugar.json` contains exactly one `all` entry, so both readers agree and nothing is wrong — this is latent, not a live bug. The asymmetry is the defect: the drift test is hardened against a re-capture that adds an `all` overload; the shared test helper is not. After such a re-capture, `TypesCase.assert_one_to_one(Relay, {"relay_sugar.json", "all"}, ...)` would compare Relay's fields against whichever overload happens to sit first in the JSON array, and a mismatch there reads as a struct bug rather than a resolution bug. Worse, the two readers would then disagree, so the drift test could stay green while the one-to-one assertions grade against the wrong shape.

Note the failure mode when no entry matches at all: `abi_entry/2` returns `nil` and the following `Map.fetch!/2` raises on nil rather than naming the function it could not resolve. Fix that at the same time — a test-support helper that cannot find its ABI entry should say which file and which signature it was looking for.

Prefer lifting the drift test's existing `function_match?/3` shape into the shared helper over inventing a second mechanism; the point of the task is that there is one resolution rule, not two.
task.implemented: TypesCase.abi_entry/3 and a new public resolve_entry/4 disambiguate by name AND input types, using the drift test's own function_match?/3 clause moved verbatim - one resolution rule, not two. abi_drift_test.exs now consumes the shared helper (its private copies deleted). No-match and ambiguous-match both flunk naming the file, the sought signature and the candidates, replacing a nil-then-Map.fetch! crash; assert_one_to_one's 2-tuple form is gone so no call site can fall back to name-alone. All call sites pass their overload's types; the two lp_sugar_test sites derive them from the fixture's captured signature. New types_case_test.exs proves selection and both loud-failure paths against an in-test two-overload ABI. 73 tests green.

task.title: check.dispatch runs NO tests in onchain_aave, onchain_aerodrome and onchain_evm — the reviewer gate grades three packages without executing their suites
acceptance_criteria: packages/onchain_aave, packages/onchain_aerodrome and packages/onchain_evm each run their test suite as part of mix check.dispatch, consistent with the five packages that already do

onchain_aerodrome's Foundry-dependent calldata fixture tests are resolved explicitly, not by accident: either Foundry is documented as a required dispatch-node prerequisite in the root CLAUDE.md Harness section AND verified present on the dispatch nodes, or those tests carry an exclusion tag that check.dispatch excludes while mix ci still runs them — state which was chosen and why in the delivery
mix check.dispatch passes in all three packages on a cold worktree with no Foundry and no RPC credentials, or the delivery names exactly which prerequisite a dispatch node must carry
The root CLAUDE.md Harness section states that check.dispatch includes a test run in every package, so a future copy of the alias template cannot silently omit it
mix ci passes at the repo root
out_of_scope: Adding agents.check, deps.audit.gated, cold-PLT dialyzer or the coverage pass to check.dispatch — they are deliberately excluded (see root CLAUDE.md Harness)
The --summary-only migration on precommit.full, which is task 9004
Changing what mix ci runs in any package
task.body:
Found during the post-merge audit of ead58bc, by running the project's own dispatch gate on a cold worktree and noticing the output contained no test summary.

Measured 2026-09-15 across all eight packages' `check.dispatch` aliases:

- WITH a test step: cartouche, hieroglyph, onchain, onchain_js, onchain_tempo
- WITHOUT any test step: **onchain_aave, onchain_aerodrome, onchain_evm**

The three failing aliases are byte-identical to each other — `format --check-formatted`, `compile --warnings-as-errors`, `credo --strict ...`, `doctor --raise`, `ex_dna --max-clones 0`, `reach.check --arch --smells`, `sobelow --skip --exit low` — one copied template with the test step dropped.

Why this matters more than its size suggests: `check.dispatch` is the project's registered `check_command`. It is what the cross-family reviewer runs, and per the harness contract the reviewer IS the gate. So for three of eight packages the gate proves the code compiles, formats and passes static analysis, and proves nothing about whether it *works*. Concretely, task 5007 landed 47 new `Onchain.Aerodrome.Types.*` tests in this very range and the reviewer worktree never executed one of them. Every green verdict on these three packages has been quieter than it looked.

This is exactly the whole-surface class the root CLAUDE.md describes: no per-task reviewer can see it, because no single task's diff contains it. Fix it in the alias, and write the invariant down so the next copy of the template cannot drop the step again.

One real obstacle, which is why this is a task rather than a one-line edit. `packages/onchain_aerodrome`'s suite does not currently pass on a bare node: `test/onchain/aerodrome/calldata_fixture_test.exs` fails 3 tests with "Foundry cast is required on PATH; never a skip" (verified on this audit node, `cast` absent; landed earlier under task 5026 in fe6faa0 / 6af0864). That refusal-to-skip is deliberate and correct for `mix ci` — an evidence harness that silently skips proves nothing. But naively adding `test.json` to `check.dispatch` would turn every future onchain_aerodrome dispatch red on any node without Foundry. Decide that explicitly: either dispatch nodes carry Foundry and the root CLAUDE.md says so, or the calldata fixture tests get a tag `check.dispatch` excludes while `mix ci` still runs. Do not resolve it by weakening the test.

Verify the other two packages' suites actually pass cold before wiring them in; `onchain_evm` has a Rust NIF build and `onchain_aave` may have integration-tagged tests needing exclusion.
task.implemented: Added complete offline suites to Aave, Aerodrome and EVM check.dispatch, preserving exclusions of heavier gates. Foundry is an explicit prerequisite: verified cast 1.8.3 installed on blockwatch-harness; Aerodrome prepends the standard ~/.foundry/bin because the service PATH omits it. All three dispatch gates pass (406/172/298 tests). An isolated intentionally failing test was executed/retried and made Aerodrome check.dispatch exit 2; after removing it the gate passed. Source-built root mix ci passed all eight packages: 3788 offline tests, 28 EVM plus 7 Solidity Rust tests, Clippy and existing quality gates. Independent crypto_review inspected gates. No muex run.

Root mix.lock and the onchain_aave, onchain_aerodrome, onchain_evm and onchain_js locks resolve the fixed Mint version, with no bound widened or narrowed and no advisory suppressed
`mix hex.audit` reports no Mint advisory at the root or in any of the five packages; `mix deps.audit` is run too and any remaining findings are reported separately
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Re-adjudicating the documented gun/cowlib mirror-grouping issue
Publishing packages or changing unrelated dependency bounds
task.body:
Current state (verified 2026-09-29): Mint 1.11.0 was published to Hex on 2026-09-28. packages/onchain, onchain_solana and onchain_tempo already lock 1.11.0, and `mix hex.audit` in packages/onchain exits 0 with only the adjudicated, ignored cowlib/gun entries. The root mix.lock (1.10.0) still reports four Mint advisories from `mix hex.audit`: EEF-CVE-2026-82672, EEF-CVE-2026-91043 (HIGH), EEF-CVE-2026-92103 and EEF-CVE-2026-94194.

OSV: EEF-CVE-2026-82672 fixed 1.10.1; EEF-CVE-2026-91043/-92103/-94194 fixed 1.11.0. hex.audit: no Mint advisory at root or in the four packages; deps.audit clean except onchain_js reporting the adjudicated gun GHSA-w4f7-4cxr-rv3c (its plain deps.audit alias lacks --ignore-file; the gated alias ignores it). check.dispatch green in all four.

task.title: Onchain.Chain as a generated chain registry: ids, currency, RPC URLs, explorers, well-known contract addresses, from a vendored upstream snapshot
acceptance_criteria: `Onchain.Chain` exposes a struct per known chain with at least: id, name, native currency (name/symbol/decimals), public RPC URLs, block explorer URLs, a testnet flag, and a well-known-contracts map carrying Multicall3, the ENS registry and universal resolver, and EntryPoint v0.6/v0.7 where deployed; `parse_id/1` and every existing caller keep working unchanged

The chain data is generated, not hand-typed: the upstream source is vendored in the repo at a named ethereum-lists/chains commit; a Mix task regenerates the definitions file from that vendored copy, and a test asserts the committed file is byte-identical to a fresh offline run, so drift fails the gate without network access; refreshing the vendored snapshot from upstream is an opt-in flag of the same task, not part of any test

Every chain the current atom->id map names (all 24) resolves to a full struct with a non-empty RPC URL list, and the generated set covers at least the chains viem ships for the same ids — spot-checked by a test against five ids taken from viem's `chains/definitions` at a named commit

The well-known-contracts overlay cites its source per address (mds1/multicall deployments.json for Multicall3, ENS docs for the registry and universal resolver, eth-infinitism for EntryPoint); ENS entries appear only on chains where ENS is deployed (mainnet and its testnets), never inferred for L2s
Runtime extension works: a caller can register or override a chain (a private chain, a custom RPC URL) without regeneration, pinned by a test
Upstream licence and attribution for the generation source are recorded in the generated file header and in the package README

The generator drops templated RPC URLs (any URL containing `${…}`, e.g. `https://mainnet.infura.io/v3/${INFURA_API_KEY}`) and keeps `wss://` URLs in a field separate from HTTP ones, so the 'non-empty RPC URL list' criterion is satisfied by directly usable HTTP endpoints only — pinned by a test on a fixture chain carrying both kinds (added 2026-09-16, parity-task review)
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Chain-specific transaction formatters (OP Stack deposit type 0x7e, zkSync 0x71, Celo) — separate task if a consumer hits one; onchain_tempo shows the pattern
A fallback or ranked transport over the RPC URL list — that is the transport-fallback task; this registry only supplies the URLs
Protocol address tables (Aave, Aerodrome) — they stay in their packages; only chain-level, protocol-agnostic contracts belong here
task.body:
Decide first (vetoable defaults written in so an unattended implementer is not guessing):

1. Generation source. Default: ethereum-lists/chains (`_data/chains/eip155-<id>.json`, CC0) for id, name, currency, RPC URLs, explorers and testnet status, plus a small hand-curated overlay file in the repo for well-known contract addresses (Multicall3 from mds1/multicall `deployments.json`, ENS from the ENS docs, EntryPoint from eth-infinitism). viem's `src/chains/definitions` is the cross-check, not the source: it is MIT with attribution required, hand-maintained TypeScript, and carries per-chain formatters this task does not want. If viem turns out to be the only source with a field the registry needs, switch and record the attribution.

2. Scope of chains. Default: every non-deprecated chain in the source, filtered to the ones that have at least one public RPC URL. That is a few hundred structs — fine for a compiled module map. Do not hand-pick; hand-picking is how the current 24-entry map fell behind.

Why: `Cartouche.Chain` today is a 96-line atom->chain-id map (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/chain.ex). It is sequenced after 9036, which renames it to `Onchain.Chain`, so build the registry under that name. Nothing in the family can answer what a chain's native currency is, which explorer to link, or which RPC to try, and the Multicall3 address is a module attribute in `Onchain.Multicall` (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/multicall.ex:32; the ENS registry is likewise a module attribute at lib/onchain/ens.ex:70) — correct only because Multicall3 happens to be deterministically deployed at one address nearly everywhere. This is the largest structural gap between the stack and viem by ratio, and the `Onchain.Client` task builds directly on it.

(2026-09-29 review, split) This task is the generator plus the registry only. Adopting the registry in Onchain.Multicall and Onchain.ENS, and the live aggregate3 reads that prove the addresses, moved to the follow-up task 'Route Onchain.Multicall and Onchain.ENS contract addresses through the Onchain.Chain registry'. Vendor the upstream data: commit the ethereum-lists/chains snapshot (or the filtered subset the generator reads) at a named commit. The gate regenerates from that vendored copy with no network access. Refreshing from upstream over the network is an opt-in Mix task flag, never a test.

Keep the struct shape small and additive; the registry is data, and consumers should be able to override or extend entries at runtime (a private chain, a custom RPC) without a regeneration.

Authority: the upstream JSON at a named commit for the generated data; the live chain for the well-known-contract addresses (the live aggregate3 read in the acceptance criteria is what proves an address, not the overlay file).

Dispatch trigger: registry plus adoption in Multicall/ENS, with a generated-artifact invariant that needs an independent reviewer to check the regeneration test actually gates.

2026-09-16 (parity-task review): ethereum-lists/chains carries templated URLs (`${INFURA_API_KEY}`-style) and `wss://` entries inside the same `rpc` array; both would pass a naive non-empty check and neither is usable by the HTTP-only fallback transport. Also a sizing correction: the source lists well over 2000 chains, not a few hundred — the public-HTTP-URL filter is what bounds the compiled module; measure compile time once and record it in the CHANGELOG entry.

task.title: Fallback transport: ranked multi-endpoint RPC with health tracking, failing over on transport errors and node refusals but never on application errors
acceptance_criteria: A caller can hand `send_rpc/3` (or its documented equivalent) an ordered list of endpoints instead of one URL; the first healthy endpoint serves the request and the result shape is identical to the single-URL path

Failover happens on transport failures (connect refused, timeout, 5xx, malformed JSON) and on node-refusal classes from task 2137 (method-not-found, namespace-unavailable, and unavailable: -32001 'Unable to complete request', which a non-archive endpoint answers for historical state), because another provider may serve the method; it never happens on JSON-RPC application errors (execution reverted, invalid params) — pinned by tests for each class

Endpoint health is tracked per endpoint (recent failure count and latency) and the ranking reorders on it; the ranking is observable through a documented function so an operator can see why an endpoint was skipped

A live test lists a deliberately unreachable URL first followed by two real hosted mainnet endpoints and asserts a successful `eth_blockNumber`; a second live test asserts an `eth_call` that reverts is returned as the revert from the first endpoint without any call reaching the second (asserted via request counting, not timing)
Telemetry from task 2137 carries the endpoint that served each request and each failover event
Single-URL callers see no behaviour change; the existing RPC suites pass without edits
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

Non-idempotent methods never fail over once a request has left the process: `eth_sendTransaction` (node-managed nonce) and every state-mutating dev-node method (`evm_mine`, `evm_increaseTime`, `anvil_setBalance`, …) fail over only on connect-level failures before send, never on a timeout or 5xx after it — pinned by a request-counting test that times out a mutating call on endpoint one and asserts endpoint two never sees it; `eth_sendRawTransaction` is exempt (same-hash idempotent) and a test asserts it does fail over. When the next endpoint answers 'already known', the call returns {:ok, hash}, with the hash precomputed as keccak256 of the signed bytes. 'nonce too low' maps to {:ok, hash} only when eth_getTransactionByHash of that precomputed hash finds the transaction; otherwise the error is returned. Both cases are pinned by request-counting tests (added 2026-09-16, parity-task review)
out_of_scope: WebSocket and IPC transports. HTTP only; zen_websocket owns the socket path
Automatic transparent request batching (viem `batch: true`). The array batch primitive is task 2137's; making it implicit is a separate decision
Onchain.Client adoption; task 9017 passes the URL list through
task.body:
The family has exactly one transport shape: one URL, one request. Task 2137 builds retry, refusal classification, telemetry and the array-batch primitive into the transport layer, and 9035 unifies Cartouche.RPC and Onchain.RPC so there is one transport to extend; this task composes the next layer on top of them — several endpoints, ranked by health, with failover. It depends on 2137 for the classification, because the interesting failover decision (a provider that does not serve `trace_*` or `eth_getBlockReceipts` should not fail the call when a second provider does) is only expressible once refusals are tagged rather than opaque strings. Task 2136's multi-endpoint live-test seam is the test infrastructure to reuse here; it is a test seam, not a runtime transport.

The one rule that must not be got wrong: application errors are final. A revert, an invalid-params error, a nonce-too-low — retrying those on another endpoint is at best wasted and at worst double-submits a transaction. Transport failures and capability refusals fail over; everything the node answered with a JSON-RPC error object that is not a refusal class is returned as-is from the endpoint that produced it.

Design freedom: whether this is a new module, an option on `send_rpc/3`, or both, is the implementer's call — read how the unified RPC module threads its `:decode` option and follow that convention rather than inventing a second one. Health tracking needs process state; keep it an explicit, supervised, optional component so a caller who passes a single URL pays nothing.

Authority: the live endpoints. Provider documentation on which methods they serve is reference material; the request-counting live test is the evidence.

Dispatch trigger: transport-layer change on the money path with a live-evidence requirement, and a sequenced dependency on 2137 that a reviewer must confirm was actually built on, not around.

2026-09-16 (parity-task review): the 'application errors are final' rule covers JSON-RPC error objects, not a transport timeout after the request was sent. Re-sending on another endpoint is safe for reads and for `eth_sendRawTransaction` (same signed bytes, same hash) but double-applies `eth_sendTransaction` and the dev-node write methods the dev-node-actions task wraps. Failover therefore needs a per-method idempotency class alongside the refusal class from 2137 — added as an acceptance criterion.

(2026-09-29 review) Two refinements. First, a re-sent eth_sendRawTransaction usually reaches an endpoint that already saw it through gossip, and that endpoint answers 'already known' or 'nonce too low'. Both are application errors on their face, but the transaction was broadcast. Return success with the locally computed hash for 'already known'. For 'nonce too low', return success only after confirming by hash, because a different transaction may have taken the nonce. Second, -32001 (tagged :unavailable by 2137) is what a non-archive endpoint answers for historical state, so it is a failover class like method-not-found. Sequenced after 9036 so the new transport code lands under Onchain.* directly instead of in Cartouche.* modules that are about to be renamed.

task.title: Local key material for the signer, part 1: BIP-39 mnemonics and BIP-32/44 HD derivation, via alloy-signer-local through the core NIF
acceptance_criteria: BIP-39: generate a 12/15/18/21/24-word English mnemonic from a CSPRNG, validate the checksum, and derive the 64-byte seed with an optional passphrase; every Trezor reference vector (english, passphrase TREZOR) round-trips

BIP-32/44 over secp256k1: hardened and non-hardened child derivation, path parsing (`m/44'/60'/0'/0/i`), private key and address out; the anvil/hardhat mnemonic `test test test test test test test test test test test junk` derives the ten default accounts at indices 0..9 (address 0 is 0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266), and BIP-32 test vectors 1 and 2 match on the derived private keys
The implementation goes through alloy-signer-local's mnemonic support in the core NIF (packages/onchain/native/); the CHANGELOG names the crate versions
A derived key plugs into the signer as a local backend through the existing `{backend, config}` carrier and signs a real transaction that a dev node accepts (live test on anvil)

No key material leaks through `inspect/1`, logs, or error messages: structs holding seeds, private keys and mnemonics have a redacting `Inspect` implementation, and NIF error terms carry no secret bytes, pinned by tests
Sobelow reports nothing new and no `.sobelow-skips` entry is added
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Web3 Secret Storage v3 keystore import/export; the part-2 sibling task owns it
Non-secp256k1 derivation (ed25519 / SLIP-0010 for the Solana tree); separate task if the Solana signer needs it
Hardware wallet or browser wallet integration
Non-English BIP-39 wordlists
task.body:
Why: key handling in the signer family is oddly shaped. Google Cloud KMS signing is a first-class backend for both EVM and Solana, but the commodity local paths every Ethereum library ships (mnemonic, HD derivation, keystore file) exist nowhere in the family (grep for bip39/mnemonic/keystore/scrypt across all packages, 2026-09-16 and re-checked 2026-09-29: zero hits in lib/ outside node-custody RPC docs). A developer with an anvil mnemonic cannot get a signer out of this stack without a second library.

(2026-09-29 review, split) This task is the mnemonic/HD half. Web3 Secret Storage (keystore v3) moved to the sibling task 'Local key material for the signer, part 2: Web3 Secret Storage v3 (keystore) import and export via alloy-signer-local'.

Implementation path, decided, not re-opened: use alloy-signer-local's mnemonic support (MnemonicBuilder over coins-bip39/coins-bip32) through the core alloy NIF that 9031 introduces in packages/onchain/native/. The family already accepts that native surface, so this adds no new supply-chain root. The earlier 'measure pure-Elixir scrypt, then decide' step is dropped. Run after 9036, so the module is Onchain.Keys (the renamed Cartouche.Keys, packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/keys.ex today, generate_keypair/0). Extend it rather than creating a parallel module.

Authority: the BIP-39 and BIP-32 specifications and their published test vectors, and anvil's derived accounts as a live cross-check. alloy is the implementation, not the oracle.

Dispatch trigger: signing and key-material surface. Security-marked; needs an independent reviewer on redaction and derivation correctness.

task.title: Typed dev-node control wrappers — anvil_*/hardhat_*/evm_* (balance, storage, code, nonce, impersonation, mining, time, snapshots, fork reset) under the non-standard-namespace portability contract
acceptance_criteria: Wrappers exist for: set balance, set code, set storage slot, set nonce, impersonate / stop impersonating an account, mine N blocks, set next block timestamp, increase time, snapshot / revert, drop a pending transaction, and reset to a fork; each accepts and returns the RPC layer's usual typed values (integers, hex addresses, binaries), not raw hex strings
hardhat-prefixed aliases are exposed for the methods hardhat names differently, dispatching to the same implementation

Every wrapper classifies node refusals through the existing typed refusal classification (task 3091) and marks the non-standard namespace consistently with the rest of the RPC surface so a call against a hosted node fails with the tagged refusal, not a decode crash — pinned by one live test against a real hosted mainnet endpoint

A live test suite against a real anvil exercises every wrapper at least once and asserts the state change through a standard read (e.g. set balance then `eth_getBalance`; snapshot, mutate, revert, then read back the original), so a wrapper that returns ok without effect fails
packages/onchain/test/support/live.ex and packages/onchain/test/rpc_dev_node_test.exs, the only hand-rolled call sites, use the new wrappers
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Starting or supervising an anvil process from Elixir — callers own the node lifecycle
Simulation — onchain_evm's revm NIF is the in-process path; these wrappers drive a real node
Ganache or other dev-node dialects
task.body:
viem's test client (`setBalance`, `impersonateAccount`, `mine`, `snapshot`, `revert`, ...) is what makes integration tests against a fork cheap to write; nothing in the family wraps these methods (grep for `anvil_`, `evm_mine`, `evm_snapshot` across lib/ and test/ 2026-09-16: re-checked 2026-09-29, hits only in packages/onchain/test/support/live.ex and packages/onchain/test/rpc_dev_node_test.exs, as raw strings; onchain_evm's tests have none).

Wrap the surface, typed, and fold the existing hand-rolled call sites onto it. The interesting part is not the wrappers, it is the contract: these are node-privileged, non-standard methods, and task 2135 owns how cartouche marks and classifies such a surface. Build on that contract; do not invent a second marking scheme. (2026-09-29 review) The dependency on 2135 was dropped: 2135 is the trace_*/debug_traceCall portability task and is itself blocked on 2137. The refusal classification these wrappers need already exists (task 3091, done: typed node-capability refusals). Reuse it, and follow 2135's marking convention if it has landed by then. Sequenced after 9036 so the wrappers are written once, under Onchain.*. Note that anvil accepts the hardhat_* names itself, so client-side hardhat aliases only matter against a real hardhat node.

Authority: the foundry repository's anvil RPC implementation (`crates/anvil/src/eth/api.rs` at a named tag) and the hardhat network reference; the live anvil decides semantics. Note anvil and hardhat disagree in places (task 2131's body records one such divergence for a standard method) — where they do, pin anvil's behaviour and document the hardhat difference.

Dispatch trigger: parallel-safe, self-contained, and gives the family's integration tests a shared surface — worth a reviewer confirming the state-change assertions are real rather than shape checks.

task.title: Onchain.Client — one struct binding chain, transport and optional signer, accepted everywhere `rpc_url` is today
acceptance_criteria: `Onchain.Client.new/1` builds a struct from a chain (registry atom, id, or `Onchain.Chain` struct) plus transport options (one URL, a list of URLs, or nothing to use the registry's public URLs) and an optional signer carrier; the struct is inspectable without leaking signer secrets

Every public onchain function that reads a node URL from opts today (`:rpc_url`, or `:ethereum_node` / the key set task 2137 settles on) also accepts `client: %Onchain.Client{}` in `opts` and resolves URL and chain from it through one shared helper; the existing keys keep working unchanged and a test asserts the two paths produce identical requests

`Onchain.Signer.send_transaction/3` accepts the client's signer, so `client |> send_transaction(tx)` works end to end on anvil; if the receipt-wait task has landed, the same anvil test extends the pipeline with its wait function
Moduledocs show the client as the primary entry point in README and the package CLAUDE.md, with the bare `rpc_url` form documented as still supported
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: The chain registry itself (task 9013, a dependency)
Fallback transport internals (task 9014). The client passes a URL list through when that lands, and a single URL until then
Removing the `rpc_url` option; deprecation is a later, separate decision
`watch_*` polling facades; task 3090 owns log/block/pending polling
task.body:
Decide first (defaults written in, vetoable):

1. Does the client carry a signer? Default yes, optional — the `{backend, config}` carrier task 3089 routes `Onchain.Signer` through — so one struct covers viem's public+wallet client split. Read-only clients simply leave it nil.

2. How is the client threaded through the existing surface? Default: an `opts[:client]` key resolved by one helper next to wherever `rpc_url` is read today, so no public arity changes and every existing call site keeps working. A positional client argument is more viem-like but is a breaking change across ~30 functions; not this task.

Why: the substrate is strong and the client layer is missing. Every onchain function takes `rpc_url` in opts, there is no notion of which chain a call is for beyond the URL.

Authority: the live node (mainnet for the mined-receipt case, anvil for the pending and replacement cases); `ethereum/execution-apis` for receipt and transaction object shapes.

Dispatch trigger: cross-cutting change through the whole read/write surface plus the signer pipeline with live evidence — earns an independent reviewer.

Honest score: no consumer in the family needs this today; the demand signal is the viem-parity review of 2026-09-16 and the fact that mpp is a Phoenix app that will eventually authenticate wallets. The rendering format is byte-sensitive (clients sign the exact string), so the spec's ABNF and the spruceid reference vectors are the contract, not a hand-written template. task.body:
Root `mix ci` fails in packages/onchain_aave with Mix.raise(... exited 139), and packages/onchain_aerodrome also exits 139, after every configured check has already printed green: doctor, advisory freshness, deps.audit, coverage (aave 408 passed / 100%; aerodrome 172 passed / 82.25%, both over threshold 65) and dialyzer with 0 errors. packages/onchain_evm's own `mix ci` returns 0 (298 tests, 28+7 Rust tests, clean clippy), as do the other packages. aave and aerodrome are the two packages that pull `sibling(:onchain_evm, "~> 0.6", only: [:dev, :test])` and load the precompiled NIF into a consumer VM.

Leads, not proven causes: (a) NIF teardown at VM halt in a consumer VM; (b) the Mix env split — the aave and aerodrome `def cli` (mix.exs:39-46 / 37-44) do not pin `ci` / `precommit.full` to :test, unlike onchain_evm, onchain and onchain_solana, so the parent Mix process stays in :dev and dialyzer analyzes _build/dev beams. onchain_js and onchain_tempo also lack that pin and exit 0, so the env split alone is not sufficient; (c) rustler_precompiled's copy of the NIF into the consumer _build.

This matters beyond two packages: task 9031 moves a precompiled NIF into core onchain, which every package loads. If (a) is the cause, the crash spreads to all seven packages.

task.title: Onchain.Safe — multiSend, execTransaction and Zodiac Roles calldata builders, extracted from aave_sim
acceptance_criteria: Onchain.Safe exposes calldata-only builders for MultiSendCallOnly multiSend(bytes) packing (call legs only; a delegatecall leg is rejected with a tagged error), execTransaction (owner pre-approved-hash signature form), getTransactionHash and execTransactionWithRole; each returns target and data without sending, and none of them touches Onchain.Signer
Byte-equality against aave_sim's committed fixtures for the same inputs (multiSend packing, execTransaction, execTransactionWithRole), so the extraction is provably lossless
Selector-and-encoding unit tests derive expected bytes from the Safe v1.4.1 and Zodiac Roles ABIs, not from the package's own encoder

A fork integration test executes a two-call multiSend batch through a real Safe 1.4.1 proxy from forked mainnet state and asserts the domain effect; negative controls with a reverting second call cover both GS013 cases: with safeTxGas = 0 and gasPrice = 0 the outer transaction reverts with GS013; with a non-zero safeTxGas the outer transaction succeeds, ExecutionFailure is emitted and execTransaction returns false; in both, no first-call state survives

@moduledoc states the GS013 rule (inner failure reverts the outer tx when safeTxGas and gasPrice are both zero, otherwise ExecutionFailure plus a false return) and names the pinned deployments: Safe v1.4.1, MultiSendCallOnly v1.4.1 at 0x9641d764fc13c8b624c04430c7356c1c7c8102e2, Zodiac Roles v2.1.0
onchain CHANGELOG and README entries
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: Safe deployment, owner management or module enabling — the account exists before this code runs
Zodiac Roles policy authoring (targets, selectors, conditions) — aave_sim task 112 owns the authority model
Replacing aave_sim's copy — a cross-repo follow-up in aave_sim's roadmap once this ships
The EIP-7702/DeleGator adapter — task 3096
task.body:
aave_sim's operator decision of 2026-09-15 made a user-owned Safe the execution account for attended and automated actions (aave_sim docs/one-transaction-rail.md, tasks 146 and 147 done). The application carries the whole encoding half app-locally in lib/aave_sim/execution/safe.ex: MultiSend packing of a call batch into `multiSend(bytes)`, owner execution through `execTransaction` with the pre-approved-hash signature form (v = 1, the signer's own address as the approver), `getTransactionHash` for the nonce-bound hash, and `execTransactionWithRole` for the Zodiac Roles keeper path. None of that exists in onchain — the package has no Safe module at all (grep for multiSend/execTransaction across packages/ on 2026-09-23 returns nothing).

Lift those builders into Onchain.Safe as calldata-only functions returning {target, value, data} in the shape the DeleGator adapter (task 3096) and the Aave calldata builders (task 4071) already use, so an application composes a Safe batch from package pieces alone. aave_sim then consumes the package and deletes its copy; that swap is a cross-repo follow-up filed in aave_sim's roadmap, not part of this task.

AUTHORITY: the Safe v1.4.1 contracts (safe-global/safe-smart-account at tag v1.4.1 — Safe.sol execTransaction/checkNSignatures/getTransactionHash, libraries/MultiSend.sol packing) and the Zodiac Roles modifier source and docs (gnosisguild/zodiac-modifier-roles) for execTransactionWithRole. aave_sim's implementation is the extraction source and a compatibility fixture, not the specification; where the two disagree, the contracts are right. (2026-09-29 review, corrected) Inner-failure semantics depend on the gas parameters. Safe v1.4.1 execTransaction ends with `require(success || safeTxGas != 0 || gasPrice != 0, "GS013")` and otherwise emits ExecutionFailure (safe-smart-account v1.4.1 contracts/Safe.sol). With safeTxGas = 0 and gasPrice = 0, which is the envelope aave_sim builds (lib/aave_sim/execution/safe.ex:97), a failed inner call reverts the whole outer transaction with GS013. Only when safeTxGas or gasPrice is non-zero does the outer transaction succeed, emit ExecutionFailure and return false. The builder's docs must state both cases, and callers must read the execTransaction return value, as aave_sim's result/1 does, rather than trusting receipt status alone.

Pinned deployments: aave_sim targets MultiSendCallOnly v1.4.1 at 0x9641d764fc13c8b624c04430c7356c1c7c8102e2, not MultiSend. MultiSendCallOnly rejects delegatecall legs, and the Safe calls it with operation = 1 (delegatecall). It targets Zodiac Roles v2.1.0 (execTransactionWithRole(address,uint256,bytes,uint8,bytes32,bool), where the bytes32 roleKey is the v2 signature; v1 used a uint16 role) at 0x9646fdad06d3e24444381f44362a3b0eb343d337, source commit 820e5bc975d1817bdd4bc4a95226f553f7b67b68 (aave_sim safe.ex:10-27). Pin the same.

Fork evidence cannot live in packages/onchain. onchain_evm depends on onchain (packages/onchain_evm/mix.exs:93), so onchain cannot take it as a test dependency without a cycle. Run the fork test from packages/onchain_evm/test/ against the onchain builders, or against an anvil --fork-url node.

Dispatch trigger: money-path calldata construction with an independent oracle available (aave_sim's committed fixtures plus a fork execution).

task.title: Replace curvy with a Rust k256 backend for all secp256k1 signing and recovery
acceptance_criteria: `mix deps.tree` in cartouche, onchain and onchain_tempo no longer lists curvy; `grep -rn Curvy packages/*/lib` returns nothing outside a deprecation alias

Differential test: for a fixed set of private keys and digests (include the existing doctest key 0x8005…f4bf and the published Ethereum signing vectors already pinned in cartouche tests), the new backend produces byte-identical r/s/v to curvy 0.3.1. Capture curvy's output once as a fixture before removing it, and note in the test where it came from
A test signs a digest whose raw k256 output would be high-s and asserts the emitted signature has s <= secp256k1n/2
Recover.recover_eth/2 and find_recid round-trip on signatures from the new backend and from CloudKMS (DER-parsed) input; malformed DER still returns an error tuple
A cartouche-owned signature struct replaces Curvy.Signature in every public @spec and struct field; the CHANGELOG lists the break, the new type and the migration line for consumers

Migrating mpp. It lives in its own repo and needs its own follow-up once this cartouche version is published

New KMS or custody backends
task.body:
Cartouche's secp256k1 signing runs on `curvy`, a pure-Elixir implementation (Hex description) whose last release is 0.3.1 from 2023-01-12 (`mix hex.info curvy`, 2026-09-29). It makes no constant-time guarantee and has no audit. `Cartouche.Signer.Curvy`'s moduledoc says it "should not be used in production", but production code signs with it anyway. Found by grep on 2026-09-29: mpp signs fee-payer transactions, Permit2 digests, EIP-3009 authorizations and Tempo access-key payloads through it (mpp/lib/mpp/methods/**, mpp/lib/mpp/client/providers/tempo.ex). Onchain and onchain_tempo sign through it as well.

Replace curvy as cartouche's secp256k1 implementation with `ex_secp256k1`. Its sign/recover path runs on RustCrypto `k256`, the same crate alloy-signer uses (verified by reading ex_secp256k1 0.8.0's native/ex_secp256k1/src/lib.rs). It ships as a precompiled Rustler NIF, so cartouche gains no native build of its own. This was decided on 2026-09-29 against the alternative of porting cartouche wholesale to alloy. The risk sits in the curve arithmetic, not in RLP, tx encoding or EIP-712, which are deterministic and vector-testable. Only ~2k of cartouche's ~22k hand-written lines touch signing, and cartouche's RPC, trace, Solana and codegen surface gains nothing from alloy.

The seam already exists: `Cartouche.Signer.Backend` (pure 32-byte digest contract, task 104). The work that is really breaking is the signature type. `Curvy.Signature` leaks into public specs (`Cartouche.Recover`, the backend behaviour, CloudKMS parsing) and consumers pattern-match on it. Introduce a cartouche-owned signature struct (r, s, recid) and move every in-repo consumer onto it. Afterwards, curvy must not remain a dependency of cartouche, onchain or onchain_tempo. The Signer.Curvy module name may stay as a deprecated alias of the new backend or be renamed. Pick one and record it in the CHANGELOG.

Low-s normalization (EIP-2, `Recover.normalize_low_s/1`) and RFC 6979 deterministic nonces must hold on the new path. k256 provides the latter. Prove both with tests rather than assuming them.

This is a public-API break in a 0.x package, so it needs a minor bump. mpp is the one known out-of-repo consumer that pattern-matches `%Curvy.Signature{}`.

The handwritten codec bodies of ABI.TypeEncoder and ABI.TypeDecoder and the src/ yecc/leex parser are deleted; ABI.TypeEncoder and ABI.TypeDecoder remain as thin facades over the NIF with unchanged module names, public functions, doctests and exception behaviour (including TypeDecoder.StrictViolation); no ABI.* public function signature changed

Tempo 0x76 — separate task
Codegen and the Solidity parser move — separate task
Changing the ABI.* public API
task.body:
Current instructions (2026-09-29 review, consolidating the attempt notes):
- Benchmarks are for checking, not a landing gate (operator correction 2026-09-29; the 2x stop rule is gone). Measure, record, explain, land.
- Start from commit f19602a5 on branch harness/run-1790670735107-a473b549. It has the pre-migration oracle fixture test/support/fixtures/abi_before_alloy.etf with its replay test, bench/, and the prototype NIF with the batch event-decode op and the normal/dirty scheduler split. Take only packages/onchain paths. Never bring over packages/cartouche or packages/hieroglyph build leftovers.
- One NIF call per decode. Bounded small inputs run on the normal scheduler, and dirty CPU is used only above a documented size threshold. The real bulk log-decode path is wired to the batch op, so the benchmark is not its only caller.
- Compile the schema once per selector or event into a NIF resource (a ResourceArc holding the parsed DynSolType plus the precomputed topic0), cache it on the Elixir side, and pass the handle on each call, for both decode and encode. This matches the old path's pre-parsed ABI.FunctionSelector. Report warm-cache numbers and, separately, the one-time compile cost. Report any remaining slowdown with a per-phase profile (term decode / alloy decode / term encode).
- Strict decoding: alloy-dyn-abi 1.7.3 has no validating decode. DynSolType::abi_decode/abi_decode_params/abi_decode_sequence take no strict flag (src/dynamic/ty.rs:520-558), and abi_decode_validate exists only in alloy-sol-types for static types. Implement `strict: true` as decode, re-encode and byte-compare. That catches dirty padding, trailing bytes and over-long length prefixes, but it can also over-reject a valid encoding with non-canonical offsets that the old strict decoder accepted. The malformed-input differential must cover that case.

Measured so far (keep for the outcome): attempt 1 (run-1790668418685-bf005ccf, baseline e669099f): 10,000-log Transfer decode 3.95x slower (43.39 vs 11.00 ips) from three dirty NIF calls per log; ERC-20 encode 1.40x, aggregate3 500 decode 0.80x, nested encode 0.084x. Attempt 2 (run-1790670735107-a473b549): single-log Transfer decode 2.12x slower (613,930 vs 289,523 ips, ~1.6 us vs ~3.45 us per log); the 10,000-log batch 0.45x; ERC-20 encode 1.82x; aggregate3 500 decode 0.60x; nested encode 0.094x. The remaining single-call gap is the per-call type-string re-parse (DynSolType::parse) and the schema/topic rebuild in the facade, which the compiled-resource step targets.

Answered 2026-09-29 (run question): ABI.TypeEncoder and ABI.TypeDecoder stay as thin facades over the alloy NIF. Their handwritten codec bodies are deleted, but the module names, public functions, doctests and exception behaviour (including TypeDecoder.StrictViolation) stay unchanged. The NIF returns error tuples and the facades raise the existing exceptions. Renaming to Onchain.* belongs to 9036. The existing ABI tests remain the byte-identical oracle and are not edited to fit. The Benchee old-vs-alloy run happens against the old implementation (e.g. the pre-change commit, or a bench-only copy under bench/) before the old code is deleted.

Operator decision 2026-09-29: deterministic encoding moves to alloy through a NIF so new EIPs arrive by a crate bump instead of hand-written Elixir. This reverses the out_of_scope note on task 9026 ('conformance vectors, not a runtime Rust dependency').

Build the NIF into packages/onchain using the rustler_precompiled setup onchain_evm already has (Onchain.Precompiled, the five targets in its @targets list, build-precompiled script, checksum file) — move that infrastructure into the core rather than duplicating it, so onchain_evm consumes it. Consumers must never need a Rust toolchain.

The boundary is generic, not one NIF function per Elixir function: type strings / JSON ABI plus values in, bytes or decoded values out. alloy-dyn-abi has coerce_str, and DynSolType::coerce_json behind the eip712 feature (docs.rs 1.7.3). Going Elixir term ↔ DynSolValue directly avoids a JSON round-trip, so one recursive converter is still the intended boundary. Then swap the backend under the existing ABI.* public API (encode/decode, selectors, events, errors, packed) to alloy-dyn-abi / alloy-json-abi and delete the hand-written encoder, decoder and the yecc/leex type parser.

Safety: a panic must never reach the BEAM (catch_unwind → error tuple); malformed input returns an error tuple; large payloads run on a dirty scheduler or are bounded so a normal scheduler is never blocked for long.
task.implemented: ABI encode/decode on alloy-dyn-abi via ABI.Native NIF; TypeEncoder/TypeDecoder facades; yecc/leex parser removed; oracle fixture replay, malformed differential, Onchain.Precompiled moved to onchain; canonical-offset fast path (reviewer)
