task.body:
Replace the hand-written encoding in Cartouche.Transaction (legacy, EIP-2930, 1559, 4844, 7702, typed_decode, call) and Cartouche.Typed (EIP-712 hashing) with alloy through the core NIF boundary from task 9031. Use alloy-consensus envelopes, whose SignableTransaction::signature_hash gives the signing hash, and alloy-dyn-abi's eip712 TypedData::eip712_signing_hash. Enable dyn-abi's eip712 feature; DynSolType::coerce_json is also gated behind it (docs.rs alloy-dyn-abi 1.7.3). alloy's TransactionEnvelope derive emits serde for the RPC JSON shape (tagged by "type") under the serde feature, and TypedData deserializes from standard EIP-712 JSON. This was verified by reading alloy-tx-macros 2.4.1 and alloy-dyn-abi 1.7.3 source, not by compiling.

Most of the work is the Elixir <-> alloy mapping, not the crate calls. Every V1/V2/V3/V4/V2930 struct, with its r/s/v and field layout, and the JSON entry points V1.from_json/1 and V2.from_json/1 (packages/onchain/lib/cartouche/transaction.ex:447, :1359), must map to and from alloy types without changing their public shape.

Signing stays on ex_secp256k1 (k256, task 9026). The NIF produces signing hashes and encodes signed envelopes. The Cartouche.Transaction and Cartouche.Typed public API does not change.

(2026-09-29 review) crates.io now has alloy-consensus and alloy-tx-macros 2.5.0 (published 2026-09-23), newer than the 2.4.1 source read above. Pin exact alloy-consensus, alloy-tx-macros and alloy-dyn-abi versions at dispatch, re-check the serde and eip712 feature claims against the pinned versions, and record the versions in the outcome.

task.title: Tempo 0x76 encoding from tempo-primitives in an onchain_tempo NIF, graded against the Tempo spec including key_authorization
acceptance_criteria: Current onchain_tempo output (tx bytes, signing hash, tx hash, cosigned bytes, 0x78 fee-payer preimage) over all fixtures, including fixtures with key_authorization, and the existing priv/verification/0x76 vectors (ox_vectors.json) is captured before deletion, and the tempo-primitives path matches byte-for-byte

Transactions with key_authorization are additionally graded against tempo-primitives and the Tempo spec (versions recorded): unsigned bytes, sender sign payload, 0x78 fee-payer preimage, serialized and cosigned bytes, and recovered sender/fee-payer; a test asserts the preimage includes key_authorization. Any divergence between the old encoder and tempo-primitives is recorded in the outcome with its vector, and tempo-primitives wins
A live Moderato run records one success with and one without key_authorization, plus one relevant live error; absent endpoint access the run fails loudly with the exact setup needed, never skips

The NIF is a separate crate in packages/onchain_tempo using the shared precompiled infrastructure; the core onchain NIF gains no Tempo or commonware dependency; the outcome records onchain_tempo NIF binary size and clean build time
Secp256k1 signing round-trips as today; no new signature types are exposed; onchain_tempo contains no hand-written 0x76/0x78 RLP encoding; its public API is unchanged

Focused tests pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA); Onchain.Tempo.Transaction stays >=95% coverage; onchain_tempo CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.md (native build notes) updated
out_of_scope: tempo-alloy network/filler/relay transport — onchain_tempo keeps its Elixir RPC
mpay-rs / mpp changes
Folding onchain_tempo into the core package
A mutation campaign over the new Tempo encoder (task 8013 is superseded; file a new task if one is wanted)
task.body:
tempo-primitives 1.11.0 (crates.io, released 2026-08-20; github.com/tempoxyz/tempo) is the official Rust definition of Tempo's transaction types: TempoTxEnvelope, TempoTransaction, AASigned, and TempoSignature with SignatureType Secp256k1 / P256 / WebAuthn (docs.rs). revm and alloy-evm are optional dependencies behind the evm feature, but commonware-cryptography ^2026.7.1 is a required dependency (docs.rs dependency list).

Build the NIF as its own crate in packages/onchain_tempo, precompiled through the shared rustler_precompiled infrastructure task 9031 moves into core, not inside the core onchain NIF. Tempo types and commonware then ship only to onchain_tempo consumers, not to every onchain (or onchain_solana) user. Use default-features = false with std + serde.

(2026-09-29 review) The current encoder is a usable oracle for key_authorization too. split_base_fields/1 (packages/onchain_tempo/lib/onchain/tempo/transaction.ex:396-401) keeps every field except the trailing sender signature, so key_authorization stays in the base fields when present. The `_has_key_auth` parameter of build_fee_payer_preimage_fields/4 (:405) is merely unused. tempo-primitives 1.11.0 includes key_authorization in the fee-payer hash the same way: fee_payer_signature_hash → rlp_encode_fields, src/transaction/tempo_transaction.rs:407-430 and :482-525. Byte parity with the old encoder is therefore required for all transactions, with and without key_authorization, and every key_authorization case is additionally graded against tempo-primitives, the Tempo spec and live Moderato. If a divergence does appear, tempo-primitives and the spec win, and the divergence is recorded in the outcome with the failing vector.

onchain_tempo signs only Secp256k1 today (transaction.ex:34), and its struct is a positional RLP fields list (fee-payer signature at @fee_payer_sig_index 11, :185). Replacing the encoder means reworking that internal representation while keeping the public functions (build, cosign_fee_payer/3, has_fee_payer_placeholder?/1, decode) and their return contracts. What remains in Elixir is the thin protocol layer: TIP-20, fee-payer flow, faucet, RPC glue.
task.implemented: Tempo 0x76 encoding moved to an onchain_tempo NIF on tempo-primitives with key_authorization byte parity; native verification + integration tests; follow-up bounds-doc fix 91ec6f2

task.body:
Two contract generators exist. mix cartouche.gen (packages/onchain/lib/mix/cartouche.gen.ex, 1,505 lines, signet heritage) emits call_/exec_vm_ wrappers and produced the 37,553-line generated lib/cartouche/contract/i_console.ex. Onchain.Contract.Generator in onchain_evm parses Solidity and ABI JSON through the onchain_solidity crate (Onchain.Solidity.parse_abi_json/1, parse_sol_file/2). That crate depends on alloy-json-abi 1.6 and solar-parse 0.2 (packages/onchain_evm/native/onchain_solidity/Cargo.toml).

Keep only the alloy-based generator. Move the ABI-JSON path (alloy-json-abi) and the generator into core, so codegen from ABI JSON no longer requires onchain_evm. Leave .sol parsing (solar-parse, a Solidity compiler frontend) in onchain_evm. Codegen runs at dev time, and a compiler frontend in the runtime core NIF would bloat it for every consumer.

Cartouche.VM (an Elixir EVM for pure functions) and Cartouche.Assembly exist only for the generated exec_vm_* wrappers; revm in onchain_evm covers local execution. task.title: Sugar.Prices — materialise a PriceMap from verified anchors and the pool graph, with a reconciliation check
acceptance_criteria: Sugar.Prices.price_map/1 returns {:ok, %Types.PriceMap{}} by fetching anchors plus the Lp set and delegating ALL arithmetic to Analytics.Price.resolve/3; a reach check plus an explicit review criterion confirm this module contains no price arithmetic of its own

A rejected anchor (stale, sequencer down, grace period) degrades explicitly — either the affected token lands in PriceMap.unpriced with the policy's reason and the rest succeeds, or the whole call fails; the choice is documented and tested, and a rejected anchor is NEVER silently replaced by a pool-derived price without the Price struct's source field reflecting that

An integration-tagged reconciliation test prices at least 10 high-TVL Base tokens both ways (Chainlink anchor versus pool route) at a pinned block and asserts agreement within a documented tolerance; the comparison table is committed with its block number and date

Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)

Caching or long-lived processes

task.body:
The network half of the price layer. It fetches validated anchors through task 5018's Bindings.Chainlink and a set of Lp rows, and delegates ALL arithmetic to Analytics.Price.resolve/3. If you find yourself multiplying prices here, the code belongs one layer down.

The reconciliation test is the honest check on the whole design: for tokens that also have a Chainlink feed, our pool-routed price must agree with the feed within a documented tolerance. A disagreement means the routing is wrong or the pool is thin, and both are worth knowing before an APR denominator is built on it. Commit the comparison. Fix the tolerance and its justification before the first run, and never widen it to make a failing comparison pass — a disagreement is a finding to report, not a number to tune.

OPEN DECISIONS to settle and record: (a) whether price_map/1 fetches the full roughly 71-page Lp enumeration or accepts a caller-supplied pool subset — full enumeration for a price map is wasteful, so a subset with a documented default is probably right; (b) partial-failure semantics when an anchor is rejected by 5018's policy.

AUTHORITY: live Base state at a pinned block, and the Chainlink feeds as validated by task 5018.

A gate that passes on absent data is not a gate: a missing report or zero modules must fail loudly.

task.title: wait_for_transaction_receipt: poll with confirmations and timeout, and detect a fee-bumped replacement by sender and nonce
acceptance_criteria: `Onchain.Wait.wait_for_transaction_receipt(hash, opts)` (packages/onchain/lib/onchain/wait.ex) polls with a configurable interval and timeout, returns the receipt once `confirmations:` blocks have followed it, and returns an explicit `{:error, :timeout}`

Replacement detection: when the original hash stops being found and a transaction with the same sender and nonce is mined under a different hash, the function returns that replacement's receipt tagged as a replacement. Pinned by an anvil test that sends a transaction, replaces it with a higher fee before mining, and asserts the tagged replacement receipt

A live mainnet test waits on an already-mined known hash and returns immediately with decoded domain fields; a live anvil test with automine off sends a transaction, mines after a delay, and asserts the wait resolves
Sender, nonce and block number come from task 2129's eth_getTransactionByHash envelope; no private copy of that read is added
Live tests flunk with exact export instructions when the node env var or anvil is absent, never skip
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA); CHANGELOG entry
out_of_scope: The Onchain.Client struct and opts threading (task 9017, which accepts a client here once it lands)
`watch_*` polling facades; task 3090 owns log/block/pending polling
task.body:
Split from 9017 (2026-09-29 review). There is no `waitForTransactionReceipt` equivalent anywhere in the family. A grep for receipt polling finds only onchain_tempo's faucet funding wait (packages/onchain_tempo/lib/onchain/tempo/faucet.ex:133), which is not a receipt wait. It is the most-used viem DX affordance after `readContract`. Replacement detection matters in practice: a fee-bumped resend under a new hash makes a naive poll on the old hash hang until timeout.

Replacement detection design hint, not a mandate: viem remembers the sender and nonce from `eth_getTransactionByHash` at the start. When the original hash stops being found, it scans newly mined blocks for a transaction with that sender and nonce. Any approach that passes the anvil replacement test is fine.

Build on the envelope task 2129 returns from eth_getTransactionByHash (from, nonce, blockNumber). Do not add a private copy of the read. The module is Onchain.Wait. Onchain.* names survive the 9036 rename unchanged, and Onchain.Receipt would collide with Cartouche.Receipt once that is renamed. The function takes a node URL through opts today; task 9017 later adds `client:`.

Authority: the live node (mainnet for the mined-receipt case, anvil for the pending and replacement cases); ethereum/execution-apis for receipt and transaction object shapes.

Dispatch trigger: money-path pipeline (send then wait) with live evidence — earns an independent reviewer.

task.title: Local key material for the signer, part 2: Web3 Secret Storage v3 (keystore) import and export via alloy-signer-local

scrypt and the keystore format come from alloy-signer-local's keystore support in the core NIF (packages/onchain/native/); the CHANGELOG names the crate versions, and the standard-parameter decrypt time on the dev machine is recorded, as information, not a gate
A decrypted key plugs into the signer through the existing {backend, config} carrier and signs a transaction a dev node accepts (live test on anvil)
No key material or password leaks through inspect/1, logs, NIF error terms or error messages, pinned by tests
Sobelow reports nothing new and no .sobelow-skips entry is added
Focused tests for the changed behaviour pass and `mix check.dispatch` is green in every touched package (full `mix ci` is post-merge QA)
out_of_scope: BIP-39 / BIP-32 / BIP-44; task 9015 owns them
Any keystore format other than Web3 Secret Storage v3
Hardware or browser wallets
task.body:
Split out of task 9015 on 2026-09-29. A developer with a geth or foundry keystore file cannot get a signer out of this stack without a second library. The family has no keystore, scrypt or mnemonic code anywhere in lib/.

Implementation path, decided: alloy-signer-local's keystore support (eth-keystore) through the core alloy NIF that 9031 introduces in packages/onchain/native/. That avoids a pure-Elixir scrypt at n=262144, r=8, which needs 128*r*n = 256 MiB of working memory per derivation and has no OTP :crypto primitive to lean on. pbkdf2 decrypt may still use :crypto.pbkdf2_hmac/5, if that keeps the MAC check in Elixir, as long as both KDFs pass the same vectors. Run after 9036, so the module is Onchain.Keys.

Authority: the Web3 Secret Storage definition (ethereum.org wiki) and its two test vectors, plus one external tool accepting a file this code writes. alloy is the implementation, not the oracle.

Dispatch trigger: key-material surface. Security-marked; needs an independent reviewer on KDF correctness, MAC-before-decrypt ordering and redaction.

task.title: A fresh monorepo checkout compiles onchain's alloy NIF before any release assets exist
acceptance_criteria: In a fresh clone of main with an EMPTY rustler_precompiled cache (point RUSTLER_PRECOMPILED_GLOBAL_CACHE_PATH at an empty temp dir) and NO ONCHAIN_BUILD set, `mix compile` succeeds at the repo root and in all seven packages. Record the commands and output in the task outcome

`ONCHAIN_PUBLISH=1 mix hex.build` in packages/onchain prints no 'excluded from the package' line, and the tarball's metadata still declares rustler as optional. A Hex-installed consumer's behavior is unchanged: it downloads, checksum mismatch fails the load, and a missing checksum entry fails the load
Onchain.Precompiled's mode resolution (checkout vs Hex-installed, ONCHAIN_BUILD, ONCHAIN_EVM_BUILD, unsupported host) is unit-tested without network access
onchain_evm's own NIFs still resolve as before: download with its committed checksums on a supported host, and source-build under ONCHAIN_EVM_BUILD=1
packages/onchain/CLAUDE.md states the checkout-vs-published rule in one place, and the lockfile changes are limited to adding rustler (and its own deps) where the dependency graph now needs it
out_of_scope: Uploading release assets or cutting any GitHub release/tag. That is the 9036 publish step and human-gated
Running mix hex.publish
Changing the target list or the build script
task.body:
Since 9031 (c9c7256), a fresh checkout of main cannot compile anything that depends on onchain unless the machine happens to have the onchain_abi artifact in its rustler_precompiled cache. The harness server has one; a clean laptop does not. Observed 2026-09-30 on macOS in a fresh worktree at 66af428:

- Without ONCHAIN_BUILD: `packages/onchain_tempo` `mix compile` tries to download https://github.com/ZenHive/onchain-stack/releases/download/onchain-v0.15.0/libonchain_abi-v0.15.0-nif-2.15-aarch64-apple-darwin.so.tar.gz and gets a 404. The committed checksum-Elixir.ABI.Native.exs lists five targets, but those assets were never uploaded. Uploading them is the 9036 release step.
- With ONCHAIN_BUILD=1: `packages/onchain` builds from source, but the root project and every in-repo dependent (verified: onchain_tempo, and the root, which the pre-commit hook compiles) fail with "Rustler dependency is needed to force the build". rustler is `optional: true` in onchain's mix.exs, and a path dependency's optional deps are not pulled into the dependent.

The earlier onchain_evm design (task 6053's acceptance criteria) already stated the rule this breaks: a Hex-installed package must download and verify, while the library's own checkout source-builds while no release exists. 9031 moved Onchain.Precompiled into core but lost the in-checkout half once it committed a checksum file ahead of its assets.

Make the checkout self-sufficient again without weakening the Hex path. One shape that fits the existing sibling/3 marker convention: onchain declares rustler non-optional when the `.onchain-monorepo-root` marker is present (and ONCHAIN_PUBLISH is unset), and Onchain.Precompiled source-builds in the checkout. The published tarball's dependency declaration must stay exactly as it is today. Another shape is fine if it meets the criteria.

The 9033 (onchain_tempo NIF) and 9034 (codegen NIF) tasks will reuse Onchain.Precompiled, so whatever rule lands here is the one they inherit.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1790724022756-49c7c245, 1ead58919988b8c5fab44543237fe74a229ca3d3).

task.title: Gate the Rust dependency tree: cargo audit (and onchain's missing cargo test/clippy) in mix ci
acceptance_criteria: `cd packages/onchain && mix ci` and `cd packages/onchain_evm && mix ci` each run `cargo audit` over every crate under their `native/` and fail on a vulnerability finding; a deliberately vulnerable lock (e.g. rustls pinned back to 0.23.43 in a scratch copy) turns the step red — negative control recorded in the verdict
Unmaintained/yanked warnings do not fail the gate by default; any ignore is an explicit, commented `audit.toml`/flag entry per advisory id, never a blanket ignore

`packages/onchain` runs `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` over `native/onchain_abi`, with the same lint policy as onchain_evm (`unwrap_used` denied, test code exempted), and the crate is clippy-clean when the gate is added
A missing `cargo-audit` binary fails with the install command; a missing cargo still follows the existing documented degrade path
Gate helper logic exists once, not copied per package; `mix hex.build` for onchain and onchain_evm shows no new runtime module or dependency from this change
Root CLAUDE.md (Gates section) and the two package CLAUDE.md files describe the Rust audit step; AGENTS.md regenerated

A test drives the onchain ABI NIF with a pathologically deep schema (nested tuples/arrays, well past any realistic depth) and a deeply nested value, and asserts an `{:error, _}` return with the BEAM still alive — no stack-overflow abort, no scheduler stall; the test states the depth used and which budget rejects it. If the current budgets do not stop it, fix the NIF so they do, rather than lowering the test depth
out_of_scope: Replacing unmaintained transitive crates (paste, derivative) — upstream alloy/revm choice
Auditing Cargo.lock files under deps/ of third-party Hex packages (ex_keccak, ex_secp256k1, oxc)
Adding the task to 9036's dependencies — this is not a release gate
task.body:
Since the alloy/tempo-primitives switch, onchain ships a Rust NIF (`packages/onchain/native/onchain_abi`) with a large crate tree, and onchain_evm has two more crates. `mix deps.audit` only sees Hex packages, so no gate looks at any Cargo.lock for advisories.

Evidence (2026-09-30, `cargo audit` 0.21 by hand): onchain_evm's crate carried RUSTSEC-2026-0285 (rustls 0.23.43, medium) with nothing flagging it; fixed inline in 1539ba1 by bumping rustls to 0.23.45. All three crates additionally report allowed warnings (unmaintained `paste`, `derivative`; yanked `chacha20` in onchain_evm) — cargo audit exits 0 on those.

Also: onchain_evm gates its crates with `cargo test` + `cargo clippy` via `Onchain.Cargo` (its `lib/`, so it ships in the tarball); onchain has no Rust gate at all — its crate's tests and lints are ungated.

Wanted: every in-repo crate is audited from its package's `mix ci`, and onchain's crate gets the same test/clippy gate onchain_evm already has. Where the shared logic lives (shared/mix_helpers.exs vs a per-package module) is the implementer's call; it must not end up in a published tarball's runtime surface if avoidable, and must not duplicate a copy per package.

Behaviour when the tool is absent: DIST-14 (docs/specs/onchain-distribution.md). The install command is `cargo install cargo-audit --locked`. This deliberately differs from the existing test/clippy skip on absent cargo, because cargo audit is a security gate.

**Added 2026-09-30 — deep-nesting runtime check (operator's call).** Reviewed `native/onchain_abi/src/lib.rs`: every export is wrapped in `catch_unwind`, the default path runs on `DirtyCpu`, only small static schemas take `abi_small` on the normal scheduler, and `spend`/`remaining` budgets bound parse and decode work; the crate has no `unsafe` of its own. What `catch_unwind` cannot catch is a stack overflow (and allocation failure), which aborts the whole VM. Premise unverified — confirm before building on it: the per-node budget should prevent recursion deep enough to overflow, but no test pins that. Add the test; if it crashes the VM, the budget needs an explicit depth limit.

task.title: Retarget the Tempo 0x76 mutation campaign at the native encoder
acceptance_criteria: `cd packages/onchain_tempo && ONCHAIN_BUILD=1 MIX_ENV=test mix test.json test/onchain/tempo/verification/mutation_test.exs` passes with no pattern skipped and `:verification` not excluded

Every mutant applies to current code (a missing pattern fails the run, as today); mutants cover field order/mapping into tempo-primitives, the 0x76 vs 0x78 domain choice, fee-payer data, key_authorization presence in sender and fee-payer paths, and signature/recid conversion
The wrong-field-index and wrong-signing-domain canaries are killed, and a dropped key_authorization in the 0x78 preimage is a killed canary; the run is invalid if a canary survives
Every surviving mutant is classified (equivalent, unreachable, redundant or genuine gap) with evidence in priv/verification/0x76/ledger.json, together with tool versions and the artifact commit
Tests that check TEMPO-2/TEMPO-3 carry `# spec-tags:` comments
onchain_tempo CHANGELOG notes the retargeted campaign
out_of_scope: Mutating tempo-primitives or other upstream crates
Changing the 0x76 encoding behaviour itself — a genuine gap found here gets fixed only if small, otherwise filed
task.body:
9033 (21ed60e) moved 0x76 encoding into an onchain_tempo NIF on tempo-primitives. The mutation campaign from task 12 still mutates the deleted Elixir encoder: `Campaign.mutants/0` replaces literals such as `@calls_index 4`, `@fee_payer_domain 0x78`, `@tempo_tx_type 0x76`, the fee-token/fee-payer indexes, `encode_uint`, `List.replace_at` and `recid + 27`. The 9033 reviewer reproduced it: `ONCHAIN_BUILD=1 MIX_ENV=test mix test.json test/onchain/tempo/verification/mutation_test.exs` fails 3 tests, first `{:pattern_missing, "@calls_index 4"}`. `:verification` is not excluded by default, so onchain_tempo's `mix ci` is red on main until this lands. 8013 is superseded and 9033's out_of_scope deferred this to a new task.

Point the campaign, canaries and lanes at what now carries the semantics: the Rust glue in native/onchain_tempo (field mapping into tempo-primitives, fee-payer/0x78 preimage choice, key_authorization handling, signature/recid conversion) and the thin Elixir protocol around it. Mutating tempo-primitives itself is not the goal — the target is our code that could still get it wrong. Graded per the onchain-verification rules; relevant spec rules are TEMPO-2 and TEMPO-3 in docs/specs/onchain-tempo-native.md.
